description_text:
Digi Security Systems is an industry leader in the design, installation and support of custom video surveillance, electronic access control, and intrusion detection solutions for public and private partners. We've built our reputation on innovation and reliable service, and we're known as the industry's experts.
About the role
Digi Security Systems is hiring a Payroll Specialist to own accurate, on-time payroll for a group of operating businesses. Our payroll processes, procedures, and systems are still taking shape. So while processing payroll is the core of this job, helping us build the way we do it — documenting steps, tightening controls, and shaping our systems as we grow — is the other part.
What you'll do
Payroll processing (most of your time)
Run end-to-end payroll for multiple businesses on weekly, biweekly and semimonthly schedules
Collect and verify hours, new hires, terminations, pay changes, bonuses and commissions before each run
Calculate and process deductions, garnishments, PTO accruals and benefit withholdings
Review payroll registers for accuracy and resolve discrepancies before funds are released
Make sure federal, state and local payroll taxes are withheld, filed and paid on time, including quarterly and year-end filings (941, W-2, W-3)
Answer employee and manager questions about pay, deductions and tax forms
Reconcile payroll to the general ledger and prepare journal entries or reports for accounting
Support audits, workers' comp reviews and year-end close
Building how we work
Write and maintain step-by-step procedures and checklists for each business you support
Spot errors, manual workarounds and risks, and propose fixes
Help evaluate, set up, or migrate payroll and HR systems as we standardize
Bring newly added businesses onto our payroll process smoothly
Partner with HR, accounting, and local business managers to keep data flowing cleanly
What you bring
3+ years of hands-on payroll processing, ideally across more than one company or EIN
Working knowledge of federal and multi-state payroll tax rules, wage and hour law, and garnishments
Experience with at least one major payroll platform (for example ADP, Paychex, Paylocity, Gusto or UKG)
Strong Excel skills: lookups, pivot tables and reconciliations
A high bar for accuracy and confidentiality
Clear, friendly communication with employees and managers who aren't payroll experts
Nice to have
Fundamental Payroll Certification (FPC) or Certified Payroll Professional (CPP)
Experience with field-service or hourly workforces (overtime, shift differentials, job costing)
Experience helping implement or migrate a payroll system
Exposure to acquisitions or onboarding new entities
Who thrives here
You're comfortable when the answer is "we haven't decided that yet" and you'll help decide it
You fix the root cause, not just this cycle's error
You write things down so the next person doesn't have to guess
You can juggle several pay calendars without missing a deadline
You ask questions early and flag problems before payday, not after
Why Digi Security Systems
Real variety. You'll support multiple partner companies, each with its own team, pay practices and history. It's not the same payroll every week.
A hand in building it. Our payroll processes and systems are still taking shape, and you'll help design them instead of inheriting someone else's.
Work that matters to people. The technicians and installers keeping our customers' buildings secure count on you to get their pay right.
Competitive base salary, full health benefits, 401(k) with match, paid time off, paid holidays, life and disability coverage, and professional development support.
Benefits
Quarterly performance-based incentive plan
Vacation accrual: 2 weeks initially, 3 weeks after 1 year
7 paid holidays annually
401(k) with company match
Full medical, dental, and vision coverage
Company-paid life insurance; optional additional coverage: accident/critical illness

description_text:
Description
United Way for Greater AustinGrant AccountantDepartment: FinanceRegular, Full-time, Exempt

Who we are:

United Way for Greater Austin brings our community together to break economic barriers and build opportunity for all. We break the cycle of economic hardships for families and individuals, striving to create a vibrant, thriving community. Recognizing the urgency of addressing economic challenges, we focus on increasing the availability of high-quality early care and education and access to pivotal resources to address financial barriers in Central Texas. Our united front includes dedicated donors, volunteers, corporate and civic partners, staff, and a connected network of neighbors. Who we want:

You will be responsible for ensuring grant compliance for United Way and funded subcontractors on federal, state, city, and private grants, including but not limited to managing grant reporting deadlines, preparing budgets, monitoring the budget and spending status of assigned grants, and ensuring requirements for monitoring and financial reporting are met You will support the development of effective systems for submitting and monitoring funding and reimbursement requests to grantors and subcontractors and work directly with grant program managers on issues related to grants. This role reports to the Finance Grants Manager and the Controller. 

Who you are:
A strong strategic thinker: You thrive on creating processes and procedures to ensure a strong financial management system – you understand and analyze challenges quickly, assess internal and external conditions that affect your strategic priorities and can develop and recommend new strategies, processes, or procedures.

Collaborates: You work cooperatively with all departments across the organization to achieve shared objectives and represent their interests while being fair to others and their area. You partner with others to get work done and credit others for their contributions and accomplishments — you garner the trust and support of others.
An excellent communicator: You can listen actively and effectively to communicate complex information to various audiences. You can influence decision-makers at all levels and speak confidently with a broad spectrum of internal stakeholders and funders.
Technologically Savvy: You are proficient in using computer software, including Microsoft Office, accounting software, and other tools. 
What you’ll do:
Ensure grant compliance for United Way and funded subcontractors across federal, state, city, and private grants.
Manage grant reporting deadlines and prepare accurate financial reports for grantors and internal stakeholders.
Develop and monitor grant budgets, tracking spending status and identifying variances. 
Maintain systems for submitting and monitoring funding and reimbursement requests to grantors and subcontractors. 
Record and reconcile grant-related transactions in accounting systems to ensure accuracy and audit readiness. 
Work directly with grant program managers to resolve issues related to grant budgets, spending, and compliance. 
Support the Finance Grants Manager and Controller with financial reporting and audit preparation. 
Contribute to the improvement of grant accounting processes and documentation. 
What you’ll bring:
A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field or four or more years experience as a grant accountant.

An ability to work independently, exercise good judgment, solve problems, and bring a high level of initiative and self-direction to work.

Excellent electronic spreadsheet and word processing skills in a Windows/Microsoft environment.
An ability to work and meet deadlines in a cross-functional, fast-paced work environment

description_text:
We are seeking an experienced Manager – First Line of Defense (1LOD) Regulatory
Compliance Advisory professional to support U.S. Commercial Card and Payments
businesses. This role is part of the GCS Regulatory Advisory Practices team and
is responsible for driving the execution of regulatory compliance activities to
ensure business operations align with applicable U.S. laws, regulations, and
internal policies.

This role provides proactive regulatory guidance to business partners, with a
focus on consumer protection, commercial card, and payments regulations,
including requirements related to customer treatment, disclosures, billing
practices, and data usage. The individual will translate regulatory requirements
into actionable business processes and controls, ensuring alignment with
enterprise compliance frameworks and regulatory expectations.

The position requires close collaboration across business units, Compliance
(2LOD), Legal, Risk, and Audit, and plays a key role in regulatory change
management, exam readiness, and issue remediation. The ideal candidate has
strong knowledge of U.S. regulatory frameworks governing payments and lending
products and can effectively balance regulatory requirements with business
objectives.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Serve as a 1LOD regulatory compliance advisor for U.S. commercial card and
   payments products, ensuring alignment with applicable regulations (e.g.,
   UDAAP, Regulation Z, Regulation B, Regulation E, GLBA/privacy, and relevant
   state laws)
 * Translate regulatory requirements into clear business requirements, controls,
   and operational processes across the customer lifecycle (origination,
   onboarding, servicing, billing, and collections)
 * Drive implementation and ongoing enhancement of regulatory controls,
   including those related to disclosures, billing accuracy, customer
   communications, error resolution, and customer treatment
 * Monitor and analyze compliance risk metrics, customer impact indicators, and
   control effectiveness, escalating issues as appropriate
 * Identify, assess, and support mitigation of compliance risks within the
   business
 * Partner with business stakeholders and Compliance (2LOD) to design,
   implement, and enhance controls
 * Execute and support compliance risk assessments (RCSA) and control monitoring
   activities
 * Support regulatory exam readiness and response efforts, including
   coordination, documentation, and remediation tracking
 * Support regulatory issue remediation and corrective action plans, ensuring
   timely and sustainable resolution
 * Provide regulatory guidance on new products, features, and business changes
 * Support consistent interpretation and application of regulatory requirements
   across the business
 * Contribute to promoting a culture of compliance and accountability within the
   organization


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Qualifications

 * 4+ years of related experience in regulatory compliance, risk management, or
   governance within a financial institution
 * Strong knowledge of U.S. regulatory frameworks/compliance laws including
   UDAAP, Regulation Z, Regulation B, Regulation E, and GLBA 
 * Experience supporting regulatory exams (e.g., CFPB, OCC, Federal Reserve)
 * Experience with compliance risk assessments (RCSA) and control
   design/implementation
 * Solid understanding of customer lifecycle risks across payments or lending
   products
 * Ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical business controls
 * Strong stakeholder management and communication skills
 * Bachelor's degree

 

Preferred Qualifications

 * Experience in commercial card, payments, or transaction banking
 * Experience in a large financial institution or highly regulated environment
 * Professional certifications (e.g., CRCM)
 * Master's degree

 

Key Competencies

 * Strong business acumen and sound judgment
 * Regulatory interpretation and control design capability
 * Effective communication and stakeholder influence skills
 * Ability to manage multiple priorities in a complex, matrixed environment
 * Execution-oriented with strong attention to detail


Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is
required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

description_text:
Description
Would you like to join a growing, member-owned, not-for-profit financial institution that is one of the Best of the Best in Monmouth and Ocean County per the Asbury Park Press Readers' Choice Awards? We have refreshed our brand, and our CEO and Leadership Team are focused on the well-being of our Employees and the enrichment of the work environment! If this appeals to you and you would like to be part of a "Winning Team", then please consider applying for the Accountantr position at First Atlantic Federal Credit Union.
Who we are:
Around here we do things differently. Maybe it's the ocean breeze. Or the music. Or the fact that we've been a part of the landscape for over 90 years. Around here we put our members first. Always have and always will. First Atlantic is Built on Trust, Driven by Members! It's knowing that when our community thrives, we all thrive. Our continued mission is to support our members and deliver the best value in financial services. It's where trust and tradition meet innovation and versatility, and the community is paramount. 
First Atlantic is headquartered in Eatontown, New Jersey, with branches in Eatontown, Oceanport, Toms River. Coming soon to Freehold and Old Bridge!. Anyone who lives, works, worships, volunteers, or attends school in Middlesex, Monmouth or Ocean counties is eligible to join. Family members of a First Atlantic member can also belong.
What we are looking for:
We are seeking an ONSITE Accountant to provide support services to staff and internal clients. The position entails the application principles of accounting to analyze financial data and prepare financial reports and reconciliations in accordance with GAAP. 
Some of the tasks include the following:
Handles system data inputs and proofing of results for varied systems, Prologue, DNA, etc. 
Accounts Payable review of invoices and retrieval of support, approvals, signatures, and payment of vendors. This includes any collections related billings, such as attorney bills, OREO bills and expenses, as well as the journal entries that are associated with payments. 
Coordinate distribution of monthly business card statements to each Department Manager, and ensure they are returned timely and accurately with proper documentation and signatures. 
Prepare entries for CD interest and other miscellaneous checks received by the Dept. Assist with maintaining accurate reporting of CDs in the investments system. Also ensure that investments reporting agrees to the GL every month. Review and correct any differences before month-end.
Prepare daily cash activity, proof shares and loans trend analysis.
Assist with entries for month end close; fixed assets, prepaids, accrued expenses and other varied month end responsibilities in accordance with procedures.
Compiles and analyzes financial information to prepare entries to accounts, such as general ledger accounts, documenting business transactions. Also handles account reconciliations, as directed.
Assist in the identification and analysis of significant fluctuations in account balances. Report findings to the Supervisor and assist with follow-up actions, as requested.
Timely preparation of GL reconciliations and timely resolving outstanding items in accordance with procedures.
Assist other members of the accounting department, as needed, or assigned by the Supervisor.


Requirements
QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE
Bachelor's Degree in Finance/Accounting two to four years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

description_text:
Position Summary

This position works under the general supervision of an assigned Supervisor to
be responsible for the collection of taxes by receipting, recording, and
depositing tax payments for Shelby County and other municipalities, and
interfaces with taxpayers and vendors daily.

Pay Grade: 46
Salary Commensurate with Experience and Education


Minimum Qualifications

 * Four (4) years of experience in municipal tax or bank receipting/collections,
   financial or mortgage institution, which includes lockbox and/or electronic
   processing; AND
 * High school diploma or possess a GED.
 * PROOF OF EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND/OR EXPERIENCE IS REQUIRED.
    

Duties and Responsibilities

 * Collects and processes property taxes, including payments received in the
   mail, over the internet, and counter transactions.
 * Performs daily file transfer associated with the posting of payments, the
   distribution of payment information to external payees (i.e., mortgage
   companies and real estate services), the sending of image cash letters to the
   bank, electronic uploads from online banking providers, and the electronic
   payments received from the State of Tennessee
 * Performs activities associated with the issuance of refunds via electronic
   workflow and routing software.
 * Assists taxpayers, mortgage companies, county offices, and other entities on
   the phone or in person with tax-related problem resolution.
 * Conducts daily deposit activities associated with electronic file transfers
   and payment activities.
 * Maintains electronic records and reports to ensure data integrity and
   transfer accuracy.
 * Assists in compiling departmental policies and procedures related to
   remittance collection activities.
 * Conducts testing of new software releases related to payment activities.
 * Interfaces with vendors to ensure optimum equipment and software
   functionality.
 * Operates as a backup to Head Cashier, Remittance Supervisor, etc. as needed.
 * Works a flexible schedule adjusted to accommodate workflow.
 * Performs other related duties as required or directed.

 

KSAs

 * Knowledge of general knowledge and use of computers.
 * Knowledge of tax receipting/ collection, lockbox and/or electronic tax
   processing
 * Knowledge of image capture processes, automated mail extraction equipment,
   batch processing, document scanners, and electronic file transfers associated
   with daily collection activities.
 * Ability to use online research tools including vendor analytical reports,
   financial and other web portals as needed or required. 
 * Ability to navigate proprietary and customized software solutions including
   Debt Manager, STAR, RAS, RTL, Opex, IP Switch, PolicyServ, City of Memphis
   software and remote deposit products from various banks.
 * Proficient knowledge of software packages including Microsoft Word, Excel,
   Power Point and (Knowledge of MS ACCESS and MS Dynamics helpful).
 * Ability to research and update taxpayer records including transaction
   histories and refunds.
 * Ability to convey tax information to the public with tact, understanding and
   courtesy.
 * Ability to prioritize workflow and comply with internal controls to meet
   daily deadlines related to tax collections processes.

 

Special Requirements

 * Must have reliable transportation.
 * May be required to work at offsite locations during tax season.

 

Disclaimer
This position is subject to a background check for any convictions that have a
substantial relationship to potential job duties. Only convictions that are
substantially related to potential job duties will be considered and will not
automatically disqualify the candidate.

and shall continue to reside in the County as a condition of their employment.

employed by the Division of Corrections, (3) Firefighters, Paramedics and
Dispatchers employed by the Shelby County Fire Department.  The residency
exemption for public safety/civil service employees does not include Appointed
positions with Sheriff’s Office, Division of Corrections or the Fire Department.

Jewish Family and Children's Services (JFCS) has served the San Francisco Bay Area for 175 years. Our mission and work are rooted in Jewish values, and we serve people of all faiths and backgrounds.

POSITION SUMMARY:
Under the supervision of the Billing Systems Manager (BSM), the Billing Systems Specialist (BSS) is responsible for third party billing and follow up for clinical programs of the Agency, posting payments for client fees, and SmartCare data entry. Additionally, the BSS reviews client billing data required for third party billing, generates third party invoices, and is responsible for follow-up on the related receivables to ensure timely collection of outstanding amounts.

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship. The company does not provide visa sponsorship for this position.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
Pay Range: $35.00 - $40.00 (depending on experience)
Employment Type: full-time, non-exempt position with benefits
Employer 403(b) retirement match plus additional employer contribution (subject to eligibility)
Cafeteria plan with medical, dental, vision, FSA, Employer-paid life, and disability insurance
16 holidays (10 federal and up to 6 Jewish holidays), annually
3 weeks of vacation and 2 weeks of sick leave, annually
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
In conjunction with other billing staff, collects, reviews, and enters time and billing data for client and third-party billing
Enters 3rd party billing information, including Medicare, indemnity insurance and/or other third-party payer information into the SmartCare system and ensures that data is current and entered correctly and accurately
At month end, generates and distributes claims to Medicare and third-party payers as well as producing reports and journal entries
Maintains knowledge of basic client/billing SmartCare system functioning; performs back-up as needed for SmartCare operations including billing, monthly closing, report generation and record maintenance
Reviews insurance and Medicare monthly billing for completeness and accuracy; assists in getting clients enrolled for Medicare billing, if they qualify
Posts payments for SmartCare into its accounting system; downloads and reviews Authorize.net credit card transactions daily, verifies settlement status, identifies and classifies payments to the correct client, program and account, and resolves unidentified or misapplied payments
Performs follow-up for delinquent accounts and rejected third-party claims (insurance, managed care, Medicare and Medi-Cal); resolves billing disputes or discrepancies; coordinates with branches, clinicians and Finance to resolve billing and payment discrepancies
Reconciles monthly Aging reports; registers clients for San Francisco and Peninsula and enters clients for all regions into the SmartCare system; provides back up and support for other billing staff members in the event of staff absences or workload demands
JOB QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business Administration or a related field preferred
Minimum of three years of relevant professional experience in accounts receivable, accounting, bookkeeping, or related work required
Medical billing experience (Medicare and insurance) in an institutional setting strongly preferred
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) required
Experience with EHR system preferred
All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, including minorities, women, veterans, and disabled individuals. Qualified applicants with arrest and/or conviction records will be considered for employment in a manner consistent with Federal, state and local laws, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran, or disability status. Cytek® Biosciences Inc. is a leading manufacturer and supplier of flow cytometry products and services. Cytek’s compact, affordable instruments and wide ranging support offerings are used by researchers and clinicians all over the world. 

Flow cytometry is a powerful analytical tool used for identifying and quantifying cellular characteristics on a cell-by-cell basis up to tens of thousands of cells per second. This technology is used in research and clinical studies with various biomedical and therapeutic applications such as investigating the role of the body’s immune system in fighting cancer, diagnosing leukemia and lymphoma, and detecting minimal residual disease in organ transplant patients. Flow cytometry has many advantages over traditional microscopy since it enables the analysis of a greater number of cells in a fraction of the time.  

At Cytek, we are focused on accelerating the adoption of flow cytometry for one simple reason: to fuel scientific discovery. We have leveraged our highly experienced, best-in-the-business team to bring forth an innovative new class of flow cytometry solutions. These solutions deliver deep biological insights at an affordable price, provide high-end capabilities, and bring simplified workflows to more researchers than ever before.  

As a company, we also seek to maintain high ethical standards and a culture that values honesty, integrity and transparency in all that we do. Company decisions are driven by what is right for scientific discovery and customer support. We are committed to our employees, to the environment in which we live and to the communities we serve worldwide.

title: Sr. Manager Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)
ai_core_responsibilities: The Sr. Manager of FP&A will serve as the primary financial partner to the Academic department, leading budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning. They will develop models to analyze faculty utilization, instructional costs, and academic capacity to support strategic decision-making and operational efficiency.

description_text:
Company Description
As a leading healthcare education organization, Unitek Learning’s family of schools helps thousands of students launch and accelerate their careers every year. As a rapidly growing and highly successful company, Unitek is also a great place to pursue a rewarding and challenging career. We offer a competitive salary, generous benefits, unlimited growth potential, and a collegiate work environment.
Job Description
About the Role
We are seeking a detail-oriented, strategic finance leader to serve as the primary FP&A partner to Unitek’s Academic department across all divisions. This role provides financial insight, decision support, and strategic direction to help Academic leaders plan effectively, allocate resources, and advance academic quality, student success, and sustainable growth.
You will lead budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, and performance analysis for academic operations, partnering closely with Academic, divisional, and campus leadership. A central focus will be developing a consistent understanding of faculty utilization, instructional costs, and academic capacity across Unitek while accounting for the needs of individual programs and campuses.
The ideal candidate combines exceptional analytical rigor with the ability to build productive relationships with Academic leaders and translate financial insights into practical recommendations. Experience supporting academic organizations with physical, ground-based campuses is a major plus.
Key Responsibilities
Serve as the strategic finance partner to Academic leadership across all Unitek divisions, providing guidance on resource allocation, operating plans, and investment priorities.
Lead budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning for academic operations, aligning faculty and instructional resources with enrollment projections, program needs, and strategic objectives.
Become the resident subject matter expert on faculty utilization and instructional workforce planning, partnering with Academic leaders to assess teaching loads, staffing models, full-time and adjunct faculty mix, and hiring needs.
Develop models that connect enrollment, cohort size, course schedules, and program progression to faculty requirements, instructional costs, and classroom, lab, and clinical capacity, where applicable.
Partner with Academic leadership to identify opportunities to improve efficiency while supporting educational quality, student outcomes, and accreditation and regulatory requirements.
Produce precise monthly variance analysis and academic performance reporting, explaining key drivers, identifying risks and opportunities, and recommending actions.
Establish consistent academic operating KPIs and cost benchmarks across divisions, with appropriate adjustments for differences in program structure, delivery format, and campus requirements.
Support monthly Private Equity reporting, monthly Operations reviews and quarterly Board presentations with clear analysis and commentary on academic performance, resource needs, and strategic initiatives.
Partner with Finance, Operations, Human Resources, and enrollment teams to align assumptions, improve data quality, and strengthen accountability for academic financial performance.
Continuously improve financial models, reporting processes, and planning tools, including Adaptive Planning or comparable systems.
Who You Are
A strategic finance partner who builds credibility with Academic leaders and connects financial decisions to educational priorities.
A meticulous analytical leader who values accuracy, consistency, and clear explanations of business performance.
Skilled at translating complex operational and financial data into actionable recommendations for both financial and nonfinancial audiences.
Comfortable challenging assumptions constructively and influencing decisions across divisions and campuses.
Able to balance enterprise consistency with the practical needs of individual academic programs and locations.
Effective in a fast-paced, results-driven environment, with the judgment to navigate ambiguity and competing priorities.
Qualifications
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field (MBA, CPA or CFA a plus).
7–12 years of experience in financial planning and analysis or corporate finance roles.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (modeling, nested logic, scenario planning).
Experience with Anaplan, Adaptive Planning, Prophix or similar planning/reporting systems strongly preferred.
Private Equity-backed or multi-site services experience a plus.
Strong communicator with the ability to present complex information with clarity and brevity.
Demonstrated career growth, with at least one internal promotion in a prior role.
Additional Information
We Offer:
Medical, Dental and Vision starting the 1st of the month following 30 days of employment
2 Weeks’ starting Vacation per year. Increasing based on years of service with company
12 paid Holidays and 2 Floating Holiday
401k with company match
Company Paid Life Insurance at 1x’s your annual salary
Leadership development and training for career advancement
Tuition assistance and Forgiveness for you and your family up to 100% depending on the program

Position Summary

Works under the supervision of an assigned Supervisor to be responsible for tax
collection by receipting, recording, and depositing tax payments for Shelby
County and other municipalities.

Pay Grade: 48
Salary Commensurate with Experience and Education
 

Minimum Qualifications

 * Four (4) years of experience in municipal tax or bank receipting/collections,
   financial or mortgage institution tax collections, lockbox transactions
   and/or electronic processing or similar; AND

   administration, management, finance; OR
 * An equivalent combination of related education and/or experience.

Duties and Responsibilities

 * Collects and processes property taxes, including payments received in the
   mail, via payment kiosks, internet, counter transactions, and over the phone.

   of payment, the distribution of payment information to external payees (i.e.,
   mortgage companies and real estate services), the sending of Image Cash
   Letters to the bank, the electronic uploads from online banking providers,
   and the electronic payments received from the State of Tennessee.

   and payment activities.
 * Interfaces with vendors to ensure optimum equipment and software
   functionality.
 * Performs activities associated with the issuance of refunds via electronic
   workflow and routing software.
 * Assists taxpayers, mortgage companies, county offices, and other entities
   over the phone or in person with tax-related problem resolution.
 * Images critical tax documents.
 * Processes uploads of delinquent tax files submitted by various
   municipalities.
 * Research tax parcels under State and/or County appeals.
 * Performs other duties as required or directed.

 

KSAs

 * Ability to effectively communicate (verbally and in writing).
 * Ability to prioritize workflow and comply with internal controls to meet
   deadlines related to tax collection processes.
 * Ability to remain calm and presentable in hectic situations.
 * Ability to handle stressful situations and distractions.
 * Skilled at operating standard office equipment.
 * Skilled in Microsoft Office Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
 * Ability to perform multiple tasks simultaneously with accuracy.
 * Ability to convey tax information with tact, understanding, and courtesy.
 * Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

 

Special Requirements

 * Must have reliable transportation. May be required to work at offsite
   locations during tax season.

 

Disclaimer
This position is subject to a background check for any convictions that have a
substantial relationship to potential job duties. Only convictions that are
substantially related to potential job duties will be considered and will not
automatically disqualify the candidate.

Shelby County Resident Disclaimer

All employees hired after September 1, 1986, must be residents of Shelby County
and shall continue to reside in the County as a condition of their employment. 
The residency requirement shall not apply to certain public safety/civil service
employees.  This means exemption from this policy is in effect for the following
departments and positions: (1) Sheriff Deputy Patrol Officers, Deputy Jailers
and Dispatchers, employed by the Sheriff Department, (2) Correction Officers
employed by the Division of Corrections, (3) Firefighters, Paramedics and
Dispatchers employed by the Shelby County Fire Department.  The residency
exemption for public safety/civil service employees does not include Appointed
positions with Sheriff’s Office, Division of Corrections or the Fire Department.

description_text:
The Senior Financial Analyst supports the financial and operational performance and strategic business decisions for our manufacturing sites. This individual will provide supply chain finance leadership to one of the Ecolab North America plants. This role reports into a Sr. Finance Manager of Manufacturing and is part of a team supporting multiple facilities.

The North America manufacturing team consists of 27 plants representing $600M in annual spend and key priorities include safety, quality, maintaining strong service levels to our customers, and driving productivity improvements.

Main Responsibilities
Drive financial performance management, including monthly closing, adhoc reporting/analytics, monthly forecasts, and annual budgets
Leverage new reporting and forecasting tools to provide new insights and create efficiencies in existing processes
Prepare cost accounting analysis and maintain strong internal financial controls, ensuring compliance with SOX requirements
Lead annual standard costing updates for the site
Identify savings opportunities and return on investment, improve financial processes through automation and redesign
Partner with other Supply Chain teams across North America
Support capital investments to ensure appropriate return on investments
Support building a TPM Loss reduction culture that drives financial accountability and ownership throughout all levels of the organization

What You Will Do
Act as a Financial Business Partner focused on driving strong financial acumen and decision support that results in financial metric improvement and profitable growth. Key business partners will be the plant manager and other plant leaderships
Drive tools and analytics locally to help business partners with areas of opportunity to improve costs and understand how projects/actions translate financially
Maintain a culture focused on policy adherence and financial controls to ensure appropriate monitoring of operations financially. Assure policies are being followed in accordance with SOX, GAAP, and Corporate Policy
Manage all accounting procedures related to operations (e.g., G/L maintenance, accruals, expense charge-off, journal entry preparation, payroll processing, capital equipment authorization, asset management, and inventory control including inventory reconciliations)
Support network-wide improvements by leading standard work and process development across the North America network focused on simplification and efficiency with leveraging shared services, consistent analytical tools, and metrics

Position Details
This position will have a seat in the Naperville, IL office with weekly onsite work expectations at the Bedford Park, IL plant location

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field
3 years of experience in finance and/or accounting
Immigration sponsorship is not available for this role

MBA, CPA, CMA
2 years of experience in a manufacturing environment
2 years of experience in cost accounting
Proficiency in SAP, PowerBI, Hyperion, Blackline

Strong change management skill set and leadership capability
Strong understanding of accounting concepts and practices
Demonstrated ability to drive financial performance, influence management, and lead change

Strong agility in learning and operating in system/data environments to drive efficiency in process and decision support

title: Special Funds Accountant
ai_core_responsibilities: The Special Funds Accountant manages daily financial operations, including bank deposits, electronic payments, and accounts receivable billings. ai_requirements_summary: A bachelor's degree in accounting or a related field is preferred, along with experience in GAAP and governmental accounting policies. Proficiency in the Cardinal accounting system, Microsoft Office, and strong reconciliation and reporting skills are required.
description_text:
Title: Special Funds Accountant

State Role Title: Financial Services Spec I

Hiring Range: $72,514 - $96,491

Pay Band: 4

Agency: Department of Juvenile Justice

Location: Main Street Centre

Agency Website: www.djj.virginia.gov

Recruitment Type: General Public - G

Job Duties

The Special Funds Accountant is responsible for managing and monitoring daily
financial operations related to special funds, revenue, deposits, electronic
payments and other assigned financial activities. The position manage all daily
bank deposits and electronic payment activity. Prepare AR billings for past-due
customer accounts, process the monthly telecommunications bill and coordinate
distribution to departments. Oversee the administration of special funds, block
grants, federal cash, and indirect cost recovery. Reconcile internal financial
records with Cardinal revenue and expenditure data to ensure accuracy and
compliance. Provide timely and accurate financial information to management to
support strategic resource allocation.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in accounting, business administration, or related field
preferred or equivalent experience.
Experience using and implementing Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
(GAAP) and governmental accounting policies and procedures for business needs.
Knowledge of governmental (state/federal) financial management and reporting
requirements.
Comprehensive knowledge of the state accounting system Cardinal.
Ability to prepare reports, use spreadsheets and pivot tables, to perform
reconciliations.
Excellent oral and written communication skills. Proficient with Microsoft
Office applications.
Knowledge of grant rules and regulations.
High degree of accuracy and the ability to prioritize to meet timelines.
Competent with organizing documents and filing both electronically and manually
for quick accessibility.
Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing and able to collect
data and prepare reports.


Additional Considerations

License as a Certified Public Accountant (CPA). Experience in indirect cost
allocation methodologies.Prior experience in data input, accounting to include
accounts receivable, and billing operations.

Special Instructions

You will be provided a confirmation of receipt when your application and/or
résumé is submitted successfully. Please refer to “Your Application” in your
account to check the status of your application for this position.

Individuals desiring to be considered for this position must submit a completed
employment application or you may attach a resume before the position’s closing
date. Applications received after the closing date will not be considered.
Documents sent through postal mail, email, or fax will not be considered.

Applicants are encouraged to be specific regarding job-related knowledge,
skills, and abilities.

You will be provided an email confirmation of receipt when your application
and/or résumé is submitted successfully. Please refer to “Your Application” in
your account to check the status of your application. Status updates will not be
provided via telephone or email.

local agency checks; employment verification; verification of education (if
required and relevant to employment); credit checks; and other checks based on
the position.

Pre-employment medical screenings are required for some DJJ positions.

or leased vehicle.

Supplemental Questions:

application. This information may help us evaluate your credentials and
qualifications for the job. Failure to respond to any questions may disqualify
you from further consideration.

Interagency Placement Screening Form (Yellow Card) or Preferential Hiring Form

position. You can include the Card as an attachment with your state application.

their spouses. Veterans who are hired into state positions may be eligible to
receive additional leave accruals based on their total years of service in the
military, National Guard, or Reserve. If applicable, please submit form DD-214
with your state application.

The Commonwealth of Virginia welcomes all applicants authorized to work in the
United States. Sponsorship is not provided; therefore, applicants must be a
citizen or national of the U.S., a Lawful Permanent Resident, or an alien
authorized to work.

Reasonable Accommodations:

application and/or interview processes per the Americans with Disabilities Act.
Contact our Human Resources Department for further assistance.

opportunities to all employees and applicants in accordance with applicable laws
and regulations. It is our policy to prohibit discrimination on the basis of
race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender
identity, age, veteran status, political affiliation, genetics, or disability in
the recruitment, selection, and hiring of its workforce. Qualified individuals
with disabilities are encouraged to apply. It is our goal to foster a culture
that demonstrates the principles of civility, diversity, opportunity, and
inclusion.


Contact Information

Phone: emails only

Email: elon.greene@djj.virginia.gov

Nikkiso Clean Energy & Industrial Gases is a leading provider of cryogenic pumps, heat exchangers, process systems, services, and solutions for the LNG and industrial gases industry. Ensure compliance with accounting standards (US GAAP / IFRS) related to revenue recognition
Support audit processes, including documentation for revenue recognition and contract accounting
Collaborate cross-functionally to resolve discrepancies and improve financial accuracy
Key Focus Areas
• Revenue recognition (POC / ASC 606) • Project accounting & contract management • Financial close & reporting excellence • Cost accounting & margin improvement • Process improvement & standardization
Qualifications

OpenAI’s Controllership team provides accurate, timely, and decision-useful financial information while building the processes, systems, and controls needed to support a rapidly growing global business. Our Accounting Operations team owns core accounting and close activities and drives improvements that help our finance organization scale.
About the Role
We are looking for an Accounting Manager with a strong general accounting foundation and hands-on intercompany experience to join our Accounting Operations team. You will own accounting and close activities across assigned balance sheet and P&L areas, manage intercompany activity for assigned entities, and build efficient, well-controlled processes.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role with responsibility for independently managing accounting processes, exercising sound judgment, and reviewing work performed by outsourced partners. You will partner closely with Tax, Treasury, Strategic Finance, and Business Systems to resolve issues, support business growth, and improve how we work.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will: 
Own the close for assigned accounting areas, including accruals, prepaids, and other balance sheet and operating expense accounts, ensuring accurate results and timely completion.
Prepare and review journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules; resolve accounting issues and maintain clear, audit-ready documentation.
Manage intercompany accounting for assigned entities, including cross-charges, reconciliations, and coordination of settlements. Investigate differences and drive timely resolution with counterparties.
Support consolidation activities, including intercompany eliminations, entity-level validations, and foreign currency accounting, in partnership with the consolidation lead.
Analyze balance sheet and P&L movements, develop clear flux commentary, and partner with Strategic Finance to explain business drivers and variances.
Coordinate and review work performed by outsourced accounting partners, setting expectations for quality, timeliness, and issue escalation.
Own and improve internal controls within assigned processes, maintain process documentation, and support external audits.
Drive process improvements and automation, partnering with Business Systems to improve Oracle workflows, strengthen data quality, and reduce manual work through tools and AI-enabled solutions.
Support new entities, acquisitions, and business initiatives by establishing accounting workflows and integrating them into the close.
You might thrive in this role if you have: 
6+ years of progressive accounting experience, with demonstrated ownership of close processes and experience reviewing others’ work or managing in outsourced support.
A strong general accounting foundation and practical knowledge of U.S. GAAP, including accruals, reconciliations, and financial statement analysis.
Hands-on intercompany accounting experience, including recording transactions, reconciling balances, and resolving differences across entities.
The judgment to independently resolve routine and moderately complex accounting issues, identify risks, and escalate matters with clear recommendations.
Experience operating and improving internal controls and supporting financial statement audits.
Proficiency with ERP systems and advanced Excel skills; Oracle Fusion experience is preferred, and exposure to Oracle FCCS or another consolidation system is a plus.
A track record of improving accounting processes, with curiosity about automation and AI tools.

description_text:
About Us
Endeavor Air is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Delta Air Lines. Flying as Delta Connection, Endeavor operates 145 regional jets on 800 daily flights to 122 destinations in the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.
Headquartered in Minneapolis, Minn., Endeavor has hub operations in Atlanta, Cincinnati, Detroit, Minneapolis, New York, and Raleigh-Durham, and 11 maintenance bases across our network.
Our Culture
We know that our people are our greatest assets, and we are committed to building a culture where employees love coming to work each day. At Endeavor Air, we foster a diverse, culturally-rich and safe workplace where employees are treated with dignity and respect. With a culture built on safety, excellence, and teamwork, Endeavor offers limitless potential for aviation professionals looking to start or continue their careers.
Our team promotes an inclusive environment in all aspects of the airline and our operation. As an EEO employer, we provide opportunities for all qualified candidates without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran, or disabled status.
Overview
The Senior Manager, Financial Planning & Analysis leads the day-to-day activities, development, and management of the Endeavor FP&A team, acting as a dynamic, high-performing leader who operates as a true financial thought partner to the business – not simply a reporter of results. 
This role owns the financial outlook for Endeavor, proactively identifies risks and opportunities, and is expected to know what good looks like in FP&A: bringing best-practice thinking, a bias for continuous improvement, and the independence to drive initiatives forward with minimal oversight. The individual will regularly engage with and present to senior leadership – including VPs and the C-suite – and must have the experience, confidence, and executive presence to do so credibly. 
This role leads a team of finance professionals focused on creating value in partnership with Endeavor business units through meaningful, insight-driven analysis that optimizes financial and operational performance.
Responsibilities
Owns the financial outlook for Endeavor – understands every major driver of the forecast, identifies emerging risks and opportunities before they become surprises, and clearly articulates what will happen and why.
Crafts the narrative, not just the variance – goes beyond explaining what happened in the numbers to build a clear, compelling story for senior management that answers "so what" and "what's next," turning analysis into a decision-ready recommendation rather than a data recap.
Serves as a key Delta Finance interface – given Endeavor's financials roll up into Delta's consolidated results, partners directly with Delta Finance counterparts to align on variance narratives, ensure Endeavor's perspective is represented in joint reviews, and maintain a consistent story across both organizations.
Operates independently, exercising sound judgment on prioritization and escalation; requires minimal day-to-day direction from the Director to move initiatives forward.
Brings a continuous-improvement mindset – proactively identifies opportunities to streamline, automate, and improve FP&A processes and the broader business, rather than waiting to be asked.
Creates and maintains ongoing reporting that influences business decisions; manages financial analysis and report generation activities to meet reporting requirements.
Presents confidently and credibly to VPs and C-suite audiences, synthesizing complex analysis into concise, executive-ready narratives and recommendations rather than data dumps.
Pressure-tests analyst work for rigor and accuracy, directs analysts toward the specific analysis needed to answer a business question, and coaches the team to raise analytical rigor, storytelling, and financial literacy.
Manages departmental activities to ensure business objectives are met on time, within budget, and with maximum accuracy and quality.
Leads analysis of key financial and operational issues and helps drive the annual operating plan preparation.
Other Duties
Other duties as assigned 
Supervisory Responsibilities
This position supervises 3–5 analysts and is responsible for employee development, performance management, coaching, and day-to-day leadership of assigned staff.
Competencies Required
Ethics and Values - Serves as a champion to employees and projects that are beneficial to the company. Displays courage and willingness to take an unpopular stance to make positive long-term progress for individuals and the organization.
Knows Our Business - Looks for ways to improve our success operationally and through people. Understands how all aspects of the business operate in a systemic way. Technically and professionally skilled to do the job at a high level of accomplishment. 
Builds Trust and Decision Making - Models honesty and open communications in large group meetings. Responds to challenge in a positive way – sees as an opportunity to learn new perspectives and perhaps improve the organization.
Drive for Results by Inspiring Others - Builds passion and enthusiasm for the organization’s mission. Identifies measurements that will drive long term positive results, and shares the rationale, thus engaging the organization.
Know Your Team and Leading People - Inspires organization to build effective work relationships that are based on strengths and focused on achieving organizational goals, understanding, and utilizing each team member’s interests and development goals. As a leader, proactively sees opportunities for talented and diverse staff to work with upper leadership to promote development and results.
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and related experience.
5+ years of experience in a dynamic finance or accounting role.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, take ownership, and drive initiatives with minimal oversight.
Strong analytical, interpretive, and organizational skills, with the ability to both perform and direct complex analysis.
Prioritization and time management skills; able to meet deadlines efficiently and effectively.
Interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills; able to work with all levels of an organization.
Ability to effectively convey a professional demeanor in all interactions.
Advanced Excel skills required.
Preferred
2+ years of supervisory experience
FP&A-specific experience (versus broader finance or accounting experience).
Experience presenting to and influencing senior leadership (VP level and above); comfortable in C-suite settings.
A demonstrated track record of proactively identifying and driving process or business improvement opportunities, not simply executing assigned tasks.
Experience building executive-level narratives/storylines (not just variance reporting), ideally including exposure to a parent company, board, or external stakeholder audience.
Advanced degree or certification (e.g., MBA, CPA)
Work Environment & Physical Demands
Can involve long periods of sitting. Computer work, repetitive motion such as typing. Subject to critical deadlines.
Minimal physical exertion such as: pulling, pushing, reaching, bending, standing, walking, and light lifting of boxes, bags files, and electronic equipment not in excess of 30 lbs.
Travel up to 10%.
What We Offer
Providing world-class service to our customers starts with providing world-class benefits to our employees. Endeavor Air employees receive a competitive total compensation package which includes a variety of benefits to choose from and some of the best perks around.
Free or reduced-rate travel privileges on Delta Air Lines and 80+ air carriers worldwide for employees and eligible family members.
Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Plans.
401(k) with Company Match starting on Day 1.
Operational Performance Rewards (OPR) Program.
Life and AD&D Insurance, Short and Long-term Disability, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), and voluntary supplementary benefit options.

title: Senior Financial Analyst
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Financial Analyst leads the delivery of clinical and financial information to support strategic decision-making and manages complex financial reporting for external partnerships. description_text:
Position Summary

The Financial Analyst leads the analysis and delivery of patient-level clinical and financial information to support operational, financial, and strategic decision-making across the medical center or health system. Develops case-based operating budgets, patient-volume forecasts, utilization projections, and gross-revenue estimates. Oversees service-line profitability reporting, cost-accounting activities, and integration of clinical and financial data within a patient-centered decision-support repository. Establishes performance measures and benchmarks business operations against healthcare industry best practices and internal objectives. Applies advanced knowledge of healthcare decision support, financial analytics, and industry standards to lead complex, high-impact projects. 

 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

 * Supports the financial management of external partnerships by providing financial reporting, planning, analysis, and presentations to UCSF leadership and joint governance boards.
 * Partners with Accounting to ensure timely and accurate monthly financial statements, supporting analyses, annual operating budgets, partner payments, and board materials.
 * Collaborates with Revenue Cycle, Contracting, and Physician Compensation teams to forecast, monitor, and evaluate performance against contractual requirements, budget targets, and organizational expectations.
 * Identifies, investigates, and supports resolution of financial and operational variances in collaboration with joint boards, advisory committees, and internal stakeholders.
 * Prepares monthly partnership profit-and-loss statements, including administrative services expenses, payment calculations, reconciliations, and adjustments to align estimated payments with actual partner liabilities.
 * Collects, analyzes, and reports physician productivity data, including work relative value units (wRVUs), FTE, and other relevant performance metrics.
 * Prepares physician payroll summaries to support accurate accounting of professional services agreement expenses.
 * Calculates physician compensation and periodic incentive payments in accordance with employment agreements; maintains accurate, auditable compensation models and supporting documentation.
 * Develops financial pro formas for physician compensation, benefits, new or existing physician practices, and other strategic initiatives.
 * Creates and enhances scalable monthly reporting, financial dashboards, performance measures, and analytical tools for internal business partners.
 * Leads or supports implementation of financial systems, reporting tools, and process improvements.
 * Develops multi-year operating and capital budgets, provides budget recommendations, and partners with department leaders to explain variances and resolve financial or procedural issues.
 * Performs complex financial, statistical, and ad hoc analyses to support leadership decision-making and partner collaboration.
 * Designs or improves analytical methods, databases, reporting structures, and performance-measurement approaches.
 * Supports data modeling, data flow design, and secure operational frameworks for reliable delivery of financial and business intelligence.
 * Prepares monthly variance analyses and narrative commentary for leadership review.
 * Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Competencies

Works closely with leadership, Joint Ventures & Affiliations, medical center and faculty practice finance teams, decision-support professionals, department managers, and external consultants. The successful candidate thrives in a fast-paced, evolving environment; manages ambiguity and competing priorities effectively; and anticipates bottlenecks, evaluates trade-offs, and advances projects with limited direction. Strong judgment, analytical ability, communication and negotiation skills, influence, and leadership are essential.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
 * Three or more years of progressively responsible financial planning, analysis, reporting, decision support, or healthcare finance experience, including at least two years in a healthcare, physician practice, medical center, or health system environment.
 * Strong knowledge of healthcare finance, clinical and operational planning, budget development, financial data management, service-line or partnership profitability, and business development analysis.
 * Demonstrated experience preparing complex financial analyses, forecasts, pro formas, budgets, variance reports, and performance reporting that inform executive and operational decision-making.
 * Advanced knowledge of decision-support methodologies, business statistics, quantitative analysis, data modeling, relational databases, performance measurement, and profitability analysis.
 * Ability to synthesize complex clinical, operational, and financial data into clear, accurate, and actionable insights, recommendations, and executive-level presentations.
 * Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to perform complex queries, assess data integrity, identify trends and variances, and develop practical solutions to business issues.
 * Strong project-management and organizational skills, with the ability to independently prioritize competing work, manage ambiguity, anticipate risks or bottlenecks, and deliver high-quality work on deadline.
 * Demonstrated ability to lead complex projects, guide cross-functional stakeholders, and build productive relationships with leaders, finance teams, clinical and operational partners, and external collaborators.
 * Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate sophisticated financial and technical information clearly and concisely to varied audiences.
 * Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and financial reporting, analytical, and business-intelligence tools. Experience with SQL and relational databases required; experience with Tableau, Essbase, Cognos, enterprise data warehouses, or comparable reporting platforms preferred.
 * Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to handle sensitive financial, compensation, and partnership information with confidentiality.

title: Senior Accountant
organization: Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Accountant performs advanced professional accounting work, including complex general ledger management, account reconciliations, and financial reporting. They also support audit processes, manage restricted funds and fixed assets, and provide financial analysis to assist with University decision-making.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must possess a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, or a related field. A minimum of four years of progressively responsible accounting experience is required, specifically in general ledger accounting and financial reporting.
description_text:
Description
Recruitment Period: 10/07/2026 - Until Filled
Status: Full-Time, 40 hours/week
Salary Information: Annual Minimum Salary-$67,200-Annual Maximum Salary-$107,500
Hiring Rate: Dependent upon qualifications and experienceOn Campus Position
Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences (PNWU) was founded as a 501(c) (3) non-profit medical institution in 2005 aimed at increasing access to health care in medically underserved areas of the Pacific Northwest.

The University currently offers the degrees of Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, Doctor of Physical Therapy, Doctor of Dental Medicine, Master of Biomedical Sciences, and Master of Science in Occupational Therapy enrolling over 550 students annually. Interprofessional education partnerships with other universities adds another 100 students to the population. The campus includes 300 employees with academic programming spread over a five-state region.

PNWU is located in Yakima, WA, a city of approximately 95,000 located in the south-central part of the state near the eastern slopes of the Cascade Mountains in a major agricultural and outdoor recreation region. It is approximately 140 miles from Seattle, 170 miles from Portland, and 200 miles from Spokane. The Yakima Valley is a wonderful place to live, work and play. For more information, visit https://www.visityakima.com/.

Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences (PNWU) does not sponsor employment visas. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and for the duration of their employment with PNWU. Employment eligibility will be verified in accordance with federal law.

General Summary: 
The Senior Accountant performs advanced professional accounting work in support of the University’s financial reporting and accounting operations. The position is responsible for complex general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, journal entries, financial reporting support, fixed assets, grants and restricted funds, audit schedules, and other assigned accounting activities.

The Senior Accountant works independently to research and resolve accounting issues, analyzes financial information for accuracy and reasonableness, and supports timely and accurate monthly and year-end close processes. The position serves as a key accounting resource to the Controller and provides guidance and backup support across Finance functions as needed.

The Senior Accountant brings initiative, ownership, and consistent follow-through to the work, establishes credibility through high-quality and well-documented results, and builds trusting relationships across Finance and the University. The position shares technical knowledge generously with colleagues, seeks and applies feedback, and approaches complex, non-routine problems with curiosity and sound judgment, understanding that reliable financial information supports the students and communities PNWU serves.

Essential Job Functions:
Duties an employee must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation.

General Accounting and Financial Reporting
Perform advanced general ledger accounting, including preparation and review of journal entries, account reconciliations, accruals, allocations, and other financial adjustments.
Maintain assigned balance sheet and income statement accounts and ensure activity is accurate, complete, properly supported, and reconciled timely.
Participate in monthly and year-end close processes and assist the Controller in ensuring established close deadlines are met.
Assist with preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements and supporting schedules.
Analyze account activity, financial results, and variances; research unusual or unexpected activity and recommend appropriate corrections.
Research and resolve complex accounting issues and document conclusions and supporting analysis.
Maintain appropriate documentation supporting financial transactions, reconciliations, and accounting conclusions.
Specialized Accounting
Perform accounting and reconciliation activities for restricted and designated funds, grants, fixed assets, leases, debt, investments, and other assigned areas.
Maintain fixed asset records and related depreciation schedules and ensure additions, disposals, transfers, and construction activity are appropriately recorded.
Support grant and restricted-fund accounting, including review of activity for appropriate classification and compliance with applicable restrictions.
Assist with accounting for capital projects and ensure expenditures are appropriately classified in accordance with University capitalization policies.
Prepare and maintain assigned supporting schedules for significant balance sheet and financial statement accounts.
Audit and Compliance
Prepare assigned schedules, reconciliations, workpapers, and supporting documentation for the annual financial statement audit and other audits or reviews.
Respond to auditor requests and assist with research and resolution of audit questions.
Assist with preparation of financial information supporting Form 990 and other regulatory or external reporting requirements.
Maintain accounting records and supporting documentation in accordance with University policies, internal control requirements, and applicable record-retention standards.
Identify accounting errors, unusual transactions, control concerns, or other financial issues and communicate them promptly to the Controller.
Financial Analysis and Support
Perform financial analysis and prepare reports to support Finance and University decision-making.
Analyze trends and account activity and assist with explanations of significant financial statement variances.
Provide actual financial information and accounting support to the Director of Budget & Financial Planning for budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
Assist University departments with accounting questions, account research, transaction coding, and interpretation of financial information, communicating clearly and patiently with non-financial colleagues.
Prepare ad hoc financial reports and analyses as requested.
Financial Systems and Process Improvement
Maintain proficiency in the University’s financial systems and related reporting tools.
Participate in testing, implementation, and improvement of ERP, financial reporting, and other systems affecting accounting operations.
Identify opportunities to improve accounting processes, documentation, reconciliations, and internal controls.
Assist with development and maintenance of accounting procedures and standardized work processes.
Support automation and transition from manual processes where appropriate while maintaining effective financial controls.
Finance Team Collaboration and Professional Practice
Serve as an accounting resource to other Finance team members, sharing knowledge generously and providing technical guidance as appropriate.
Provide backup support for critical accounting and Finance functions as assigned, and assist with cross-training and documentation of accounting procedures.
Work collaboratively with Accounts Payable, Payroll, Student Accounts, Budget & Financial Planning, and other University departments to resolve financial issues.
Take initiative and ownership for assigned work, follow through on commitments, and communicate early when a deadline or result is at risk.
Build trusting working relationships across Finance and with University departments, clarifying expectations and roles before and during shared work and including the right people in the right conversations.
Resolve differences constructively and with care, listening to understand others’ perspectives and engaging in honest dialogue when there is disagreement.
Actively seek and apply feedback, regularly ask whether the work is being done right, and pursue continuous learning and technical growth relevant to current and future responsibilities.
Connect daily work to PNWU’s mission of serving rural and medically underserved communities, understanding how accurate, well-stewarded financial information supports students and the University.
Other duties as assigned

Standard Institutional Requirements (apply to all roles):
Performs job duties in accordance with safety, legal, and regulatory requirements; University policy and procedures; and accepted business practices.
Acts with the highest level of professional ethical standards in all aspects of job performance, in accordance with the mission and values of PNWU.
Understands and adheres to accreditation standards and expectations specific to the department.

Salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience. Pro-rated based on hours/week. For this role, our anticipated hiring range is $67,200/$107,500 annual.
Every range at PNWU divides into four quartiles anchored at the midpoint. Quartile placement blends what a person brings and how they perform, which is our commitment to behaviors and results expressed in placement mechanics. The general framework:
1st Quartile ($67,200-$77,250/annual). New to this level or role. Brings relevant experience but is new to the scope of work at this level; developing the full breadth of the role; generally 0 to 3 years at this level. Meets expectations and is still establishing a track record.
2nd Quartile ($77,250-$87,300/annual). Developing to proficient; generally 3 to 5 years at this level or equivalent. Proficient across core responsibilities, consistently meets and sometimes exceeds expectations, and has established credibility with colleagues and partners.
3rd Quartile ($87,300-$97,400/annual). Fully qualified and performing at market rate. The midpoint marks the fully qualified employee whose performance is satisfactory in all respects. Substantial experience, generally 5 to 10 years; consistently strong performance; serves as a trusted expert resource.
4th Quartile ($97,400-$107,500/annual). Highly skilled, consistently high-performing, high-contributing. Extensive experience, typically 10 or more years; recognized institutional expert whose work adds significant value. Reserved for the most senior and exceptional cases.
Requirements
Education & Experience:
To perform the essential functions of this position, the incumbent must have:
A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field from an accredited institution. AND Four years of progressively responsible accounting experience, including experience with general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, journal entries, and financial reporting. OR
An equivalent combination of education and experience that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the essential functions of the position.
Desired Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:
Strong accounting knowledge, attention to detail, and analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to independently research, analyze, and resolve complex accounting issues.
Experience in financial systems and enterprise resource planning (ERP) platforms.
Experience preparing audit schedules and supporting external financial statement audits.
Sound professional judgment, integrity, and commitment to accuracy, with the ability to recognize unusual financial activity and communicate concerns appropriately.
Effective written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain accounting matters clearly to non-financial colleagues and to provide technical guidance to peers.
Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple deadlines.
Reliability, ownership, and follow-through, with a track record of delivering accurate work on recurring deadlines.
Ability to solve non-routine problems with curiosity and sound judgment, and to recognize when a matter should be escalated.
Ability to build trusting working relationships across Finance and with departments throughout the University.
Openness to feedback and a demonstrated commitment to continuous learning and professional growth.
Emotional intelligence and flexibility in navigating change, ambiguity, and differences in communication style and workstyle.
Ability to connect day-to-day financial work to PNWU’s mission and to the students and communities the University serves.
Commitment to documentation, internal controls, continuous improvement, and responsible stewardship of University resources.
To ensure full consideration submit:
A letter of introduction outlining background and qualifications for the position.
Detailed resume.
Contact information for three professional references.
The job announcement above is not the full job description but represents the job responsibilities and requirements. A full job description can be provided upon request.
