ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have three to five years of accounting experience, specifically within the nonprofit sector. Proficiency in fund accounting, GAAP, and ERP software like Sage Intacct is required.
description_text:
Description
Position Summary
The Accounting Specialist plays a key role in the Finance Department by performing day-to-day accounting functions including journal entries, bank reconciliations, grant accounting support, intercompany billing, account reconciliations, cost allocations, and maintaining accurate financial records to support organizational compliance and reporting requirements.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
General Accounting
Prepares and posts routine and recurring general journal entries. 
Supports month-end, quarter-end, and year-end closing processes. 
Complete and maintains accurate bank reconciliations for multiple bank accounts. 
Performs balance sheet account reconciliations and resolves discrepancies in a timely manner.
Maintains detailed schedules and supporting documentation for assigned accounts.
Assists with preparation of monthly financial statements and support schedules.
Maintains organized, accurate, and accessible financial records for audit and compliance purposes.
Maintains accurate contract, grant, and financial files.
Accounts Payable Support
Assists with accounts payable processing, including invoice coding, expense allocations, check requests, vendor payments, employee expense reimbursements, and supporting documentation.
Ensures expenditures are coded to the appropriate program, department, location, and funding source.
Preform and/or assist with bank reconciliations and check clearing.
Assists with maintaining vendor files, W-9 documentation, and payment records.
Reconciles company and employee credit card statements and ensures expenditures are properly coded and supported.
Intercompany Accounting and Allocations
Prepares and records intercompany billings and allocations to ensure accurate cost sharing across entities, programs, departments, and locations.
Maintains detailed allocation schedules and supporting documentation.
Tracks construction contracts and pass-thru funds account balances and reconciliations.
Assists with monthly cost allocations and shared expense distributions.
Grant Accounting and Compliance
Maintains grant-related financial spreadsheets, including revenue, expenses, match requirements, and funding utilization.
Tracks restricted and unrestricted funding activity.
Verifies that grant expenditures are properly coded and comply with funding source requirements.
Assists with reimbursement requests and invoicing to funding agencies.
Compiles supporting documentation for grantors monitoring reviews and site visits.
Assists with grant reporting and financial compliance requirements.
Maintains supporting schedules for federal, state, county, city, and private grants.
Audit and Financial Reporting Support
Assists with year-end audit preparation, supporting schedules, and auditor requests.
Assists with preparation of information required for Form 990 filings.
Supports internal and external audits, monitoring reviews, and compliance examinations.
Assists in maintaining effective internal controls and identifying process improvements.
Other Duties
Performs special projects and other duties as assigned.
Supports cross-functional Finance Department activities as needed.
Requirements
REQUIREMENTS
Three to five years of accounting or finance experience required.
Nonprofit accounting experience required.
Knowledge of fund accounting principles required.
Knowledge of grant accounting and compliance requirements preferred.
Experience with bank reconciliations, account reconciliations, and general ledger accounting required.
Experience with Sage Intacct or similar ERP accounting software required.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, including formulas, Pivot Tables, lookups, and financial reporting.
Working knowledge of GAAP and internal control practices required.
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise professional judgment.
WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL WORK DEMANDS
Sit and work at a computer station for extended periods of time.
Stand and work at a computer station for extended periods of time.
Stoop, kneel, bend at the waist, and reach on a daily basis.
Lift and move up to 20 pounds occasionally.
Regular and reliable attendance is required.
Hours may occasionally exceed 40 hours per week to meet organizational deadlines.
ESSENTIAL JOB COMPETENCIES: 
Collaborative: Works harmoniously with others to get a job done; responds positively to instructions and procedures; able to work well with staff, co-workers, peers and managers; shares critical information with everyone involved in a project; works effectively on projects that cross functional lines; helps to set a tone of cooperation within the work group and across groups; coordinates own work with others; seeks opinions; values working relationships; when appropriate facilitates discussion before decision-making process is complete.
Confidentiality; maintains company (employee, finance, customer, etc) information confidential; work area is secure; distributes information only for legitimate business reasons and according to company and legal guidelines.
Detail Oriented: Is alert in a high-risk environment; follows detailed procedures and ensures accuracy in documentation and data; carefully monitors gauges, instruments or processes; concentrates on routine work details; organizes and maintains a system of records.
Flexibility: Remains open-minded and changes opinions based on new information; performs a wide variety of tasks and changes focus quickly as demands change; manages transitions from task to task effectively; adapts to varying customer needs.
Honesty; has honest, direct, and factual communication and actions with internal and external customers.

Full-time employees are offered medical, dental, vision and 403b options. The Society covers 90% of the cost for medical, vision, and HMO dental benefits
SVDPLA provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics.

title: Senior Analyst, Financial Planning & Analysis
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Financial Analyst will support annual budgeting, forecasting, and month-end reporting to provide actionable business insights. They will also maintain financial systems and develop analytical models to improve reporting automation and operational efficiency.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a Bachelor's degree in Finance or Accounting and at least 5 years of progressive experience in FP&A or finance. Strong proficiency in financial analysis, Microsoft Office, and experience with reporting tools like SAP or Tableau is preferred.
description_text:
Overview
We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) at Shure. 
As our Senior Financial Analyst, you will support financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and analysis that contribute to informed decision-making and business performance. You will support budgets, forecasts, financial results, and operational insights across multiple functions and geographies, while contributing to the FP&A organization through reporting and analytics, financial systems support, process improvement initiatives, and continuous enhancement of planning and analytical capabilities.
This role will be hybrid from our Niles HQ office.
Responsibilities
Support annual budgeting activities across assigned areas including budget preparation, systems coordination, deadline management, and validation of submitted budgets.
Prepare month-end reporting packages and analyze financial performance to identify key trends, risks, opportunities, and variances.
Provide financial analysis and support to cross-functional stakeholders by translating financial information into actionable business insights that support decision-making.
Develop monthly forecasts and planning updates by incorporating business drivers, assumptions, and emerging trends, while supporting alignment on outcomes and expectations.
Identify business risks, opportunities, and emerging issues, and develop recommendations that support informed decision-making and business performance.
Develop, maintain, and enhance financial reporting, dashboards, analytical models, and business intelligence tools to improve visibility, efficiency, decision-making and reporting automation.
Maintain and support financial systems, master data, planning tools, and reporting platforms to ensure data accuracy, reliability, and effective business support.
Support the implementation, enhancement, and adoption of financial planning, reporting, and analytics tools and systems.
Identify opportunities to improve planning, reporting, forecasting, automation, data quality, and process efficiency, and develop recommendations that enhance financial operations and analytical effectiveness.
Support special projects, strategic initiatives, and other business priorities as assigned.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Accounting or related field. MBA is a plus.
At least 5 years of progressive FP&A, finance or accounting experience in a complex business environment. Experience working within a manufacturing or CPG company is a plus.
Strong understanding of financial statements, budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and business performance management.
Strong communication skills both written and verbal. Demonstrated ability to synthesize and effectively convey findings to management and functional areas.
High level of detail orientation and organization, as well as ability to multi-task and handle multiple concurrent projects.
Proven ability to self-motivate in a fast-paced environment, ability to deal with ambiguity, change and a dynamic business environment.
Proven ability to develop strong relationships and partnerships with internal customers, peers and effectively manage those relationships.
Experience effectively working across multiple departments to complete a project or resolve an organizational challenge.
Advanced computer literacy skills with an emphasis on Microsoft Office, specifically Excel, Word, and Power Point.
Experience with SAP, OneStream, Tableau, Power BI, Microsoft Copilot, or similar reporting, planning, and analytics tools preferred, but not required.
Able to exercise judgment within defined procedures and practices to determine appropriate action.
Strong business acumen and ability to appropriately handle confidential information.
Detail-orientated with strong organizational skills.
Applicants for this position must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Shure will not sponsor applicants for this position for work visas.
WHO WE ARE
Shure’s mission is to be the most trusted audio brand worldwide – and for over a century, our Core Values have aligned us to be just that. Founded in 1925, we are a leading global manufacturer of audio equipment known for quality, reliability, and durability. We engineer microphones, headphones, wireless audio systems, conferencing systems, and more. And quality doesn’t stop at our products. Our talented teams strive for perfection and innovate every chance they get. We offer an Associate-first culture, flexible work arrangements, and opportunity for all.
Shure is headquartered in United States. We have more than 35 regional sales offices, engineering hubs, distribution centers and manufacturing facilities throughout the Americas, EMEA, and Asia.
Join Shure and Amplify Your Impact. Explore our unique culture and learn the key pillars that define our legacy of excellence.
THE MIX MATTERSDon’t check off every box in the job requirements? No problem! We recognize that every professional journey is unique and are committed to providing an equitable candidate experience for all prospective Shure Associates. If you’re excited about this role, believe you’ve got the skills to be successful, and share our passion for creating an inclusive, diverse, equitable, and accessible work environment, then apply!PAY TRANSPARENCYShure offers a competitive compensation structure that is reviewed annually to attract, hire, and retain the industry’s top talent. Base salaries vary based on qualifications, geography, experience, and expertise in each respective discipline. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum base salary for the opportunity. The base salary for this position ranges from $86,800 to $138,900 with a target salary of $86,800-$113,000. If your salary expectations do not align, still apply as we are often flexible on the seniority of posted positions. All positions also include an award-winning benefits package.
WE GOT YOU - Our BenefitsAt Shure, we prioritize the well-being of our Associates. We offer competitive rewards packages that address physical, mental, financial, and overall well-being. Our benefits include comprehensive healthcare, mental health and retirement savings plans, generous paid time off programs, employee discounts, professional development opportunities, work-life balance initiatives, employee recognition programs, and volunteering/community involvement opportunities. To learn more, check out our Benefits At A Glance.

title: Senior Cost Accountant
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Cost Accountant is responsible for executing standard cost updates, managing co-manufacturer cost audits, and supporting financial reporting and planning. This role also involves maintaining inventory costing accuracy, performing variance analysis, and ensuring data integrity within SAP.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a bachelor's degree in accounting or finance and 3-5 years of cost accounting experience, preferably in CPG or food production. Proficiency in SAP or similar ERP systems and strong Excel skills are required for this role.
description_text:
BUILT ON FLAVOR. FUELED BY PEOPLE.
What’s it like to work at Kinder’s? Well, there’s a lot of snacking and geeking out over what we all cooked over the weekend. Beyond that, there’s also plenty of hard work. Because we don’t just like flavor, we’re obsessed with it. 
With over 100 products sold nationwide, we’re now a top-five brand in multiple flavor categories at Costco, Walmart, Whole Foods, and more. We’re not your typical CPG company. Privately held and founder-led, we like to think of ourselves as a pirate ship in a sea of cruise ships. Our crew is adventurous and fearless. We chart our own course and chase big ideas to make food unforgettable. 
As we expand globally and approach $1 billion in revenue, we need more smart-and-scrappy, flavor-obsessed people to come aboard. If you’re looking for a place where you can see the real impact of your work... this is it! Every day, you’ll be part of a journey to add flavor to millions of meals and lives. 
About The Role
We are seeking a Senior Cost Accountant to support the accurate and timely costing of co-manufactured products. This role is responsible for executing standard cost updates, assisting in co-manufacturer cost audits, and contributing to financial reporting and cross-functional planning efforts.
While this position requires strong cost accounting skills, it also demands more than technical proficiency. The ideal candidate is someone who understands cost drivers, can identify material changes or trends, and thrives in environments where not all inputs are finalized. This role requires the ability to assess cost sensitivities, flag risks, and make recommendations that help inform financial and operational decisions — even in the face of ambiguity.
This is a high-visibility, high-impact role well suited for someone looking to deepen their cost accounting expertise - in a fast growing CPG company - and grow into broader ownership within a dynamic and rapidly scaling company.
This is also a highly impactful role for someone who wants to own meaningful financial processes and contribute to a fast-growing business. It is also a role that requires comfort with ambiguity and proactive problem-solving. You’ll thrive in this role if:
You enjoy solving problems in fast-moving, sometimes ambiguous environments
You’re comfortable working with incomplete information and can build credible estimates based on what’s known today while flagging what might change tomorrow
You bring strong technical fundamentals in cost accounting and have the mental agility to go beyond inputs and think in terms of cost drivers, sensitivities, and decision impact
You can collaborate cross-functionally with clarity, patience, and influence, whether it’s with finance, procurement, operations, or external partners
You’re energized by owning your work, building scalable processes, and improving things as you go
This is not the right role for someone who needs all inputs finalized before moving forward or who prefers highly structured environments with little ambiguity. Kinder’s moves fast. Some cost inputs won’t be perfect. But your ability to create clarity, offer insight, and take ownership is exactly what will make you successful - and satisfied - here.
Key Responsibilities Include:
Standard Cost Execution & Ongoing Maintenance
Execute standard cost updates for co-manufactured SKUs, ensuring calculations are accurate, timely, and well-documented
Use BOMs and recipes to calculate cost per unit, incorporating raw materials, packaging, tolling and processing fees, and warehousing or logistics components
Coordinate with Procurement, Operations, and internal and external Co-Manufacturing teams to collect inputs, validate changes, and prepare updates for manager review and approval
Maintain organized costing support files and documentation to enable traceability and audit readiness
Inventory Costing Support & Audit Preparation
Support accurate inventory valuation at Kinder’s 3PL warehouses by preparing costing schedules, tie-outs, and supporting analyses
Assist in internal and external inventory audits by compiling documentation, reconciling variances, and supporting audit requests
Identify inventory costing issues and elevate exceptions and risks to the Cost Accounting Manager with clear supporting detail
Cost Analysis, Variance Reporting & Driver Identification
Perform product-level variance analysis and investigate key cost drivers, including material changes and co-manufacturing performance impacts
Support pricing and promotional decisions by providing accurate cost data
Assist with gross margin and product-level profitability reporting

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting Support

Track key input costs (materials, packaging, tolling, freight) and surface meaningful changes that could impact margin performance

Co-Manufacturer Cost Support & Invoice Reconciliation
Support ongoing co-manufacturer cost monitoring by preparing invoice reviews, tie-outs, and reconciliation schedules

Audit & Compliance Testing Support
Perform compliance testing of co-manufacturer charges and ingredient pass-throughs, including reasonableness checks and contract-based validations
Document results, exceptions, and follow-up requirements in a structured and audit-ready format
Escalate anomalies and recurring issues to the Cost Accounting Manager with supporting evidence and recommendations
Month-End Close Support Activities
Prepare close support schedules, journal entry support, and reconciliations related to COGS and inventory costing under manager direction
Assist with monthly variance explanations by preparing detail and analysis to support reporting narratives
Ensure deliverables are complete, accurate, and delivered on schedule to support the broader close process
SAP Costing Execution & Data Integrity Support
Maintain costing accuracy in SAP through disciplined execution of updates, validation checks, and error resolution support
Support product costing, BOM maintenance processes, and inventory transaction reviews to ensure costing outputs remain reliable
Identify recurring data integrity issues and propose improvements to reduce manual rework and improve consistency
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Continuous Improvement Support
Work closely with Finance, Operations, Procurement, and external co-mans to ensure alignment on cost inputs and impacts
Contribute to initiatives that improve cost visibility, reporting reliability, and execution efficiency
Build credibility through responsive communication, high-quality analysis, and strong ownership of deliverables
Skills & Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or related field
3–5+ years of cost accounting experience, preferably in a CPG or food production environment
Experience supporting cost analysis, standard costing, and co-manufacturer invoice reviews

Strong Excel and data analysis skills
Excellent communication and collaboration skills

description_text:
Description
Join Blue Sky Bank's dedicated team as a Treasury Management Professional!

At Blue Sky Bank, we help businesses optimize cash flow, improve operational efficiencies, and safeguard assets through innovative treasury management solutions. As a Treasury Management Professional (TMP), you will serve as a senior treasury expert responsible for business development, consultative sales, client support, and treasury solution implementation.

This highly visible role partners with commercial clients, Treasury Management Officers, lenders, and internal teams to identify opportunities, deliver customized treasury solutions, and strengthen client relationships. The TMP serves as the team's subject matter expert on treasury products, payment technologies, and industry trends while providing mentorship, technical support, and guidance to Treasury Management Specialists.

Why Blue Sky Bank?
Benefits – Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes a starting accrual of three weeks of paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employer matching, and medical, dental, and vision insurance. Additional benefits include a Health Savings Account (HSA), Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Dependent Care FSA, voluntary accident and critical illness coverage, and 100% employer-paid short-term Disability, long-term disability, and group life/AD&D insurance, as well as optional voluntary life/AD&D coverage.
Strategic Influence – Serve as a trusted treasury expert who directly impacts client success, deposit growth, and treasury management strategy.
Professional Growth – Expand your expertise in treasury products, payment technologies, and commercial banking solutions.
Meaningful Relationships – Build lasting partnerships with business clients while collaborating with lenders, branch teams, and executive leadership.
What You'll Do
Serve as the Bank's subject matter expert on treasury management products, services, payment technologies, and industry trends.
Develop and manage treasury relationships with commercial clients, prospects, and internal business partners.
Identify, market, sell, and cross-sell treasury management solutions and commercial deposit products.
Conduct treasury needs analyses and recommend customized cash management, liquidity, payment, and fraud mitigation solutions.
Prepare and deliver treasury presentations, product demonstrations, and consultative client recommendations.
Analyze account, transaction, and portfolio data to identify growth, retention, and cross-sell opportunities.
Partner with Treasury Management Officers, lenders, and branch teams to support business development and relationship growth.
Lead treasury onboarding, implementation, and resolution of complex customer service and technical issues.
Serve as a liaison between customers and internal departments to ensure exceptional service and operational efficiency.
Review treasury documentation and implementation activities to ensure accuracy, compliance, and a seamless customer experience.
Mentor and train Treasury Management Specialists on treasury products, technology platforms, sales strategies, and industry best practices.
Monitor emerging payment technologies, fintech developments, and market trends to support innovation and product enhancement.
Assist with treasury reporting, audits, risk assessments, conversions, and special projects.
Support operational oversight functions, including reconciliations, exception resolution, service fee reviews, and cash logistics processes.
Promote a culture of professionalism, collaboration, innovation, and exceptional customer service.
Requirements
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Experience: 3+ years of treasury management or commercial banking experience.
Valid driver's license, proof of insurance, qualifying motor vehicle record report, and reliable transportation.
Demonstrated expertise in treasury management products, services, and payment technology (e.g., ACH, wire transfer, positive pay, remote deposit capture, merchant services).
Advanced analytical and financial/cash-flow modeling skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations.
Ability to pull, analyze, and interpret client, account, and product data from core banking, reporting, or CRM systems to identify and support marketing and cross-sell opportunities for treasury management products.
Strong, demonstrated comfort with technology, including treasury/cash management platforms and online banking systems, with the ability to quickly learn and champion new tools.
Forward-thinking approach to identifying industry trends, emerging payment technology, and competitive positioning.
Proven ability to mentor, train, and develop less experienced treasury management staff.

ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounting Manager oversees high-volume transactional accounting, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and cash management while supervising an Accounting Associate. They are responsible for month-end close, financial reporting, and ensuring all accounting practices remain GAAP-compliant across multiple entities.

description_text:
Description
The Accounting Manager is an accounting leader responsible for both high-volume transactional accounting and higher-level financial oversight. This position personally manages daily accounts payable, accounts receivable, payment processing, cash activity, reconciliations, month-end close, and financial reporting while supervising an Accounting Associate primarily responsible for accounts receivable. Success requires someone who is comfortable moving between detailed data entry, daily problem-solving, team management, and accurate GAAP-compliant reporting in a fast-paced, multi-entity environment.
This is not a review-only, advisory, or purely managerial accounting position. The successful candidate must be willing and able to personally process a significant volume of daily transactions, maintain accuracy under frequent deadlines and interruptions, and take ownership of both routine accounting work and complex financial responsibilities.
Key Responsibilities
Personally perform and support high-volume daily accounting operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payment processing, cash application, account maintenance, transaction entry, and reconciliation.
Oversee accounts receivable operations and personally assist with invoicing, cash application, collections, account reconciliation, refunds, deposits, and issue resolution as volume and deadlines require.
Direct, support, and hold accountable the Accounting Associate responsible primarily for accounts receivable, including assigning priorities, reviewing work, resolving escalated issues, providing training, and ensuring daily and monthly deadlines are met.
Manage the month-end close process, including preparation and review of journal entries, accruals, supporting schedules, and account reconciliations.
Prepare accurate and timely monthly financial statements and management reports, including consolidation of multiple entities.
Review and reconcile balance sheet accounts; investigate and resolve discrepancies promptly.
Reconcile and explain variances between actual results and monthly revenue projections for each branch.
Manage daily cash activity, bank reconciliations, payment processing, and weekly cash-flow reporting.
Prepare monthly commission reports and maintain accurate supporting documentation.
Maintain fixed-asset records and track capital expenditures.
Monitor accounts receivable aging, support collection efforts, and coordinate lien filings when appropriate.
Maintain strong internal controls and ensure accounting records comply with GAAP and company policies.
Coordinate annual insurance audits and provide accurate schedules and supporting documentation.
Prepare minority-business applications and related documentation.
Support special projects, including business acquisitions, system improvements, process documentation, and other accounting initiatives.
Communicate clearly with branch leaders, vendors, customers, and internal stakeholders to resolve accounting issues and meet deadlines.
Perform other accounting-related duties assigned by the supervisor or manager.

Requirements
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, with at least three years of progressive accounting experience in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment. Candidates must have demonstrated hands-on experience processing accounts payable, accounts receivable, payments, cash activity, reconciliations, financial and management reports, and multi-entity consolidations, as well as experience supervising or developing accounting staff.
CMP or CMA preferred but not required.
The ideal candidate combines strong technical accounting knowledge with the willingness and capacity to perform detailed daily accounting work consistently.
Strong working knowledge of GAAP, internal controls, financial reporting, journal entries, and account reconciliation.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and proficiency with QuickBooks or a comparable accounting system.
Demonstrated ability to organize and complete a high volume of recurring transactions while managing competing daily, weekly, and month-end deadlines without sacrificing accuracy or follow-through.
Proven ability to lead, train, prioritize work for, and hold accounting staff accountable.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve issues independently using available written or verbal guidance.
Excellent written, telephone, and in-person communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across departments and maintain a collaborative team environment.
High level of accuracy, confidentiality, integrity, dependability, and professional judgment.
Successful completion of required background check and drug screening.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in a multi-entity, multi-branch, professional-services, construction, engineering, or similarly transaction-intensive environment.
Experience supporting business acquisitions, audit preparation, process improvement, or accounting-system enhancements.
Working knowledge of lien processes and collections practices.

description_text:
About us 
Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today's needs and transition to more sustainable solutions. 
Purpose of the role
You will be responsible for providing intermediate-level accounting support for field operations. The role involves performing a range of semi-routine accounting and data-related activities, maintaining accurate information, and applying established procedures to complete assignments with minimal instruction.
You will use accounting systems, spreadsheets, databases, and other tools to enter, retrieve, calculate, and review information. You will also use sound judgment when determining the appropriate procedure or established practice to follow, recognizing issues and recommending practical solutions when needed.
Core Responsibilities
Perform field accounting and administrative activities in accordance with established procedures, processes, and project requirements.
Enter, retrieve, calculate, and maintain financial and operational information accurately and efficiently.
Review data and documentation for completeness, accuracy, and consistency and identify discrepancies or missing information.
Process routine accounting transactions and supporting documentation within established guidelines.
Maintain organized and accurate electronic and/or physical records.
Use spreadsheets, accounting systems, databases, and other applicable tools to support daily activities.
Perform calculations involving decimals, fractions, and other financial or operational data as required.
Research and resolve routine discrepancies by applying established procedures, prior experience, and available resources.
Recognize issues that fall outside established procedures and recommend appropriate solutions or escalate them to the appropriate team member.
Communicate accounting information, questions, and issues clearly with field personnel, project teams, and other stakeholders.
Support the timely completion of accounting activities and reporting requirements.
Follow applicable company, project, financial, and internal control procedures.
Maintain confidentiality and exercise appropriate care when handling financial and project information.
Contribute to a collaborative team environment and support continuous improvement in day-to-day processes.
What you’ll bring to the role
You will bring a practical approach to accounting support, strong attention to detail, and the ability to work independently within established processes.
Key qualifications and skills include:
Secondary school education or equivalent required.
2+ years of relevant accounting, finance, clerical, administrative, or project support experience.
Experience performing data entry, maintaining records, processing documentation, or supporting financial transactions.
Working knowledge of basic accounting principles and terminology.
Proficiency with spreadsheets and the ability to accurately enter, retrieve, organize, and calculate data.
Intermediate understanding of accounting systems, databases, or other tools used to support financial and field activities.
Strong attention to detail and a consistent focus on accuracy.
Ability to work with numerical information, including decimals, fractions, calculations, and financial data.
Ability to follow established procedures while determining the appropriate process or precedent to apply when situations vary.
Good problem-solving skills, with the ability to recognize issues and recommend solutions from a defined range of options.
Ability to manage multiple routine activities and maintain accuracy while working to established deadlines.
Clear and professional communication skills, with the ability to explain information and collaborate effectively with others.
Ability to work with minimal instruction while recognizing when an issue requires additional guidance or escalation.
A dependable, collaborative approach and willingness to support field and project team objectives.
Previous experience supporting accounting activities within an engineering, construction, energy, industrial, or project environment is beneficial. 
Moving forward together
We want our people to be energized and empowered to drive sustainable impact. So, our focus is on a values-inspired culture that unlocks brilliance through belonging, connection and innovation. We're building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Creating a space where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and are heard.
And we're not just talking about it; we're doing it. We're reskilling our people, leveraging transferable skills, and supporting the transition of our workforce to become experts in today's low carbon energy infrastructure and technology. Whatever your ambition, there's a path for you here.
And there's no barrier to your potential career success. Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities, and be part of delivering sustainable change.

Above all, what makes us different is our people. Operating as trusted partners to our clients, we deliver intelligent solutions through a combination of technical expertise and strong relationships based on deep client understanding. 
We’re driven by our Group purpose, to power people and possibilities.

As a senior manager on our fund administration team, you’ll work directly with leading private equity clients, supporting fund operations, financial reporting, and investor communications under the guidance of our experienced team. You’ll oversee client deliverables, review complex fund calculations and financials, manage audits, train junior staff, and drive process improvements across multiple engagements.
What you’ll do
You’ll lead client relationships across multiple Private Equity funds, ensuring expectations are met and timelines are followed.
You’ll apply your understanding of limited partnership agreements to fund operations, reporting, and investor communications.
You’ll prepare and review key financial components like journal entries, capital calls, distributions, and performance metrics such as IRR.
You’ll manage audits, tax requests, and financial statement reviews while continuously improving operational processes.
You’ll prioritize tasks, respond to client requests, and train junior team members to support team development and efficiency.
What we offer
IQ-EQ offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support employees' well-being and work-life balance. 
Employees receive generous paid time off, including 4 weeks of PTO that increases over time, sick time and paid holidays, and financial wellness is supported through a 401(k) plan with a company match (subject to eligibility).
Health benefits include medical, dental, vision, mental health support and additional ancillary insurance plans. 
Additional benefits include paid parental leave and a hybrid work schedule, promoting both personal and professional fulfillment.
The salary for this position will be dependent on experience and location ($107,000-$170,000). 
Qualifications
You bring over five years of progressive experience in private equity, public accounting, or a mix of both within alternative asset firms.
You demonstrate strong analytical and technical skills in accounting, finance, and fund administration.
You hold at least a Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance, giving you a solid foundation for your work.
You consistently deliver exceptional client service, building trust and long-term relationships.
You apply your expertise to support complex fund operations and drive high-quality outcomes.
Additional Information
Sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Our sustainability depends on us building and maintaining long-term relationships with all our stakeholders – including our employees, clients, and local communities – while also reducing our impact on our natural environment. 
There is always more we can, and should do, to improve – whether in relation to our people, our clients, our planet, or our governance. Our ongoing success as a business depends on our sustainability and agility in a changing and challenging global landscape. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable and diverse culture for our people, led by our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion steering committee. 
Our learning and development programmes and systems (including PowerU and MyCampus) enable us to invest in growing our employees’ careers, while our hybrid working approach supports our employees in achieving balance and flexibility while remaining connected to their colleagues. We want to empower our 6,500+ employees - from 94 nationalities, across 24 countries - to each achieve their potential. Through IQ-EQ Launchpad we support women managers launching their first fund, in an environment where only 15% of all private equity and venture capital firms are gender balanced. 
We’re committed to growing relationships with our clients and supporting them in achieving their objectives. We understand that our clients’ sustainability and success lead to our sustainability and success. We’re emotionally invested in our clients right from the beginning.

title: Finance Manager (FP&A)
ai_core_responsibilities: The Finance Manager will lead enterprise consolidations, maintain the long-range revenue model, and provide actionable insights to support executive decision-making. They will partner cross-functionally with commercial, product, and supply chain teams to drive growth and improve forecasting accuracy.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or Economics and at least 8 years of experience in FP&A or corporate finance. Proficiency in advanced financial modeling, ERP systems, and reporting tools like Oracle or Tableau is required.
description_text:
About us: Stanley 1913 - Built for Life® since 1913. 
The Stanley 1913 brand has fueled the human experience since the iconic Stanley vacuum bottle revolutionized the way people enjoyed food and beverage. Today, our colorful and thoughtfully designed products including the popular Quencher™ series go beyond function, elevating everyday moments with style and empowering active lifestyles. We’re a community of creators, builders, and inventors who believe in creating sustainable products for a better life and world that minimizes our impact on the planet. Learn more at www.stanley1913.com. 
Position Overview
Stanley 1913 is seeking a highly analytical and business-focused Finance Manager to support enterprise planning, forecasting, and performance management across the business. Reporting to the Senior Director of Global Finance Planning & Analysis, this role will serve as a key partner in driving insight into company performance, long-range growth planning, and execution of critical commercial initiatives.
This position will lead enterprise consolidations, maintain the Long-Range Planning (LRP) revenue model, provide insights into category and channel performance, and coordinate financial results tied to key Go-to-Market (GTM) achievements. The Finance Manager will partner closely with Commercial, Product, Demand Planning, Supply Chain Finance, and Marketing Finance leaders to translate business performance into actionable insights that support executive decision making.
This role serves as the Senior Director's key deputy for Global FP&A. It involves representing the function to senior leadership and handling a growing scope. It is an ideal platform for someone aiming to advance in finance leadership. This role leads one Financial Analyst and plays a senior leadership role within the FP&A organization. While the position is not responsible for a business unit P&L, it serves as a central point of coordination and strategic analysis across the enterprise.
This is a Seattle-based role requiring regular onsite presence at Stanley 1913's Seattle headquarters.
What You'll Do
Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidation process, ensuring timely and accurate aggregation of financial forecasts and business performance across functions.
Own and continuously enhance Stanley's Long-Range Planning (LRP) revenue model, partnering with business leaders to evaluate growth scenarios, strategic investments, and market opportunities.
Drive enterprise revenue forecasting processes, ensuring alignment between commercial strategies, product launches, channel plans, and financial expectations.
Partner with Category, Commercial, and Product teams to evaluate category performance trends and find opportunities to accelerate growth and improve execution.
Monitor in-year product and channel performance, delivering actionable analysis regarding sales trends, demand signals, launch performance, and business risks.
Coordinate financial support for key Go-to-Market (GTM) milestones, including product launches, commercialization plans, executive reviews, and strategic business updates.
Support pricing strategy activities in partnership with Global Merchandising, Strategy, and Regional Commercial teams to drive profitable growth.
Develop executive-level reporting, dashboards, and insights that communicate business performance, forecast changes, risks, and opportunities.
Support annual operating planning processes and key forecasting cycles through consolidation, scenario modeling, and business partnership.
Drive financial modeling and decision-support analyses related to growth initiatives, portfolio optimization, and commercial performance.
Partner cross-functionally to improve planning processes, forecasting accuracy, and reporting effectiveness.
Mentor and develop a Financial Analyst while fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and business partnership.
Leverage financial systems and reporting tools to automate processes, improve data visibility, and increase analytical capabilities across the organization.
Champion continuous operational improvement across planning and reporting, thoughtfully employing automation and emerging AI tools to accelerate analysis, deepen insights, and scale the team's impact.
Who You Are
A strategic finance professional who enjoys connecting financial insights to business outcomes and influencing decisions across a complex organization.
Experienced in managing enterprise planning processes and translating large volumes of data into clear, actionable recommendations.
A strong collaborator who builds credibility and partnerships across Finance, Commercial, Product, Supply Chain Finance, and Marketing Finance teams.
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where priorities evolve and ambiguity is common.
An exceptional communicator who can confidently present financial insights to senior leaders and executive partners.
Naturally curious, thorough, and proactive in identifying risks, opportunities, and operational improvements.
Passionate about developing talent and building successful teams.
Education & Experience
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.
8+ years of dynamic experience in FP&A, commercial finance, strategic finance, or corporate finance.
Experience leading enterprise forecasting, planning, and financial consolidation processes.
Advanced financial modeling skills, including scenario planning, revenue forecasting, and long-range planning.
Experience analyzing category, channel, customer, or product performance within a consumer products or retail environment preferred.
Advanced Excel skills and experience building sophisticated, driver-based forecasting models.
Experience with ERP, planning, and reporting tools such as Oracle, Essbase/SmartView, Power BI, Tableau, Anaplan, or similar solutions.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively in a matrixed environment.
Demonstrated people leadership experience, including directly managing and developing analysts.
Success Measures
Within the first 12 months, this leader will:
Improve visibility and accuracy of enterprise revenue forecasts.
Establish robust governance around the Long-Range Planning revenue model.
Deliver consistent insights on category and channel performance to support executive decision making.
Deepen financial Revenue and Margin target setting support for major GTM achievements.
Develop team capabilities while creating scalable forecasting and reporting processes across Stanley's growth agenda.

The Stanley 1913 brand is owned by Morgan Street Holdings (formerly HAVI), a privately held enterprise with a diverse portfolio of operating companies, including HAVI Supply Chain, tms, and Continental. Morgan Street Holdings’ portfolio provides best-in-class sourcing and supply chain capabilities, brand-defining marketing and promotion services, innovative consumer products, and dining and refreshment food solutions. Morgan Street Holdings employs over 10,000 people and serves 300+ customers across the globe.

title: Assistant Controller
ai_core_responsibilities: The Assistant Controller manages accounting operations, ensures compliance with GAAP and internal controls, and oversees financial reporting for the division. They also participate in the financial close process, support audits, and provide leadership to the finance team.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance and at least 5 years of experience in accounting and financial reporting. Proficiency in ERP systems and knowledge of manufacturing sector accounting practices are required.
description_text:
Federal Signal is looking for an Assistant Controller to serve as a member of
site Finance team, responsible for the accounting operations of assigned
division(s) including generation of periodic financial reports, maintenance of
accounting records in accordance with a comprehensive set of controls designed
to mitigate risk, and ensuring reported results comply with generally accepted
accounting principles.

Key Activities/Responsibilities :

 * Provide support to BU Controller ensuring information is prepared and
   maintained in accordance with all statutory and regulatory requirements for
   the jurisdictions in which the business unit operates as well as Generally
   Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Company standard policies and
   procedures (SPP).
 * Assist in maintaining internal control systems to satisfy Sarbanes Oxley
   requirements and Federal Signal Standards of Internal Controls (SICs) and
   confirm all documentation is prepared and completed in accordance with
   Company policy.
 * Hands on participation in the financial close process including
   preparing/reviewing journal entries, submission of results to Corporate,
   account reconciliations, providing financial information/analytics as
   requested.
 * Prepare relevant financial reporting of performance and detailed analysis of
   variances.
 * Oversee intercompany and CAPEX activities for the business unit.
 * Support internal and external audits and work with Controller to resolve any
   identified issues timely.
 * Attend S&OP and Budget/Forecast meetings to remain informed of key business
   developments.
 * Apply continuous improvement methodology to improve the cost structure of the
   business unit.
 * Manage assigned team and provide for the following:  coaching, training,
   development, policy enforcement, performance management, and corrective
   action.
 * Participate in acquisition diligence and integration efforts.

Job Requirements/ Skills Needed:

 * Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting or Finance required, Master’s or MBA
   preferred
 * Certified Public Accountant (CPA) Preferred
 * 5+ years’ experience in accounting and financial reporting
 * 3+ years’ experience in a manufacturing environment preferred
 * 3+ years’ Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems experience
 * Strong working knowledge of accounting practices in the manufacturing sector
 * Knowledge of finance operations and cost control principles including the
   following:
   * Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
   * Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) requirements
 * Knowledge of automated financial and accounting reporting systems (JDE
   preferred)
 * Proven effectiveness in leading and directing the work of others
 * Ability to ensure compliance to and identify weaknesses in accounting
   controls and policies
 * Ability to prepare financial reports, statements, and projections
 * Demonstrated resourcefulness in setting priorities and proposing new ways of
   creating efficiencies
 * Strong written, communication and interpersonal skills required with the
   ability to participate in and facilitate group meetings
 * Advanced MS Office skills, especially Excel

Salary Range: $88,892 - $126,989 Plus Annual Bonus Opportunity

Benefits of Employment

In addition to excellent career growth opportunities, Federal Signal Corporation
offers a wide array of benefits including annual bonus potential, insurance
(life, medical, dental, vision), paid holidays, paid vacation, 401(k) with
matching contributions and tuition reimbursement. We provide our employees with
a smoke-free, drug-free workplace.

About Us

Federal Signal in University Park is a leading manufacturer and supplier of
comprehensive systems and products used to protect people and property. Our
products and integrated solutions include systems for campus and community
alerting, emergency vehicles, first responder interoperable communications,
industrial communications, and command and municipal networked security.
Specific products include: lightbars and sirens, public warning sirens and
public safety software.

Federal Signal Corporation (NYSE: FSS) builds and delivers equipment of
unmatched quality that moves material, cleans infrastructure, and protects the
communities where we work and live. Founded in 1901, Federal Signal is a leading
global designer and manufacturer of products and total solutions that serve
municipal, governmental, industrial and commercial customers. Headquartered in
Downers Grove, IL, with manufacturing facilities worldwide, the Company operates
two groups: Environmental Solutions and Safety and Security Systems. For more
information on Federal Signal, visit: www.federalsignal.com
[http://www.federalsignal.com]

The Company is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will not be
discriminated against on the basis of, and will receive consideration for
employment without regard to, race, color, religion, national origin, sex,
sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information,
status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category, characteristic,
or trait under applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation in the
application process, contact Human Resources at HR@federalsignal.com
[HR@federalsignal.com]. All other applications must be submitted online.

description_text:
RubinBrown LLP is one of the nation’s leading accounting and professional
consulting firms with a commitment to building personal relationships and
delivering totally satisfied clients. The RubinBrown name and reputation are
synonymous with experience, integrity, and value. We have revenue of
approximately $265 million with 1,000+ team members across locations in Chicago,
Denver, Detroit, Kansas City, Las Vegas, Mumbai (India), Nashville, and St.
Louis.

Overview

The SALT Manager will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of state and
local income tax compliance, planning, audits, and consulting for a diverse
client base. This individual will collaborate directly with firm partners and
team members in delivering superior quality income tax consulting and compliance
services. The SALT Manager is responsible for the development, motivation, and
supervision of SALT engagement team members. This includes providing leadership,
coaching, and career guidance to foster a high-performing team and ensure the
delivery of superior quality and service to clients.

Major Responsibilities

Client Service & Tax Consulting

 * Review state income, franchise, and other state and local tax returns for
   accuracy and completeness.
 * Identify, research and consult on complex state and local tax matters.
 * Utilize tax-related software to prepare, review, and process returns.
 * Respond to inquiries, notices, and audit requests from tax authorities.
 * Review client documentation and SALT workpapers for completeness and
   technical accuracy.
 * Work closely with partners and team members to promptly resolve client issues
   or tax matters.
 * Develop and maintain strong working relationships with client management
 * Maintain working knowledge of accounting principles and federal taxation.

   consulting.
 * Plan and complete assignments efficiently while recognizing, researching,
   documenting, and resolving technical tax issues.

   objectives to support tax planning and consulting services.

Engagement & Practice Management

   collections.

   timely.
 * Participate in firm practice development activities, including proposals,
   presentations, and client meetings.

   regulations.

Leadership & Team Development

   client operations and outcomes.
 * Demonstrate ability to cultivate and expand professional relationships with
   clients, firm leadership, and external stakeholders to strengthen client
   engagement, generate new opportunities, and support firm growth

Preferred Experience/Background/Skills

 * Bachelor’s degree in accounting (preferred), Finance, Taxation, or related
   field required.
 * 5-8+ years of state & local income tax experience in public accounting or
   corporate tax
 * CPA or other similar professional designations
 * Advanced technical knowledge of state & local income tax laws, regulations,

 * Ability to manage multiple engagements and deadlines effectively.

 * Ability to demonstrate proficiency with Firm-adopted technology systems and
   databases.

 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills, interpersonal, analytical
   and research abilities
 * Demonstrate leadership, mentoring, and team building capabilities.
 * Proficiency in Microsoft Office programs (Word and Excel required)
 * Strict adherence to professional ethics

WORKING CONDITIONS

 * The typical office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Core Responsibilities
The Risk Manager will provide direction and oversight of risk management at a corporate and national level for development and operational assets. The successful candidate will work alongside the client’s risk management committee and partner with internal and external legal, development, and acquisitions teams to oversee and manage risk-related matters across a diverse portfolio of development, redevelopment, and stabilized real estate investments. This individual will enforce and drive strategy as it pertains to compliance, loss events and will improve internal processes to mitigate future loss and risk. Duties and responsibilities will include:
Serve as the primary risk and insurance liaison among client leadership, asset management, business partners, and Lockton teams. 
Build and maintain relationships with executives, legal teams, joint venture partners, lenders, and external advisors. 
Communicate risk, insurance, and claims matters effectively to senior stakeholders. 
Lead strategic oversight and coordination of insurance claims. 
Manage builder's risk, OCIP, and construction liability programs for development projects. 
Develop and implement risk management policies, procedures, and governance practices. 
Oversee master and asset-level insurance programs and support renewal strategy. 
Review and analyze insurance requirements, partner programs, contracts, and indemnification provisions. 
Maintain compliance with third-party insurance obligations and related documentation. 
Oversee enrollments, contracts, safety initiatives, and regulatory compliance matters. 
Evaluate project risks and recommend risk mitigation strategies for development, construction, and asset management activities. 
Partner with operational teams to align exposures with appropriate insurance coverage. 
Support enterprise risk management initiatives, including business continuity, emergency response, ESG, and sustainability programs.


Bachelor’s degree in business-related field, or equivalent education and experience 
Minimum 5 years of risk management experience
Strong understanding of real estate development, operations and related insurance and risk management practices.
Experience with contract review and negotiation specific to the insurance and indemnity sections of loan documents and other legal agreement.
The ability to provide guidance on insurance requirements to the executive teams, counsel, asset managers, clients, and business partners. 
General knowledge of legal and compliance; experience in working directly with legal counsel
Working knowledge of all lines of insurance – including policies, coverages and fundamentals 
Real estate industry experience preferred
Excellent analytical, organizational, interpersonal, critical thinking skills
Administrative and organizational skills critical; excellent time management skills, flexibility, and management of a variety of tasks simultaneously
Reliable and thorough with a deep commitment to accuracy
Excellent client service skills with the ability to develop sound relationships with internal and external stakeholders at all levels of the organizations
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States and not require sponsorship for this position, now or in the future
Benefits
Lockton is committed to advancing diversity and inclusion. We have a dynamic entrepreneurial culture in which our people are empowered to make a difference to better serve client needs. We are committed to giving back to our communities and we are invested in your success.
We offer a competitive total rewards package, continuing education & training, and tremendous potential with a growing organization.

title: Accounts Payable Technician II
ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounts Payable Technician II is responsible for processing vendor invoices, maintaining accurate financial records, and resolving payment discrepancies. They also support internal and external audit activities while ensuring compliance with established accounting procedures.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must possess a high school diploma and one to three years of experience in bookkeeping or accounting. Proficiency in accounting software, Microsoft Office applications, and strong data entry skills are required.
description_text:
Overview
Chenega is a mission-driven Alaska Native corporation and a top Alaska revenue business, with nearly 9,000 employees worldwide and 50 years of steady growth. Consistently ranked among the Top 5 Alaska-owned businesses in the Alaska Top 49ers list, we deliver professional services across defense, intelligence, and civilian markets with operational excellence, integrity, and accountability.
As an Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (ANCSA) corporation, Chenega combines strong business performance with a commitment to community and cultural values. We are a recognized military-friendly employer, with many veterans, reservists, and military spouses across our workforce. Our culture is performance-driven, team-oriented, and focused on doing the job right while providing long-term career opportunities.
Summary: 
The Accounts Payable Technician II is responsible for processing vendor invoices, maintaining accounts payable records, researching payment discrepancies, and supporting timely payment of financial obligations. The position works closely with Chenega subsidiaries and internal departments to ensure accurate invoice processing, compliance with established accounting procedures, and effective support for month-end, year-end, and audit activities.
Work Location: 
In-office 3000 C St, Ste 301, Anchorage, AK 99503.
Responsibilities
Duties and Responsibilities:
Process accounts for payable transactions, including invoice review, coding, entry, validation, and payment processing, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and adherence to departmental procedures.
Serve as a primary point of contact for accounts payable inquiries from Chenega subsidiaries, providing timely responses and resolution of invoice and payment-related issues.
Utilize CHIP and related accounting systems to process invoices, maintain records, research transactions, and support payment activities.
Support internal and external audits by maintaining accurate records and providing accounts payable documentation in accordance with established accounting and records retention procedures.
Other duties as assigned
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications: (To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.) 
High school Diploma.
One (1)- three (3) years’ experience in bookkeeping and accounting required.
Experience working with accounting processing software, an Internet browser, Excel, Outlook, and any word processing software.
Excellent time management skills and strong attention to detail
Experience in Data Entry-Keyboarding)
Successfully pass background and drug screening.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with Costpoint.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Knowledge of accounts payable principles, invoice processing, and financial recordkeeping practices.
Ability to review invoices and support documentation for completeness and accuracy.
Strong attention to detail and ability to identify discrepancies in financial transactions.
Proficiency using accounting systems, spreadsheets, and Microsoft Office applications.
Ability to research and resolve payment discrepancies independently.
Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive financial and business information.
Physical Demands:
(The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.)
Sufficient fine motor skill for use of computers, calculator with an ability to withstand repetitive keyboarding for extended periods of time
Visual, auditory and communication abilities sufficient to perform the essential functions of the job
Ability to kneel bend and twist at the waist on an occasional basis,
Ability to push, pull, carry and lift objects weighing up to 20 pounds on a regular basis and more on an occasional basis
Ability to travel by plane and safely operate a motor vehicle
Work Environment: The employee will normally work in a temperature-controlled office environment, with frequent exposure to electronic office equipment.
During visits to areas of operations, may be exposed to extreme cold or hot weather conditions. Is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals, and loud noise.
Chenega Corporation and family of companies is an EOE. 
Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled
Native preference under PL 93-638.

title: Accounting Specialist - Full Time Days

address.addressLocality: FL, Riviera Beach, Kindred Hospital ,  Palm Beach

ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounting Specialist is responsible for managing accounts payable processes, including invoice matching, check runs, and vendor inquiries. Additionally, the role assists with journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, budget preparation, and maintaining fixed asset records.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a high school diploma or equivalent, with a bachelor's degree in accounting preferred. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and a thorough knowledge of accounts payable are required.
description_text:
Kindred Hospital The Palm Beaches and Acute Rehabilitation Unit (ARU) is a 68-bed specialty hospital. With 57 long-term acute care hospital (LTACH) beds, we offer the same in-depth care you would receive in a traditional hospital, but for an extended recovery period. Our 11-bed ARU is designed for people who have experienced the debilitating effects of an acute injury, impairment, or illness and like the LTACH, we partner with your physician and offer 24-hour clinical care seven days a week so you can start your journey to wellness. We are located just North of downtown West Palm Beach and about four miles inland from Riviera Beach.
Job Summary
Complies and reviews accounts payable documents and prepares document batches for processing, reviews completed accounts payable runs; prepares special manual checks; responds to employee and vendor inquiries; and prepares and maintains accounts payable records and reports. Assists the Accounting leader on journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, the reimbursement package, preparation of the budget and other accounting tasks as assigned. 
Essential Functions 
Participates in hospital and departmental performance improvement activities to measure and assess the quality of services provided. 
Adheres to all financial policies and procedures as established by the Corporation through its Board of Directors. 
Complies and reviews accounts payable documents according to established procedures. Matches receiving reports, purchase orders and invoices, and compares price and quantity information. Identifies any discrepancies and takes appropriate corrective action. 
Records appropriate vendor and expense account numbers on invoices and prepares accounts payable document batches for data processing. 
Reviews completed accounts payable check runs and ensures their accuracy. 
Matches suppliers credit memos with hospital debit memos. Investigates and resolves any identified discrepancies. 
Prepares special manual checks as directed, according to established procedures. 
Receives and answers inquiries from hospital employees and vendors regarding purchase orders, invoice data, accounts payable reports, maintains accounts payable records, and performs special projects related to accounts payable as assigned. 
Prepares accounts payable reports, maintains accounts payable records, and performs special projects related to accounts payable as assigned. 
Maintains hospital fixed asset records and coordinates payment off capital items with corporate accounts payable. 
Prepares monthly accrual journal entries with all necessary backup. 
Prepares other journal entries as directed by the Controller or Accounting Manager. 
Prepares monthly account reconciliations as directed by the Controller, or Accounting Manager. 
Prepares monthly reimbursement package as directed. 
Assists in the preparation of the annual budget. 
Assists on other close and accounting tasks, as required. 
Prepares daily statistical and cash reports. 
Assists in the preparation of payroll, if needed. 
Knowledge/Skills/Abilities/Expectations
Approximate percent of time required to travel: 0%25 
Basic computer skills with working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including excel spreadsheets, general ledger systems and accounts payable systems. 
Thorough knowledge of accounts payable. 
Must read, write and speak fluent English. 
Must have good and regular attendance.
Performs other related duties as assigned.


Education
High School Diploma or Equivalent including education equivalent to completion of secondary school or demonstrated ability to perform the essential functions of the role. (AND) Bachelor’s Degree in accounting (Preferred) Or Equivalent Combination of Education and Experience in accounting or finance in lieu of degree requirements (May be Considered)
Licenses/Certifications
None
Experience
Experience in a hospital or healthcare setting preferred.
