title: Controller
ai_core_responsibilities: The Controller will own the end-to-end accounting and financial operations, including the monthly close, audit, and financial controls. This role is also responsible for leading the integration of AI into finance workflows to automate repetitive tasks and improve reporting accuracy.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have 10+ years of relevant accounting experience, including at least 3 years as a Controller or Assistant Controller in a high-volume, recurring-revenue environment. Proficiency in QuickBooks, Excel, and a demonstrated ability to implement AI tools in finance are required.
description_text:
InterPayments is a San Francisco, CA-based, FinTech SaaS company sitting at the exciting intersection of payments and data intelligence. Our Mission is to empower merchants and the software vendors they use to lower payment processing costs. We create innovative data services that Fortune 1000 companies rely upon to lower fees by putting payments in competition on every swipe. 
We empower dedicated team-first individuals who are driven to solve problems to foster innovation, perform at their highest potential, and make a meaningful impact - while creating meaningful relationships along the way.
About the Role 
The Controller is a key member of the management team and owns InterPayments' accounting and financial operations end to end: the books, the close, audit, and the controls behind them. This role also leads our use of AI in finance, so that a high volume of recurring-revenue, partner, and commission transactions is processed accurately, on time, and with less manual effort every quarter. 
Key Responsibilities 
Accounting and reporting. Oversee all operational and reporting accounting. Maintain the general ledger and the Company’s books and records. 
Close. Own the monthly close and consolidation, including account reconciliations. Deliver against a defined close calendar and keep it moving earlier over time. 
Invoicing, AR, and AP. Oversee invoicing, AR, and AP. Keep invoices out on schedule and aged payables under control. 
Partner rev share and commissions. Own partner revenue share calculations and payouts, and the review and audit of sales commissions and MBO payouts. Work with HR on variable and year-end compensation. 
Controls and compliance. Design, implement, and monitor financial processes, policies, and controls that keep the Company audit-ready and compliant. 
Audit. Serve as the primary contact for the external audit firm and complete the annual audit on time. 
Planning. Partner with management on budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis. 
Cross-functional workflow. Work with Sales, Professional Services, and Legal to keep order-to-cash handoffs clean, including contract terms, subscription start dates, and invoice timing. 
Systems. Lead systems implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement across accounting (QuickBooks Online, Salesforce, Ramp, Gusto, and related tools). 
AI in Finance 
We expect the Controller to use AI as a standard part of how the finance function works, not as a side project. Within the first year you will: 
Automate the routine. Identify and automate repetitive workflows such as reconciliations, journal entry preparation, accrual support, invoice and bill coding, and rev share and commission workpapers. 
Add a control layer. Use AI to review transactions and payout data, flag anomalies and mismatches before close, and reduce rework and audit findings. 
Speed up reporting. Use AI to draft variance commentary, flux analyses, board and investor finance summaries, and audit support schedules, with human review before anything is issued. 
Govern it. Set clear guardrails for AI use in finance: data privacy and confidentiality, review and sign-off requirements, documentation for auditors, and approved tools. 
Build capability. Train the finance team and partner teams to use AI well, and track the hours saved and accuracy gained. 
Experience and Education 
10+ years of relevant accounting experience. 
3+ years as Controller, or equivalent experience as an Assistant Controller at a medium to large enterprise. 
Significant experience managing accounting for high-transaction-volume, recurring-revenue businesses, ideally SaaS or fintech. 
Proven track record running an efficient close and using systems to automate and remove manual processes. 
Hands-on experience applying AI tools to accounting or finance work, or a demonstrated ability to learn and adopt them quickly. 
Strong QuickBooks and Excel skills. Experience with Salesforce, Ramp, or similar tools is a plus. 
Excellent written and verbal communication, and comfort working across teams. 
CPA, public accounting, and FP&A experience preferred but not required. 
How We Work 
InterPayments values putting customers first, building trust, and doing the harder thing. We are team oriented, impact driven, and structured in how we make decisions. More information about the company will be shared with interested candidates. 
Remote pay range
$145,000—$165,000 USD
InterPayments’ core values are the building blocks of how we achieve our mission: Obsess about our Customers’ and Partners’ Needs; Be Relentless, Resilient, and Responsive; Collaborate with Teammates, Customers, and Partners; Act with Integrity and Empathy; Outperform your Potential; and Communicate Honestly and Respectfully. 
Remote Work Eligibility:
This position is open to candidates who are located in the United States. All remote roles are limited to U.S.- based residents, and the company does not sponsor visas or employ individuals who require work authorization outside of the United States. Only applicants who are legally authorized to work in the U.S. will be considered.
InterPayments is an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status, and encourage all qualified applicants to apply.

title: Controller
organization: Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences
ai_core_responsibilities: The Controller provides leadership and oversight for the university's accounting and financial operations, ensuring accurate financial reporting and effective internal controls. They are responsible for managing the accounting team, coordinating audits, and overseeing payroll, treasury, and financial systems.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, or business administration. A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in accounting or finance, including staff supervision, is required.
description_text:
Description
Recruitment Period: 10/07/2026 - Until Filled
Status: Full-Time, 40 hours/week
Salary Information: Annual Minimum Salary-$102,700-Annual Maximum Salary-$174,600
Hiring Rate: Dependent upon qualifications and experience
On Campus Position


Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences (PNWU) was founded as a 501(c) (3) non-profit medical institution in 2005 aimed at increasing access to health care in medically underserved areas of the Pacific Northwest.


The University currently offers the degrees of Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, Doctor of Physical Therapy, Doctor of Dental Medicine, Master of Biomedical Sciences, and Master of Science in Occupational Therapy enrolling over 550 students annually. Interprofessional education partnerships with other universities adds another 100 students to the population. The campus includes 300 employees with academic programming spread over a five-state region.


PNWU is located in Yakima, WA, a city of approximately 95,000 located in the south-central part of the state near the eastern slopes of the Cascade Mountains in a major agricultural and outdoor recreation region. It is approximately 140 miles from Seattle, 170 miles from Portland, and 200 miles from Spokane. The Yakima Valley is a wonderful place to live, work and play. For more information, visit https://www.visityakima.com/.


Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences (PNWU) does not sponsor employment visas. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and for the duration of their employment with PNWU. Employment eligibility will be verified in accordance with federal law.

General Summary:
The Controller provides leadership and oversight for PNWU’s accounting and financial operations, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial reporting, effective internal controls, regulatory compliance, and efficient financial processes. The Controller oversees general accounting, financial reporting, accounts payable, payroll, treasury operations, audit coordination, and related financial systems and processes.
The Controller serves as the University’s senior operational finance leader and works closely with the Vice President for Finance & Administration/CFO to safeguard University resources, strengthen financial operations, and support responsible financial stewardship.
As a leader of others, the Controller is responsible for building a cohesive, collaborative accounting and financial operations team grounded in trust, clear expectations, and psychological safety. The Controller coaches and develops the Senior Accountant, Accountant, Senior Accounts Payable Specialist, and Senior Payroll Specialist toward their full potential, delegates thoughtfully as people grow in capability, addresses concerns directly and with care, and keeps the connection between the team’s daily work and PNWU’s mission of serving rural and medically underserved communities visible and meaningful.

Essential Job Functions:
Duties an employee must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation. 
Accounting and Financial Reporting
Lead the University’s general accounting function and monthly and annual close processes, ensuring financial records are complete, accurate, timely, and appropriately supported.
Oversee preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements and related financial reports in accordance with GAAP and University policies.
Ensure timely completion and review of journal entries, general ledger activity, balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, allocations, and financial adjustments.
Oversee accounting for restricted and designated funds, grants, fixed assets, leases, debt, investments, and other significant or complex transactions.
Establish clear account ownership, reconciliation standards, documentation requirements, and close deadlines.
Research and resolve complex accounting and financial reporting matters and provide guidance to Finance staff and University leadership.
Financial Operations and Internal Controls
Provide leadership and oversight of accounts payable, payroll, and related financial operations, keeping the purpose behind the work visible so the team understands how sound financial operations support students and the University’s mission.
Establish and maintain effective internal controls, including appropriate segregation of duties, approval authority, transaction review, cash controls, and financial-system access.
Identify, investigate, and promptly communicate unusual transactions, financial errors, control deficiencies, compliance concerns, and other material financial risks to the CFO.
Develop, maintain, and enforce financial policies and procedures and recommend improvements that strengthen controls, efficiency, service, and accountability.
Partner with the CFO to establish and maintain procurement policies, approval thresholds, vendor controls, purchasing requirements, and related financial controls.
Promote electronic workflows, automation, and process improvements where appropriate while maintaining effective internal controls.
Treasury and Cash Management
Oversee University bank account activity, bank reconciliations, transfers, and related treasury controls within established authority.
Maintain appropriate controls over restricted funds and ensure restricted resources are used, transferred, recorded, and reported in accordance with applicable donor, grant, legal, and institutional requirements.
Support daily and periodic cash monitoring and provide accurate cash balances and actual financial information for liquidity planning and forecasting.
Coordinate with the CFO and Director of Budget & Financial Planning regarding cash needs, anticipated activity, and financial trends.
Audit, Compliance, and External Reporting
Lead Finance preparation for the annual financial statement audit and other financial audits or reviews, including preparation of schedules and supporting documentation, resolution of audit questions, and implementation of recommendations.
Serve as a primary Finance contact for external auditors and other financial reviewers.
Oversee applicable tax, regulatory, debt, grant, and financial compliance requirements and ensure required reporting and filings are accurate and timely.
Support preparation and review of Form 990 and other required external financial reports.
Maintain current knowledge of accounting standards, regulatory requirements, and emerging issues affecting higher education and nonprofit financial operations.
Financial Systems and Process Improvement
Provide Finance leadership for the general ledger and financial components of ERP, SIS, payroll, banking, and other integrated financial systems.
Participate in financial system implementations, upgrades, testing, process redesign, and development of internal controls.
Ensure system configurations, interfaces, reconciliations, and financial processes support complete and reliable financial reporting.
Identify opportunities to reduce manual processes, strengthen workflows, improve data integrity, and increase operational efficiency.
Leadership and Team Development
Lead, develop, and establish clear expectations, accountabilities, and priorities for staff within the Controller function, including accounting, accounts payable, payroll, and related financial operations.
Coach and develop each team member toward their full potential and career goals, providing timely, specific, and growth-oriented feedback along with technical guidance and professional development opportunities.
Build staff development plans that align individual growth with PNWU’s mission and strategic direction, and recognize and celebrate work that advances it.
Delegate thoughtfully, matching responsibility to capability and readiness, and expand authority as people grow in skill and confidence.
Address performance concerns proactively, directly, and with care, creating space for learning and growth.
Establish and sustain a team culture grounded in trust, psychological safety, and open communication, where questions, honesty, and mistakes are met with curiosity.
Ensure every team member has a voice in decisions that affect their work, and invite the team to solve problems together, drawing on diverse perspectives and creative thinking.
Lead the team through system implementations, process changes, and periods of transition with stability, transparency, and attention to the emotional dynamics of change.
Establish appropriate cross-training and backup coverage for critical Finance functions, and ensure staff understand their responsibilities, deadlines, internal controls, and escalation requirements.
Model transparency, consistency, and follow-through in words, decisions, and actions, and hold the team accountable for results and for the way those results are achieved.
Regularly ask whether the Controller function is doing the right things, and create space for the team to ask that question too, using data to evaluate the team’s impact and drive continuous improvement.
Encourage sustainable work practices, balance, and renewal across the team, recognizing that a healthy team is a prerequisite for serving students and the University well.
Collaborate closely with the Director of Budget & Financial Planning to ensure actual financial results, budgets, forecasts, and management reporting are aligned and reconciled.
Retirement and Benefit Plan Financial Oversight
Work collaboratively with Human Resources in the administration and financial oversight of the University’s 403(b) and 457 retirement plans and self-funded health plan.
Coordinate and lead Finance responsibilities for the 403(b) and 457 plan audits, including preparation and review of financial schedules, reconciliations, census and contribution data, supporting documentation, and responses to auditor requests.
Reconcile retirement plan contributions and related general ledger activity and coordinate with Payroll, Human Resources, plan administrators, recordkeepers, and auditors to investigate and resolve discrepancies.
Support financial oversight and reconciliation of the University’s self-funded health plan, including review of plan activity, funding, expenses, liabilities, and related financial reporting.
Monitor financial controls and accounting processes related to retirement and benefit plans and promptly communicate significant discrepancies, compliance concerns, or control issues to the CFO and Human Resources.
Support required financial reporting, audit follow-up, and implementation of corrective actions related to retirement and benefit plans.
Other duties as assigned

Standard Institutional Requirements (apply to all roles):
Performs job duties in accordance with safety, legal, and regulatory requirements; University policy and procedures; and accepted business practices.
Acts with the highest level of professional ethical standards in all aspects of job performance, in accordance with the mission and values of PNWU.
Understands and adheres to accreditation standards and expectations specific to the department.
Salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience. Pro-rated based on hours/week. For this role, our anticipated hiring range is $102,700-$174,600/annual)
Every range at PNWU divides into four quartiles anchored at the midpoint. Quartile placement blends what a person brings and how they perform, which is our commitment to behaviors and results expressed in placement mechanics. The general framework:
1st Quartile ($102,700-$120,650/annual). New to this level or role. Brings relevant experience but is new to the scope of work at this level; developing the full breadth of the role; generally 0 to 3 years at this level. Meets expectations and is still establishing a track record.
2nd Quartile ($120,650-$138,600/annual). Developing to proficient; generally 3 to 5 years at this level or equivalent. Proficient across core responsibilities, consistently meets and sometimes exceeds expectations, and has established credibility with colleagues and partners.
3rd Quartile ($138,600-$156,600/annual). Fully qualified and performing at market rate. The midpoint marks the fully qualified employee whose performance is satisfactory in all respects. Substantial experience, generally 5 to 10 years; consistently strong performance; serves as a trusted expert resource.
4th Quartile ($156,600-$174,600/annual). Highly skilled, consistently high-performing, high-contributing. Extensive experience, typically 10 or more years; recognized institutional expert whose work adds significant value. Reserved for the most senior and exceptional cases.


Requirements
Education & Experience:
To perform the essential functions of this position, the incumbent must have:
A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field from an accredited institution. AND Seven years of progressively responsible accounting or finance experience, including significant responsibility for financial reporting, general ledger accounting, financial close, internal controls, and audit, and including experience supervising and developing staff. OR
An equivalent combination of education and experience that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the essential functions of the position.
Desired Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:
Strong knowledge of GAAP, financial reporting principles, and accounting and financial-management practices.
Demonstrated experience leading accounting or finance staff and managing multiple financial functions.
Experience in financial systems and enterprise resource planning (ERP) platforms, with advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
Knowledge of payroll administration, payroll tax compliance, and payroll systems management, including multi-state payroll processing where applicable.
High degree of integrity, transparency, accountability, and professional judgment, including the ability to identify issues independently and communicate concerns promptly and clearly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to translate complex financial information for non-financial audiences, including at the board level.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines while establishing accountability across organizational boundaries.
Demonstrated ability to coach and develop staff, set clear expectations, recognize good work, and hold people accountable with directness and care.
Ability to build a cohesive team environment grounded in trust, psychological safety, and open communication in every direction.
Skill in delegating thoughtfully, matching responsibility to capability and readiness, and providing clear technical guidance.
Ability to lead through change and periods of transition with stability and transparent communication.
Ability to resolve conflict constructively and to address performance concerns early, directly, and with compassion.
Ability to connect the team’s work to PNWU’s mission and to the students and communities the University serves.
Commitment to continuous improvement and responsible stewardship of University resources.

To ensure full consideration submit:
A letter of introduction outlining background and qualifications for the position.
Detailed resume.
Contact information for three professional references.
The job announcement above is not the full job description but represents the job responsibilities and requirements. A full job description can be provided upon request.

PNWU offers a comprehensive benefits package to eligible employees first of the month following date of hire and competitive salary.

Benefit Package:

description_text:
Company Overview




Green Courte Residential Holdings, LLC, located in Clearwater, Florida, is a high growth real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns and operates properties across the United States which include 23 land-lease manufactured home communities with approx. 7,900 home sites, 21 senior living communities with over 3,300 senior living units, and 7 truck storage facilities.

Green Courte Residential Holdings is an exciting, fast-growing company, exploring ways to enhance our residents experience and grow our footprint across the United States. We own and operate our active adult/independent living senior housing communities under the True Connection Communities brand and our land lease communities under the Windward Communities brand. We are an affiliate company with Green Courte Partners, LLC, a private equity real estate investment firm focused on building industry-leading companies within niche real estate sectors. To learn more about our entities visit: www.trueconnectioncommunities.com [http://www.trueconnectioncommunities.com] or www.livewindward.com [http://www.livewindward.com]




Job Purpose




The Senior Accountant will own the accounting and monthly close process for an assigned portfolio of 5-8 communities and their related entities. This role requires strong understanding of accounting fundamentals and the ability to explain financial results. The successful candidate will prepare accurate financial statements, investigate unusual activity and discrepancies, reconcile accounts to supporting documentation, and resolve accounting issues proactively.

 

The Senior Accountant will interact with corporate leadership and collaborate closely with on-site community managers to provide accounting support, assist in timely completion of monthly accounting processes, and ensure that all portfolio transactions are recorded accurately and reported on a timely basis. Additionally, this position will assist in identifying areas of improvement and implementing best practices to facilitate Green Courte Residential’s ongoing expansion. 

 

Duties and Responsibilities

 * Responsible for the accurate and timely preparation of all required financial information for an assigned portfolio of communities.
 * Collaborate with community managers and accounting team members to account for day-to-day financial operations, which include:
   * Review tenant ledger activity for accuracy.
   * Review accounts payable invoice activity and related general ledger account coding.
   * Assist in the accounting and reconciliation of other property transactions and home sales activities, as needed.
 * Complete monthly financial closing processes, which include: 
   * Complete bank reconciliations.
   * Prepare monthly closing journal entries.
   * Proactively manage closing matters.
   * Prepare and review monthly financial reports.
   * Prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations.
 * Partner with the Reporting team to provide meaningful variance comments.
 * Assist Operations Team with annual budget process.
 * Participate in the external audit process, including preparation of schedules.
 * Identify and recommend process improvements and efficiencies.
 * Administering accounting procedures and monitoring internal controls.
 * Complete other ad hoc projects as assigned in a timely manner.
 * Utilize accounting IT systems such as Yardi and Rent Manager.
 * Complete special projects assigned in a timely manner.
 * Performs other duties as assigned.




Qualifications

 * Minimum of 3-5 years of accounting experience. 
 * Bachelor’s degree in accounting, business, finance, or related field. 
 * Advanced degree and/or CPA are strongly preferred but not required.
 * Real estate or manufactured housing background is a plus but not required.
 * Proficiency in Microsoft Excel required (must be able to manipulate pivot tables & utilize formulas such as xlookups, sumifs, if statements, etc.).
 * Experience with databases, power query, SQL, VBA, etc. a plus.
 * Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and demonstrate initiative.
 * Good verbal and written communication skills that enable you to work in a collaborative manner with diverse teams in a variety of different departments.
 * Ability to work on multiple assignments, prioritize tasks, and manage rapidly changing assignments in a team environment.
 * Strong work ethic and the ability to meet deadlines.
 * Persistent sense of urgency and accuracy, with a keen appreciation for detail.
 * Self-starter with a creative, enthusiastic, innovative, and collaborative outlook.
 * Aptitude for learning and utilizing various accounting systems.
 * Willing to travel 1-2 trips a year for training or to visit communities.




We offer a great opportunity to sharpen your skills, enhance your real estate knowledge, and grow in your profession. We are proud of our company culture and work hard to build a strong connection among our team members. We offer a competitive compensation package and comprehensive benefits plan including:

 * Base salary, a merit-based bonus program, annual performance increase and equity participation opportunity
 * Medical, dental, vision, life, short-term disability, long-term disability insurance
 * Matching 401(k) Plan, holidays, and paid time off

title: Payroll Specialist

description_text:
Randa Apparel & Accessories is one of the world’s leading fashion clothing and accessories companies, spanning 11 countries with a portfolio of 30 brands, including Haggar, Levi’s, Tommy Hilfiger, Calvin Klein, and Dockers, and more than 100 years of industry leadership. RAA produces exceptional products and services worldwide, delighting customers and helping business partners succeed.


POSITION OVERVIEW

The Payroll Administrator is a hands-on member of the payroll team responsible for accurate, timely, and well-controlled payroll processing across multiple legal entities and U.S. states, and Canada. The role supports hourly and salaried employees working in corporate, distribution centers, and retail environments with different pay schedules, timekeeping practices, and state or country-specific requirements. This position must provide high-quality customer service to both internal and external groups related to inquiries and resolution of payroll errors or changes.

Schedule: Hybrid (3 days in-office / 2 days remote)

What success looks like: A dependable payroll professional who can own assigned payrolls, spot exceptions before they become errors, communicate clearly with employees and partners, document processes, and grow into broader payroll responsibility and backup coverage.


ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Process assigned payrolls from start to finish in ADP Workforce Now, including reviewing time and attendance data, earnings, deductions, taxes, benefit deductions, paid time off, bonuses, commissions or incentives, and other payroll inputs.
 * Support payrolls for multiple companies, employee populations, work locations, and pay schedules, including hourly and salaried employees in corporate, distribution center, and retail operations.
 * Perform detailed pre-processing and post-processing reviews, reconcile payroll registers and funding reports, investigate unusual results, and resolve errors before payroll is finalized.
 * Process off-cycle and manual payments when required, including time-sensitive final pay, while following approval, documentation, and duplicate-payment controls.
 * Research and resolve employee payroll questions promptly, professionally, and confidentially. Explain outcomes in plain language and escalate complex matters when appropriate.
 * Apply federal, state, and local payroll requirements to day-to-day processing. Monitor issues involving state and local taxes, wage and hour rules, paid leave, garnishments, and final-pay timing, escalating questions when needed.
 * Support payroll tax account setup, notices, registrations, and agency correspondence in partnership with payroll leadership, Human Resources, and external service providers.
 * Assist with onboarding acquired businesses and employee groups, including payroll calendars, employee data validation, company and tax setup, timekeeping interfaces, parallel testing, reconciliations, and transition support.
 * Prepare recurring and ad hoc payroll reports, reconciliations, and audit support. Maintain clear evidence of review and protect confidential payroll information.
 * Document payroll procedures, calendars, controls, and backup instructions. Participate in cross-training so critical payrolls and tasks have reliable coverage.
 * Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate payroll activities while maintaining strong controls and service quality.
 * Partner effectively with Human Resources, Finance, Treasury, Operations, ADP, and other vendors.
 * Perform other payroll-related duties and special projects as assigned.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 * At least 3 years of hands-on payroll processing experience, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
 * Experience processing payroll in ADP Workforce Now or another large payroll platform. Direct ADP Workforce Now experience is strongly preferred.
 * Working knowledge of multi-state payroll requirements and experience supporting more than one company, employee group, location, or pay schedule.
 * Experience with both hourly and salaried payroll, including time and attendance data, deductions, taxes, paid time off, and payroll adjustments.
 * Strong reconciliation and problem-solving skills, with careful attention to detail and the ability to recognize results that do not look reasonable.
 * Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including sorting, filtering, lookups, pivot tables, and comparing large data sets.
 * Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a calendar-driven environment and maintain accuracy during high-volume or abbreviated payroll cycles.
 * Strong service mindset, written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and discretion with confidential information.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 * Experience supporting retail, distribution, manufacturing, consumer products, or another business with varied schedules and employee populations.
 * Experience with payroll integrations, timekeeping systems, pay-card or same-day payment processes, acquisitions, company-code changes, or payroll conversions.
 * Experience preparing payroll reconciliations, audit support, payroll tax research, or general-ledger interface review.
 * Exposure to Canadian payroll is helpful but not required.


WHAT WE OFFER

 * Competitive base salary.
 * Three weeks of paid time off within the first year of employment.
 * Company-provided life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, and paid parental leave.
 * Health, vision, and dental insurance options with low employee contributions.
 * Commuter benefit plan.
 * Optional supplemental life insurance, pet insurance, and accident and critical illness insurance offered at a group discount rate.
 * 401(k).
 * Unlimited access to our online fitness and wellness program.
 * A fast-paced workplace with opportunities to learn, contribute, and grow.

title: ACCOUNTS PAYABLE SPECIALIST
ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounts Payable Specialist is responsible for processing vendor invoices, managing payments, and maintaining accurate financial records. They also support month-end close activities and collaborate with internal teams and external vendors to ensure efficient financial operations.
ai_requirements_summary: The ideal candidate should have at least three years of experience in accounts payable or a related accounting function. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with ERP or financial management systems are preferred, along with an associate degree in a relevant field.
description_text:
Are you a detail-oriented accounting professional who takes pride in accuracy
and organization? Join our KENT WORLDWIDE™ Shared Services team as an Accounts
Payable Specialist and play a key role in ensuring the smooth operation of our
shared services accounting function. In this role, you'll be responsible for
processing vendor invoices, managing payments, supporting month-end close
activities, and maintaining accurate financial records. You'll partner with
internal teams and external vendors to ensure transactions are handled
efficiently, compliantly, and with exceptional customer service. If you thrive
in a fast-paced environment and enjoy balancing analytical work with
collaboration, we'd love to hear from you.

 * This role is designed and intended to be performed on-site in Muscatine,
   Iowa.

PRIMARY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

 *   Process vendor invoices, ensuring proper approvals, accurate account
   coding, and appropriate sales/use tax treatment.
 * Process, distribute, and reconcile vendor payments in a timely and accurate
   manner.
 * Maintain organized electronic and physical accounting records, including
   invoices and supporting documentation.
 * Prepare miscellaneous invoices, accounting documentation, journal entries,
   and account reconciliations as needed.
 * Assist with month-end close activities, financial reporting, and sales/use
   tax filings.
 * Track, distribute, and maintain capital expenditure requests and related
   documentation.
 * Respond to vendor inquiries and resolve payment or invoice discrepancies.
 * Support accounting operations through report preparation, spreadsheet
   maintenance, process improvements.
 * Performs other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION, QUALIFICATIONS, &/OR SKILLS NEEDED

 * Associate degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a
   related field preferred.
 * Minimum of three (3) years of experience in accounts payable, accounting
   support, financial administration, or a related accounting function
   preferred.
 * Experience working with ERP, accounting, or financial management systems
   preferred.
 * Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas, spreadsheets,
   and reporting functions.
 * Strong knowledge of accounts payable processes, invoice coding, and payment
   procedures.
 * Understanding of sales and use tax requirements preferred.
 * Exceptional attention to detail with a high degree of accuracy.
 * Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to
   prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
 * Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across
   departments.
 * Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 * Demonstrated professionalism, discretion, and commitment to maintaining
   confidential financial information.

The Senior Financial Analyst contributes to development, delivery and related consulting on health and welfare financial work for employer clients Midwest Series. They will leverage and analyze data in collaboration with other financial and client service team members to prepare and deliver comprehensive financial reporting and insights for clients related to their health benefit plans. The ideal candidate will demonstrate a high level of professionalism, possess the ability to work well in a fast-paced environment and the flexibility to easily adapt to changing priorities.
Essential Duties
• Financial analysis for employer group health plans including ongoing claim reporting, rate setting, contribution development and plan design modeling
• Leverage existing models to assist in analysis and illustration of client health plan financial patterns and outcomes. As needed, contribute to custom reports and analysis for specific client needs
• Evaluate benefits utilization and claims data to assist clients in developing cost management and health risk management strategies
• Proactively looking at multiple data sources for ongoing benchmarking and storytelling
• Prepare spreadsheets, graphs, charts, diagrams, and other illustrative tools for presentations and reports
• Support development of health plan reserve estimates for self-funded clients
• Participate in client meetings as needed, delivering financial information and results

• Ability to travel as needed

title: Investment Banking Vice President - Business Services
ai_core_responsibilities: The Vice President will lead deal teams in transaction execution while supporting senior bankers with client coverage and business development. They are also responsible for managing complex workstreams, mentoring junior staff, and ensuring high-quality work product.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have at least 3 years of investment banking associate experience and specific experience in the business services industry. A bachelor's degree is required, along with strong financial modeling, valuation, and leadership skills.
description_text:
SUMMARY



Title: Investment Banking Vice President

Group: Business Services

Location: Atlanta

 

WHY STEPHENS



Founded in 1933, Stephens is a privately held, family-owned financial services
firm built on long-term relationships, independent thinking and a commitment to
earning our clients’ trust. For generations, Stephens has helped clients
navigate changing markets, pursue opportunities and develop thoughtful financial
solutions that create lasting value.

 

With offices in strategic locations across the U.S. and Europe, we provide
objective advice and precise execution across the full array of investment
banking services, including M&A, public and private debt and equity capital
raising, restructurings, recapitalizations and other strategic transactions. We
bring sector-informed insight to public, private and family-owned businesses, as
well as financial sponsors, family offices and other institutional investors.

 

At Stephens, bankers build their careers in a collaborative environment that
values sound judgment, initiative, integrity and a commitment to client
outcomes. For candidates who want to be challenged, contribute to meaningful
client work and grow within a stable, relationship-driven platform, Stephens
offers a place to build a meaningful investment banking career over the long
term.

 

BUSINESS SERVICES

 

Our Business Services groups have a seasoned team of experts who bring sector
and execution expertise to middle market founder-owned and institutionally
backed businesses. Our senior bankers have strong relationships across a variety
of business services sectors, with sub-sector areas of focus including
commercial and residential services, professional services and tech-enabled
services. We have extensive experience conducting successful M&A transactions on
both the buy-side and sell-side, as well as equity and debt capital raises.

 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES



As a Vice President at Stephens, you will play a leadership role on deal teams,
overseeing transaction execution while supporting senior bankers in client
coverage, business development, and relationship maintenance. Vice Presidents
are expected to manage complex workstreams, guide Associates and Analysts,
maintain high standards for execution quality and develop the judgment, client
instincts and commercial perspective expected of future senior bankers. Key
tasks include:

 

 * Leading the execution of live engagements from initial preparation through
   transaction closing
 * Supporting senior bankers in client coverage and business development through
   idea generation, market analysis, client targeting and creation of marketing
   materials
 * Reviewing work product prepared by Associates and Analysts to ensure
   accuracy, timeliness and quality
 * Recruiting, training, and mentoring Associates and Analysts

 

QUALIFICATIONS



 * 3+ years of Investment Banking Associate experience
 * At least some experience advising companies in the Business Services industry
   required
 * Bachelor’s degree
 * Strong analytical, financial modeling and valuation skills, including the
   ability to review and guide work product prepared by Associates and Analysts
 * Demonstrated ability to manage transaction execution, prioritize competing
   workstreams and maintain high standards in a fast-paced, deadline-driven
   environment
 * Ability to support senior bankers in client coverage and business
   development, including idea generation, market analysis and the development
   of marketing strategies
 * Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills
 * High level of personal integrity, accountability and attention to detail
 * Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a
   team-oriented environment
 * Commitment to respecting and safeguarding confidential information and
   adherence to regulatory requirements

 

For benefits information, please visit:
https://www.stephens.com/careers/benefits

Financial Analyst is responsible for financial planning, analysis and projections for Capital BlueCross and its subsidiaries. description_text:
About MCE
At MCE, we tackle the climate crisis with a shared commitment to innovation, community, and equity. Together, we foster an inclusive, collaborative, and flexible work environment where creativity thrives, work-life balance is prioritized, and every voice is valued.
MCE is a not-for-profit public agency that has set the standard for clean energy in our communities since 2010. We provide more renewable power at stable rates, and deliver cutting-edge energy programs to residents and businesses across four Bay Area counties: Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, and Solano. Our team, drawn from all walks of life, embodies a shared passion for environmental stewardship and community service. You’ll work alongside dedicated professionals innovating and collaborating to make our communities more energy-efficient, resilient, and sustainable.
MCE is in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in San Rafael and Concord. Employees have the option to work remotely, in a hybrid arrangement, or in the office, depending on the role responsibilities and any in-person meeting requirements. I am happy to provide more details if needed. 
We value a range of experience. Even if you feel that you do not meet all of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Application materials will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
Summary of Role
Under the general supervision of the Manager of Finance, the Finance Manager, FP&A owns MCE’s budget development process, management reporting, and variance analysis to provide clear financial visibility across the organization. This role ensures spending and financial decisions align with Board-approved budgets, policies, thresholds, and limits.
The Finance Manager, FP&A manages MCE’s day-to-day financial planning and analysis functions, with primary responsibility for recurring budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, financial modeling, dashboards, and analytical support. This role develops and presents financial materials for the Finance Committee and other Board meetings, ensuring information is clear, accurate, and decision ready. This position also supports the Finance department’s day-to-day operations, including approving wires and coordinating with banks, vendors, and other operational partners as needed.
The Finance Manager, FP&A translates accounting results, departmental plans, and operating assumptions into budgets, forecasts, management reports, dashboards, and forward-looking analysis. This position works with Rates, Power Resources, Risk Management, MCE’s external accountancy firm, and other departments where analysis crosses functional areas. The Finance Manager, FP&A, also develops materials and works closely with leadership and department heads. This position will have supervisory responsibilities.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities (Illustrative Only)
Budgeting and Forecasting 
Manage the annual budget development process and budget amendments, including the calendar, assumptions, and departmental submissions.
Coordinate with department leaders to develop and review operating, staffing, and program budgets to ensure they are on track and identify opportunities for correction as necessary.
Model the financial impact of rate changes, program decisions, staffing changes, or other strategic initiatives.
Management Reporting and Financial Analysis
Prepare management staff reports, variance analyses, dashboards, and concise explanations of financial results for senior management and MCE’s Board.
Lead the preparation, internal review, and quality control of recurring Board and Committee financial materials, including the Treasurer's Report package, the investment report, budgetary comparison schedules, and financial results narrative.
Draft clear explanations of financial results in preparation of responses to Board and Committee questions for review.
Analyze trends in revenues, expenses, staffing, customer programs, investments, and other key financial drivers.
Develop scenario analyses to assess the impact of rate initiatives, programs, and other financial initiatives.
Model the financial statements to forecast cash flow.
Business Partnership and Process Management 
Serve as a resource to department leaders and staff during budget development, forecasting, and financial review.
Translate financial information into practical and understandable insights for non-finance audiences.
Identify opportunities to streamline recurring FP&A processes, improve reporting, and reduce manual work.
Establish and maintain clear workpapers, calendars, documentation, and back-up procedures for recurring responsibilities.
Team Leadership and Continuity
Supervise, coach, and review the work of assigned staff.
Set priorities and manage deadlines across recurring FP&A deliverables.
Escalate significant financial issues and recommendations to appropriate stakeholders.
Contribute to a collaborative Finance Department culture with clear accountability and strong service to internal partners.
Minimum Qualifications
Skills
Advanced in Microsoft Excel, with demonstrated experience using financial systems, reporting tools, dashboards, Microsoft Office Suite, Asana, Adobe software, and project management applications.
Advanced knowledge of budgets, budgeting practices, and related financial planning processes.
Confident in preparing and delivering presentations to a variety of audiences.
Advanced understanding of the Income Statement, Balance Sheet, and Statement of Cashflows.
Advanced financial modeling skills.
Education/ Experience
Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business administration, or other closely related fields.
A minimum of five (5) years of direct experience in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, or closely related field.
Experience in FP&A, budgeting, financial analysis, management reporting, or comparable finance functions. 
Experience partnering with operational departments and explaining financial information to non-finance audiences.
Experience managing complex recurring processes, leading projects, and reviewing the work of others.
Knowledge of
Financial modeling, forecasting, data analysis, and clear written communication.
Current Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) or Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) accounting frameworks.
Methods for energy and power contract invoice validation.
Ability to
Manage recurring responsibilities with minimal supervision while maintaining accuracy, timeliness, and clear communication of technical concepts to diverse audiences.
Learn new subject matter, systems, and processes quickly with limited direction while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders encountered in the performance of duties.
Language and Reasoning Skills
Exercise exceptional analytical skills, sound judgment, creative problem solving, and commercial awareness.
Analyze and interpret large amounts of information quickly and accurately and make sound policy recommendations.
Develop high-quality writing, research, and communication work products.
Deliver clear and persuasive oral communication.
Interact effectively with administrative bodies and MCE staff, Chief Executive Officer and Board of Directors.
Compensation & Benefits
Competitive compensation package offered, based on candidate experience along with generous benefits and perks, including fully paid premiums for health insurance, parental leave, dependent care subsidies, student loan repayment, and employee wellness program.
Starting range for Finance Manager, FP&A is $132,105 - $172,838.
Application Process
We value a range of experiences. Even if you feel that you do not meet all the qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Application materials will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
As a part of the application process for the Finance Manager, FP&A; all candidates must submit a resume, a cover letter as to how they think their skills are a match for this position and why they want to work at MCE and answer all the applicable questions within the application.
As we narrow to our top pool of applicants, candidates moving through the recruitment process may participate in an Initial All in One Initial Interview, Face to Face Cross team Panel Interview, Face to Face Executive Interview.
About the Finance Team
The Finance Team manages MCE’s financial planning and analysis, treasury and investment strategies, risk management, accounting, and the agency’s rate (revenue) setting process. The team is responsible for maintaining MCE’s investment grade credit ratings, building reserve levels, and managing relationships with external financial institutions.

description_text:
Job Summary:

The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented individual with a strong background in accounting, billing processes and accounts receivable management. They should be able to efficiently manage multiple accounts, resolve discrepancies and ensure timely processing of outstanding payments. This person should possess the ability to apply strong analytical, organizational, technical and problem-solving skills on a daily basis.

The Billing and A/R Specialist has moderate interaction with clients and is responsible for managing and overseeing the billing process and accounts receivable related to our clients. This role involves coordinating with internal teams and clients to ensure accurate and timely billing, collection of outstanding payments, and resolution of discrepancies. In this role you are expected to maintain up-to-date records of all transactions, track payments, and manage the payment processes to optimize cash flow for the organization. The position requires strong attention to detail, excellent communication skills, and a deep understanding of billing practices.

Key Responsibilities:

 * Accounting Functions:

 * Deposit group premiums through check and ACH methods.
 * Reconcile invoices in our policy administration system. 
 * Monitor accounts receivable. 

 * Billing Functions:

 * Maintain master billing files for Group Payroll/List Bill groups.

 * Follow up:

 * Contact agent/broker or client if a problem exists with the invoice.

 * Documentation:

 * Maintain accurate records of customer payments and transactions in the system.

 * Collaboration:

 * Provide assistance and/or information as needed from the Client Representative, Account and Sales Managers.
 * Asist company representatives in researching and gathering information for various requests. 

Qualifications:

 * Bachelor’s degree and/or equivalent previously related work experience desired. 
 * One to three years’ experience in the insurance industry.
 * Intermediate knowledge of MS Office, particularly in Excel. 
 * Ability to apply concepts of basic math principles to calculate discounts, interest, proportions, percentages, etc.
 * Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions.
 * Ability to apply rules of policy contracts to carry out instructions furnished in written or oral form. 

Skills:

 * Communication Skills: Ability to convey information clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing.
 * Accounting Knowledge: Intermediate understanding of financial transactions, invoicing, and payment processing.
 * Problem-Solving Skills: Quickly identifying issues and finding effective solutions to meet customer needs
 * Attention to Detail: Accuracy in entering and managing data efficiently, including maintaining financial records.
 * Adaptability: Flexibility to handle various situations and adjust to changing customer needs or company policies
 * Product Knowledge: A thorough understanding of the company's products or services to provide accurate information and assistance.
 * Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to resolve discrepancies between customer accounts and billing records efficiently.
 * Positive Attitude: Maintaining an upbeat demeanor to create a friendly and welcoming atmosphere for customers.
 * Time Management: Effectively managing time to handle multiple inquiries and prioritize tasks.

Work Environment / Physical Requirements:

The work environment is a standard office setting with typical office equipment. This role involves professional collaboration with colleagues and clients. Responsibilities may involve extended periods of sitting, occasional walking between departments or meeting rooms, and periodic standing, reaching, stooping, and lifting office items weighing up to 25 pounds.

description_text:
Position Overview

Peachtree Group is seeking an experienced Controller to join our SBA division.
This individual will play a key role in overseeing accounting and financial
reporting activities across the platform, including securitization activity,
secondary market loan sales, and SBA-related reporting.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on accounting professional with strong technical
accounting knowledge, excellent organizational and analytical skills, and the
ability to work collaboratively across Accounting, Servicing, and other areas of
the business. This role will also be instrumental in enhancing processes,
implementing new technology, and identifying opportunities to leverage AI within
the accounting function.

 

Key Responsibilities

 * Oversee and maintain the general ledgers and the securitization, including
   preparation and support of journal entries.
 * Prepare and review monthly balance sheet reconciliations, fluctuation
   analyses, and other financial reporting schedules.
 * Perform interest income and expense reasonableness analyses, including
   secondary market interest expense.
 * Prepare and maintain required data tapes and support financial information.
 * Manage and support BOC, OCRM, CAFR, E-Tran, and other required SBA and
   regulatory reporting.
 * Review reserve calculations and related supporting documentation.
 * Review securitization reporting for accuracy and completeness.
 * Record, review, and summarize secondary market loan sale activity.
 * Conduct technical accounting research and provide guidance on complex or
   emerging accounting matters.
 * Coordinate with external auditors and prepare requested schedules, supporting
   documentation, disclosure checklists, and other audit materials.
 * Coordinate with external valuation firms and prepare required schedules and
   supporting information.
 * Serve as a backup for key financial controls and operational functions,
   including cash management, payoff approvals, accounts payable approvals, and
   internal and external wire approvals.
 * Partner closely with the Servicing and Accounting teams to ensure accurate
   loan-level and financial reporting.
 * Coordinate with iBusiness on the rollout of the new loan ledger, including
   integrity testing, validation, and reconciliation of data.
 * Identify opportunities to leverage AI and automation to improve accounting
   processes, reporting, reconciliations, and other applicable tasks.
 * Support the implementation and utilization of new accounting systems, tools,
   and process improvements.
 * Assist with special projects and other accounting initiatives as needed.

 

Qualifications

 * Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
 * CPA required.
 * Strong accounting background with experience in financial reporting, general
   ledger accounting, reconciliations, and technical accounting research.
 * Experience working with external auditors and preparing audit schedules and
   supporting documentation.
 * Experience coordinating with external valuation firms and preparing required
   schedules preferred.
 * Basic knowledge of commercial mortgage loans, loan accounting, and SBA
   lending programs is a plus.
 * Experience with securitizations, secondary market loan sales, or financial
   services accounting is highly preferred.
 * Strong computer skills, including advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel
   (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, pivot tables, and related functions), PowerPoint, Word,
   Adobe/Nitro, and Microsoft Office.
 * Experience with accounting software, loan accounting systems, or Access-based
   systems is a plus.
 * Knowledge of AI tools and an interest in utilizing AI to improve accounting
   processes and efficiencies.
 * Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 * Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively
   across departments and with multiple supervisors and stakeholders.
 * Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively across both
   Accounting and Servicing functions.

 

Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a detail-oriented, collaborative accounting
leader who is comfortable balancing day-to-day accounting responsibilities with
higher-level technical and strategic initiatives. This individual should be
comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, taking ownership of complex
accounting matters, and continuously looking for ways to improve processes
through technology and automation.

description_text:
About Mass Audubon 

Mass Audubon is the largest nature-based conservation organization in New England. Founded in 1896 by two women who fought for the protection of birds, Mass Audubon carries on their legacy by focusing on the greatest challenges facing the environment today: the loss of biodiversity, inequitable access to nature, and climate change. With the help of our 160,000 members and supporters, we protect wildlife, conserve and restore resilient land, advocate for impactful environmental policies, offer nationally recognized education programs for adults and children, and provide endless opportunities to experience the outdoors at our wildlife sanctuaries. Explore, find inspiration, and take action at massaudubon.org [http://www.massaudubon.org/]. 




About This Position
The Staff Accountant supports the day-to-day accounting operations of Mass Audubon by ensuring financial transactions are recorded accurately and timely. This position assists with accounts payable, account reconciliations, journal entries, month-end close activities, financial reporting, audit, and compliance with organizational policies and generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).


Application Instructions
Please submit a resume and cover letter with your ADP application.

Responsibilities

General Ledger and Month-End Close

 * Prepare and enter journal entries in the financial system monthly.
 * Perform monthly reconciliations of balance sheet and income statement accounts.
 * Investigate and resolve accounting discrepancies and variances.
 * Support monthly, quarterly and annual close processes to ensure timely and accurate reporting.
 * Maintain supporting schedules and documentation for account balances.

Cash, Investments and Reconciliations

 * Record and reconcile cash receipts and deposits.
 * Prepare monthly bank reconciliations and resolve outstanding items.
 * Reconcile investment activity and prepare related journal entries.
 * Assist with accounts receivable tracking and collection efforts.

Accounts Payable and Financial Operations 

 * Serve as back up to Accounts Receivable Clerk for review and processing of invoices, expense reimbursements and other accounting transactions.
 * Ensure transactions are properly coded and supported by appropriate documentation. 
 * Assist staff with accounting questions, payment inquiries, and financial procedures. 
 * Support implementation and maintenance of accounting policies and procedures. 

Audit, Compliance and Internal Controls

 * Prepare audit schedules and supporting documentation for annual financial statement audits.
 * Assist with grant, tax and regulatory reporting requirements
 * Support maintenance and documentation of internal controls.
 * Ensure compliance with organizational policies, accounting standard and applicable regulations.

Process Improvement and Cross Functional Support

 * Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and automation within accounting processes.
 * Assist with implementation of new financial systems and process improvements.
 * Document accounting procedures and contribute to cross-training efforts.

Other

 * Support Financial Operations Manager and Senior Accountant with special projects as needed.
 * Provide excellent customer service to Mass Audubon staff, volunteers and members of the public.




Qualifications
At Mass Audubon, our highest priority is finding the best candidate for the job. Research has shown that people of color and women are less likely to apply for jobs if they don’t believe they meet every one of the qualifications described in a job description. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't believe you meet every one of our described qualifications or you have a less traditional background. We are looking for applicants with the following qualifications:

Must Haves

 * Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related field (CPA track a plus)
 * 2-4 years of accounting experience (Non-profit accounting experience a plus)
 * Solid understanding of Generally Accepted Account Principles (GAAP)
 * Experience with general ledger accounting and account reconciliations
 * Strong Microsoft Excel skills
 * Experience with accounting software and financial systems
 * Excellent attention to detail, communication and customer service skills
 * Ability to relate to a diverse group of people, exercising cultural competence and inclusion




Compensation, Benefits and Perks
This position’s pay range is $75,000 to $85,000; actual salary will reflect level of experience and qualifications relative to position requirements.

title: Compliance Analyst
ai_core_responsibilities: The Compliance Analyst will review marketing materials and customer accounts to ensure adherence to insurance and financial regulations. They will also support monitoring procedures, document audit evidence, and assist in maintaining compliance policies and training.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a bachelor's degree and at least three years of experience in compliance, risk, or a related regulatory field. Strong writing skills, organizational abilities, and experience in regulated industries like insurance or banking are required.
description_text:
About the role
Thatch is rethinking how health insurance is provided and used in the US, and compliance is core to what we do. Our compliance obligations span insurance regulation, financial services, employee benefits, and IRS requirements–often at the same time. You'll be part of the team that keeps that program running: reviewing marketing and advertising against state insurance rules and federal advertising requirements, executing our monitoring and testing procedures and documenting the results, and working second-line review of customer accounts and transaction monitoring escalations. You'll do this alongside experienced compliance and legal colleagues and, regardless of your level, will learn so much as you help build this function out. We're looking for someone with a few years of compliance or regulatory experience who is precise, organized, and genuinely interested in why a rule exists, not just whether a box got checked.
What you'll do
Review marketing copy and customer-facing materials against policy, rules, and requirements. Maintain the advertising files and approval records those rules require
Support monitoring and testing procedures: pull samples, gather evidence, document results, and track identified issues through remediation
Work second-line review of customer onboarding (KYB/C) and transaction monitoring escalations, complete enhanced due diligence (EDD) requests, document dispositions, and escalate cases that warrant review by senior team members or financial partners
Maintain compliance recordkeeping, policy and procedure documentation, and the evidence needed to support audits, examinations, and partner diligence
Partner with teams around Thatch including Marketing, Product, Operations, and Financial Partnerships to answer routine compliance questions and route the harder ones to the right person
Support employee compliance training delivery and completion tracking
Background we're looking for
Bachelor's degree with 3+ years of experience in compliance, regulatory operations, risk, audit, or a closely related function
Exposure to at least one regulated environment — insurance, banking or payments, securities, healthcare, or benefits
Strong writing skills and real precision with detail; you can document what you did clearly enough that someone else can rely on it a year later
Highly organized with a demonstrated ability to manage recurring workflows and competing deadlines without dropping threads
Curiosity about overlapping regulatory regimes and the judgment to know when to ask rather than assume
Good sense of humor… you work in compliance, so it's ok if it is a little dark
Experience we’d be particularly excited about
Experience in health insurance, financial services, or another regulated industry
Hands-on KYB/C, AML, or transaction monitoring alert review experience
Experience executing control testing or supporting an audit or regulatory examination
Comfort with modern compliance tooling and an interest in using AI to make recurring review work faster and better documented
Experience in a startup or high-growth environment where the procedure didn't exist yet or decision frameworks are evolving
What to expect
We interview rigorously based on integrity, talent, and drive; the trust we display in our teammates from day 1 is a reflection of the confidence we have in this process. We aim to evaluate the things you’ll be doing every day as best we can, and we move quickly. Here's what to expect:
30 minute video meeting to talk through your background and interest in Thatch
30 minute video meeting with the hiring manager to dive deeper into your experience and the role
30 minute video meeting to meet 2-3 members of the team
30 minute video meeting with department leadership to discuss alignment to the role and career goals
30 minute video meeting with our founders to discuss your approach to culture and our operating principles
Estimated Compensation Range
$65,000—$77,000 USD
About Thatch
We’re a fully distributed early stage company using technology to change the way America does healthcare. We’re a happy, friendly, high-velocity team. You can read more on Thatch here.

description_text:
JOB SUMMARY



Functions as the property’s strategic financial business leader. As a member of
the Executive Committee, the position champions, develops and implements
property-wide strategies that deliver products and services to meet or exceed
the needs and expectations of the brand’s target customer and property
employees. The position provides the financial expertise to enable the
successful implementation of the brand service strategy and brand initiatives
while maximizing the return on investment. In addition, creates and executes a
business plan that is aligned with the property and brand’s business strategy
and focuses on the execution of financial and accounting activities and the
delivery of desirable financial results.



CANDIDATE PROFILE



Education and Experience

• 4-year bachelor's degree in Finance and Accounting or related major; 2 years
experience in the finance and accounting or related professional area.

OR

• Master's degree in Finance and Accounting or related major; no work experience
required.



CORE WORK ACTIVITIES



Engaging in Strategic Planning and Decision Making

• Analyzes financial data and market trends.

• Analyzes information, forecasts sales against expenses and creates annual
budget plans.

• Compiles information, analyzes and monitors actual sales against projected
sales.

• Develops means to improve profit, including estimating cost and benefit,
exploring new business opportunities, etc.

• Analyzing differences between actual budget wages and forecasted wages for
more efficient budget planning.

• Identifies the underlying principles, reasons, or facts of information by
breaking down information or data into separate parts.

• Thinks creatively and practically to develop, execute and implement new
business plans

• Protects and strengthens our competitive advantage by advocating and
supporting sound business and financial decision making.

• Ensures a strong accounting and operational control environment to safeguard
assets, improve operations and profitability.

• Implements a system of appropriate controls to manage business risks.



Leading Accounting Teams

• Utilizes interpersonal and communication skills to lead, influence, and
encourage others; advocates sound financial/business decision making;
demonstrates honesty/integrity; leads by example.

• Communicates the strategic goals, the focus and the owner priorities to
subordinates in a clear and precise manner.

• Provides excellent leadership by assigning team members and other departments
managers' clear accountability backed by appropriate authority.

• Holds staff accountable for successful performance.



Developing and Maintaining Finance and Accounting Goals

• Submits reports in a timely manner, ensuring delivery deadlines.

• Ensures Profits and Losses are documented accurately.

• Achieves and exceeds goals including performance goals, budget goals, team
goals, etc.

• Ensures appropriate corrections are made to audit results if necessary.

Managing Projects and Policies

and/or accrued.

• Generates and provides accurate and timely results in the form of reports,
presentations, etc.

• Ensures compliance with standard and local operating procedures (SOPs and
LSOPs).

• Oversees internal, external and regulatory audit processes.

• Ensures compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

• Ensures that the P&L is accurate (e.g., costs are properly matched to revenue,
costs are recorded in the proper accounts).



Anticipating and Delivering on the Needs of Key Stakeholders

• Understands and meets the needs of key stakeholders (owners, corporate,
guests, etc.).

• Understands the owners' perspective and ROI expectations.

• Anticipates and addresses owner needs and involves ownership in key decisions.

• Leverages strong functional leadership and communication skills to influence
the executive team, the property's strategies and to lead own team.

• Advises the GM and executive committee on existing and evolving
operating/financial issues.

• Facilitates critique meetings to review information with management team.

• Attends owners meetings in order to provide context and explanation for
financial results.

• Attends meetings and communicates with the owners, understands the priorities
and strategic focus.

• Demonstrates a commitment to meeting the needs of all key stakeholders.

• Communicates financial concepts in a clear and persuasive manner that is easy
to understand and drives desired behaviors.



Managing and Conducting Human Resource Activities

• Ensures team members are cross-trained to support successful daily operations.

• Ensures property policies are administered fairly and consistently.

• Ensures new hires participate in the department’s orientation program.

• Ensures new hires receive the appropriate new hire training to successfully
perform their job.

• Creates appropriate development plans which develop team members based on
their individual strengths, development needs, career aspirations and abilities.
