description_text:
Company Description
At Brightspeed, we are reimagining how people live, work, play and connect by providing fast, reliable internet connections and an awesome customer experience in twenty states throughout the Midwest and South.
Backed by funds managed by Apollo Global Management, our vision is to accelerate the upgrade of copper to fiber optic technologies, bringing faster and more reliable internet service to many rural markets traditionally underserved by broadband providers, while delivering best-in-class customer experience. 
Be a part of the team that will make this vision a reality….designing and building a world class fiber network and creating a customer experience second to none.
Check us out on the web! 
Job Description
The Business Analyst, Finance & Billing serves as a critical bridge between Finance and Technology, translating business strategy into system-enabled solutions that improve financial operations, billing accuracy, and reporting. This role partners closely with Finance, IT, and cross-functional leaders to define requirements, optimize processes, and ensure technology platforms effectively support Brightspeed’s financial and customer lifecycle operations.

Key Responsibilities
Partner with Finance leaders to understand business objectives and translate them into clear, measurable business and functional requirements.
Lead the end-to-end requirements lifecycle, including stakeholder interviews, workshops, documentation, and validation across Finance, Billing, and Revenue functions.
Develop and maintain business requirements documents, process flows, and functional specifications to support IT design and development.
Ensure alignment between Finance business needs and enterprise platforms, including SAP S/4HANA, BRIM, ARIBA, RAR, billing systems, and analytics platforms.
Identify process gaps and recommend automation, system enhancements, and workflow improvements to increase efficiency, accuracy, and control.
Partner with Product Owners and Platform teams to translate requirements into user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritized backlogs in Jira or similar tools.
Participate in sprint planning, backlog grooming, testing cycles, and release readiness to ensure solutions are delivered on time and meet business expectations.
Support development and testing teams by clarifying requirements, validating solutions, and assisting with defect triage and resolution.
Serve as the primary Finance liaison for technology initiatives, ensuring transparency, alignment, and timely decision-making.
Communicate project status, risks, dependencies, and outcomes to Finance and IT stakeholders through governance forums and project updates.
Develop test scenarios and lead or support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to validate solutions before deployment.
Validate post-deployment results, ensuring adoption, performance, and business outcomes meet expectations.
Qualifications
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field required.
5–10 years of experience as a Business Analyst, Systems Analyst, or similar role in a technology-enabled business environment.
5–10 years of experience supporting financial systems, billing platforms, or enterprise technology implementations.
Experience leading business requirements, functional specifications, testing cycles, and release readiness across multiple systems.
Experience working in Agile/Scrum delivery environments.
Skills & Competencies
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex business needs into system-based solutions.
Advanced stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to work across Finance, IT, and business leadership.
Proficiency with Agile and Waterfall delivery methodologies.
Experience using tools such as Jira, Confluence, Zephyr, QTest, Smartsheet, or similar project and testing platforms.
Strong documentation, organization, and process design capabilities.
Ability to drive continuous improvement and challenge existing processes constructively.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with SAP S/4HANA, BRIM, RAR, ARIBA, billing platforms, and revenue or cash applications.
Experience with data analytics, reporting, and customer lifecycle systems (e.g., Looker, Power BI, SQL).
Experience in telecommunications, subscription-based, or high-volume billing environments.
PMP, ScrumMaster, or similar project management or Agile certification.
Physical Demands & Work Conditions
Primarily office-based or remote work environment with prolonged use of a computer and standard office equipment.
Ability to attend meetings (virtual and in-person) and work across multiple time zones as needed.
Occasional travel may be required based on project needs.

Qualifications:

 * Strong organizational, communication and decision making skills
 * Problem solver and detail oriented
 * Great verbal and written communication skills
 * Positive attitude
 * Ability to meet deadlines

description_text:
Description

GCEFCU is seeking a Senior Accountant to join our team. We are looking for a detail-oriented professional with strong accounting expertise who is committed to accuracy, collaboration, and delivering exceptional results.

This position will be located at our Pasadena branch with the schedule of M-F 8:00am-5:00pm.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities:
Prepares, reviews, and verifies journal entries and accounting classifications assigned to financial records. Prepares, examines, and analyzes accounting records, reconciliations, financial statements, and other financial reports to assess accuracy, completeness, and conformity with established accounting and reporting standards. Prepares assigned month-end, quarter-end, and year-end entries, reconciliations, schedules, and reports accurately and timely. Maintains regular contact with other departments to obtain supporting information and resolve accounting discrepancies.
Performs various accounting transactions in support of the day-to-day operations of the Accounting Department. Ensures assigned daily accounting functions are completed accurately and timely. Researches and resolves discrepancies and assists with correcting accounting transactions as necessary.
Posts and reconciles investment activity and payments and reconciles Federal Home Loan Bank accounts. Maintains investment accounting records, including investment file and yield updates, and prepares assigned month-end investment reporting. Processes and reconciles fixed assets and prepaid expenses monthly. Analyzes financial records and prepares supporting schedules related to assets, expenses, reserves, and other assigned accounts.
Reconciles officer pay and related general ledger accounts and prepares applicable tax reporting. Balances federal income tax withholding and prepares Form 945 and related year-end reporting. Performs other specialized accounting and regulatory reporting functions as assigned.
Processes and reports unclaimed property and escheat activity annually. Maintains and updates reporting procedures and requirements for applicable states and ensures required reports and remittances are completed accurately and timely.
Provides a high level of accounting support to Credit Union employees by researching transactions, resolving errors and discrepancies, and responding to accounting-related questions and inquiries. Responds professionally to member inquiries when applicable and directs members to the appropriate staff for additional assistance.
Assists in developing, documenting, maintaining, and implementing accounting policies and procedures. Identifies opportunities to improve accounting processes, internal controls, documentation, and efficiency. Ensures assigned procedures remain current and accurately reflect accounting processes.
Assists with internal and external audits, regulatory examinations, and other financial reviews by preparing schedules, gathering supporting documentation, researching questions, and responding to requests related to assigned accounting functions. Assists with implementing corrective actions related to accounting findings when applicable.
Provides training and technical guidance to accounting staff on assigned accounting functions, procedures, systems, reconciliations, and other departmental processes. Assists with cross training staff to promote adequate backup coverage and consistency within the Accounting Department. Serves as a resource to less experienced accounting staff by answering questions and assisting with the research and resolution of accounting issues. Maintains current job knowledge and serves as backup for other critical accounting functions as needed. Participates in educational opportunities and completes required training by assigned deadlines. Performs other job related duties as assigned.
Responsible for identifying reportable transactions under the Bank Secrecy Act, obtaining required information, and reporting transactions in accordance with established procedures. Complies with applicable federal and state laws and regulations and NCUA requirements.

Knowledge and Skills:
Three years to five years of similar or related experience.
(1) A two-year college degree, or (2) completion of a specialized certification or licensing, or (3) completion of specialized training courses conducted by vendors, or (4) job-specific skills acquired through an apprenticeship program.

description_text:
FINANCE MANAGER | FRIENDLY CHEVROLET, FRIDLEY, MN

Full-time | In person | $120,000-$250,000/year

Join a dealership that invests in its people and its customers. We're hiring an experienced Finance Manager to support our sales team, protect our lender relationships, and help build a brand customers trust. You'll handle 50-70 deals per month in a role with real room to grow.


HOW WE DO BUSINESS: OUR 7 BRAND PROMISES

At Friendly, our customers know exactly what to expect, and so will you. Every team member works to deliver on these promises:

 1. One low price, always. Everyone sees the same upfront price, online or on the lot, with no haggling.
 2. Relaxed, consultative shopping. We listen first, and our team is paid on customer satisfaction, not on how much someone spends.
 3. Real cash value for trades. Customers know their trade value before they shop, and we honor it even if they don't buy from us.
 4. The right vehicles at the right time. Hundreds of vehicles to choose from, priced up front and with transparent reconditioning.
 5. Financial services for today and the future. Competitive rates, and a customer's credit or choices never change the price.
 6. You can't buy the wrong vehicle from us. Our money-back guarantee and exchange policy give customers real peace of mind.
 7. Dependable service on your schedule. Extended hours, quick lube, and a customer-friendly collision center.

As Finance Manager, you're where several of these promises come to life, especially transparent pricing and financing that works for the customer's long-term budget.


WHAT WE OFFER

 * Base pay plus commission, with a highly competitive plan
 * Medical, dental, and vision insurance
 * 401(k) retirement plan
 * Flexible spending accounts for medical expenses
 * Paid time off
 * Promotion from within


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 * Present finance and insurance products to customers using a professional menu presentation
 * Build customer relationships that turn into referrals
 * Prepare and submit accurate contracts and title paperwork so deals fund quickly
 * Work with sales managers to structure deals, including desking and taking T.O.'s when needed
 * Coach and mentor finance staff to reach top-of-market PVR
 * Strengthen relationships with lenders, reduce C.I.T. errors, and keep an excellent reputation with banks and manufacturer representatives
 * Partner with service advisors when they hand off customers who have warranty questions
 * Ensure every deal complies with local and national regulations
 * Meet monthly performance objectives


WHAT YOU BRING

 * At least 3 years of dealership finance experience (required)
 * A proven track record of strong performance
 * Working knowledge of DMV requirements
 * Proficiency with RouteOne, Tekion, VinSolutions
 * Strong leadership skills, attention to detail, and a team-first attitude
 * The ability to build and maintain lasting customer relationships
 * A strong personal code of ethics, plus drive and self-motivation

 * Assist with external audits by preparing and providing AP documentation as needed.
 * Identify opportunities for process improvement and support implementation of AP best practices.

Experience and Education 

 * Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field preferred, or equivalent work experience.
 * 3+ years of experience in Accounts Payable, with a strong focus on manufacturing environments using purchase orders.
 * Demonstrated leadership skills, including training or supervising other AP team members or leading process improvements.
 * Experience using OCR/AP automation technology preferred.
 * Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 or similar ERP system preferred.
 * High attention to detail and strong organizational skills.
 * Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a customer service mindset.
 * Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

description_text:
United States Polo Association (USPA)




USPA ACCOUNTING COORDINATOR

 

Reports Directly To:      Corporate Controller

Reports Indirectly To:  Chief Financial Officer




 USPA Accounting Coordinator: 

The USPA’s Accounting Coordinator is responsible for supporting the financial accounting functions for Polo Development LLC and USPA Services department ensuring accurate and efficient financial transactions management.




The position is within the USPA Corporate Division and reports directly to the USPA Corporate Controller and indirectly to the Chief Financial Officer.




POSITION DESCRIPTION INCLUDES BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: 

Accounts Payable

 * Manage and review the setup of vendor records in Ramp, verifying banking information and all onboarding information as required prior to services being performed or payments being processed
 * Manage and process invoices, ensuring accuracy and compliance with company policies.
 * Coordinate payments to vendors ensuring appropriate documentation, approvals and GL coding are obtained.
 * Handle invoice discrepancies and promptly resolve billing issues.
 * Reconcile accounts payable transactions for accuracy and completeness.
 * Review and approve company credit card transactions and reimbursements, ensuring supporting documentation is maintained.

 

 Polo Development

 * Process stipends for PDI, NYTS travel reimbursements, TUSPA Grants, YPO Young Player Outreach, Young Industry Professional, Scholarships and other programs as needed.
 * Ensure all stipend and reimbursement requests include required supporting documentation, applicable MOUs, proper approvals, and accurate GL coding prior to payment.
 * Coordinate the purchase of trophies for Polo Clubs as needed.

 

 TSP Prize Money Invoices

The Accounting Operations Team Lead is responsible for overseeing the daily distribution and completion of balance due and refund assignments, providing training and operational support to the Accounting Operations team, and ensuring work is completed accurately and within established timelines. This position will monitor team workloads, resolve aged or complex booking issues, identify operational trends, and partner with management and other departments to improve processes and support passenger satisfaction. The Team Lead will also provide day-to-day coaching and guidance to team members while maintaining responsibility for assigned accounting operations activities.
This is a hybrid position based in our Woodland Hills, CA office. You will be required to adhere to our hybrid work policy, working from our office Monday and Thursday plus one additional weekday on a weekly basis.

Support team members by answering questions, providing guidance, and assisting with issue resolution.
Monitor workloads, aging items, and completion status to ensure assignments are completed accurately and on time.
Assist with training, onboarding, cross-training, and ongoing development of team members.
Identify operational trends, volume increases, recurring issues, and process improvement opportunities and communicate recommendations to management.
Review and resolve complex or escalated booking, balance due, refund, receivable, and payment-processing issues, identify recurring trends, and coordinate resolutions with appropriate internal teams.
Monitor and manage refund, balance due, receivable, and ARA workflows, ensuring exceptions, aged items, payment issues, and upcoming departure balances are resolved accurately and within established timelines.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

Experience with reservation, accounting, or payment processing systems preferred.

description_text:
Thanks for your interest in applying to the Bank of Utah. My name is Mark Purcell, and I work as AVP Consumer Lending Compliance. As an introduction to our company, the Bank of Utah was founded in 1952, and is one of Utah’s largest privately owned community banks. We were named S&P Global Top 20 Bank two years in a row and a Top 100 Fastest Growing Company.

Our Mission Statement:

We strive to unlock the potential of our team members, clients, and community. We act with integrity in every decision, build trust through every interaction, and exceed expectations at every opportunity. We seek to responsibly create lasting prosperity today and for generations to come.

Job Opening Details:

If our mission statement piques your interest, we encourage you to apply for the currently open position of Consumer Servicing & Credit Reporting Compliance Specialist to work Monday - Friday 8:00-5:00 PM at our Branch located in 2292 1930 N St, Lehi, UT. The Consumer Servicing & Credit Reporting Compliance Specialist serves as a technical subject matter expert (SME) within the Compliance Department, responsible for providing second-line oversight of the Bank’s consumer loan servicing and credit reporting activities. This role supports the 2nd Line of Defense by interpreting regulatory requirements, advising business units, conducting risk-based monitoring and testing, identifying control gaps, and supporting sustainable remediation. The role will also support compliance oversight of consumer credit card activities as the Bank’s program expands.

Job Qualifications:
 * Bachelor’s degree preferred
 * CRCM Certification preferred
 * 5 to 7 years of consumer lending, loan servicing, credit reporting, or compliance experience, preferably within a regulated financial institution.
 * Expert knowledge of federal and state consumer lending and servicing regulations, including Regulation Z, Regulation X, FCRA, ECOA/Regulation B, FDCPA, and applicable mortgage servicing requirements.
 * Expert knowledge of credit reporting requirements, Metro 2 reporting, furnishing accuracy, dispute processes, and charged-off account reporting.
 * Experience with compliance monitoring, testing, quality control, audit, or regulatory examination processes.
 * Strong analytical, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills with a high level of attention to detail.
 * Ability to interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical business processes and controls.

Regular Duties and Responsibilities:
 * Serve as the subject matter expert for consumer servicing and credit reporting laws and regulations, including but not limited to TILA (Reg Z), RESPA (Reg X), FCRA, ECOA (Reg B), FDCPA, Fair Lending, UDAAP, and applicable state requirements.
 * Provide day-to-day compliance advisory support to Consumer Lending, Loan Servicing, Operations, and other applicable business units.
 * Conduct risk-based compliance monitoring and testing of consumer servicing activities, including periodic statements, escrow administration, initial and annual escrow statements, ARM rate change notices, index validation, payment application, and other servicing requirements.
 * Conduct ongoing oversight and testing of consumer credit reporting processes, including furnishing accuracy, Metro 2 reporting, account status reporting, charged-off accounts, dispute handling, and correction processes.
 * Analyze servicing and credit reporting data to identify trends, exceptions, systemic issues, control weaknesses, and potential regulatory risk.
 * Partner with business leaders to develop and operationalize policies, procedures, controls, and processes that align with regulatory requirements and support sustainable compliance.
 * Collaborate across Compliance, Risk, Consumer Lending, Loan Servicing, Operations, and other business units to evaluate compliance risks, identify root causes, and drive timely and effective remediation.
 * Validate corrective actions resulting from compliance monitoring, testing, audits, complaints, regulatory examinations, and other identified issues to ensure remediation is complete and sustainable.
 * Support Regulatory Change Management by assessing the impact of new or revised laws and regulations affecting consumer servicing and credit reporting and working with business management to operationalize requirements.
 * Monitor regulatory developments and communicate applicable changes, risks, and compliance expectations to business partners and Compliance leadership.
 * Assist in the development and delivery of regulation-based and role-specific training related to consumer servicing, credit reporting, and applicable consumer lending requirements.
 * Socialize compliance policies, regulatory requirements, and best practices across applicable business units to reinforce a culture of compliance and accountability.
 * Maintain appropriate documentation and evidence supporting monitoring, testing, issue management, remediation, and regulatory examination readiness.
 * Provide targeted guidance to frontline staff and management to ensure responsibilities related to servicing and credit reporting compliance are clearly understood and appropriately executed.
 * Assist with compliance oversight and monitoring of consumer credit card activities as the Bank’s credit card program expands.
 * Support Compliance leadership with reporting, risk assessments, examination requests, and other governance activities related to consumer servicing and credit reporting.
 * Identify opportunities to improve processes, controls, data quality, and monitoring methodologies to strengthen the Bank’s overall Compliance Management System.

Benefits of Working with Us

Bank of Utah's comprehensive benefits package includes:
 * Great work-life balance, with a Monday-Friday schedule
 * Competitive pay and benefits, including medical, dental and vision plans
 * 401(k) plan and match up to 5 percent in our employee stock ownership program (eligibility requirements must be met)
 * 12 paid bank holidays + paid time off, including paid parental leave
 * Volunteer opportunities to make a difference in the communities where you work and live
 * Awards and recognition to celebrate you and your colleagues for living the bank's values


*The wage listed is within the range associated with this position. Actual compensation will be based on qualifications and experience.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION: 
Under general direction, the Budget & Finance Director serves as HCEO’s senior fiscal leader and directs the Budget & Finance function, with responsibility for its overall management, administration, and continuous improvement. The Director leads the development and administration of HCEO’s operating and capital budgets and provides financial oversight for other entities, programs, projects, or initiatives for which HCEO provides fiscal administration or financial coordination. The position oversees financial planning and analysis; revenue, expenditure, and cash-flow monitoring; financial administration of capital projects and grants; governmental and management reporting; purchasing and contract administration; audit coordination; fiscal compliance; and related financial systems, internal controls, and processes. The Director serves as a key advisor to senior leadership and operational departments on budgetary, financial, procurement, and compliance matters.
The Director is accountable for the effective management and development of assigned staff and for the quality, timeliness, continuity, and accountability of work performed by the Budget & Finance team. The position establishes priorities and performance expectations; delegates, coordinates, and reviews work; provides regular coaching, feedback, training, and cross-training; develops employee capability and continuity of critical functions; and addresses performance or conduct concerns as appropriate. The Director evaluates and improves division practices, workflows, and internal controls and is expected to lead through effective delegation and oversight while remaining directly engaged in complex fiscal matters that require director-level judgment.
 
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE POSITION:  For purposes of 42 USC 12101:
 * Manages HCEO Budget & Finance operations and personnel
 * Directly supervises assigned staff; establishes clear roles, work priorities, performance expectations, and accountability; appropriately delegates, coordinates, and reviews work while maintaining oversight for accuracy, timeliness, and service
 * Monitors workload and work quality; provides regular coaching, feedback, training, cross-training, and employee development; builds staff capability and continuity of critical functions
 * Evaluates performance and addresses performance or conduct concerns; approves or disapproves leave requests and takes or recommends other personnel actions within delegated authority
 * Participates in recruitment, selection, compensation, and employee-relations matters;
 * Develops and implements division procedures and work practices consistent with departmental policy.
 * Plans, develops, and administers annual budgets and ongoing fiscal operations for HCEO and other entities, programs, projects, or initiatives for which HCEO provides fiscal administration or financial coordination.
 * Monitors and forecasts revenues, expenditures, cash balances, encumbrances, and other financial activity.
 * Prepares or oversees monthly, quarterly, and other budget-to-actual and financial performance reporting; reviews and approves or authorizes fiscal transactions within delegated authority, including disbursements, internal transfers, journal entries, purchase orders, travel reimbursements, and related transactions.
 * Recommends, develops, implements, and periodically evaluates fiscal policies, procedures, internal controls, and workflows; and advises leadership and departments regarding budget availability, funding, fiscal requirements, and financial impacts.
 * Directs and performs financial administration and reporting for capital improvement projects, grants, and intergovernmental programs from project setup through final closeout.
 * Coordinates project legislation and financial setup; establishes and monitors project cash, appropriations, encumbrances, purchase orders, funding shares, and payment activity.
 * Reviews project payments and prepares funding summaries
 * Prepares reimbursement requests, expense billings, grant financial documentation, and project closeout materials.
 * Coordinates fiscal activities for municipal road and township funding programs, transportation improvement districts, state public works and transportation programs, and other federal, state, and local funding sources.
 * Prepares or oversees required fiscal reports and schedules, including information and schedules supporting the County’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards, grant reporting, roadway and bridge infrastructure reporting, fringe-benefit reporting, state financial reporting for related entities or programs, annual report financial data, and other required reports.
 * Administers HCEO central purchasing and competitive procurement functions for goods and services, excluding road and bridge capital improvement program construction contracts unless otherwise assigned.
 * Monitors procurement needs and contract or bid expirations; prepares or coordinates invitations to bid, specifications, contracts, and required approval documentation.
 * Coordinates required County Purchasing and Board of County Commissioners approval processes; establishes and monitors purchase orders; verifies contract pricing and billing.
 * Assists departments with procurement requirements and contract administration.
 * Coordinates agency-wide inventory control and required inventory reporting as assigned.
 * Serves as HCEO’s fiscal representative and liaison during state, county, grant, and other audits.
 * Coordinates and responds to audit requests and supporting documentation.
 * Communicates with the County Auditor, Board of County Commissioners, state transportation and public works agencies, grantors, municipalities, and other governmental or partner agencies regarding fiscal procedures and requirements.
 * Provides cash-flow and financial information.
 * Coordinates financial documentation related to claims involving HCEO vehicles, equipment, or property with Risk Management.
 * Coordinates the annual Tax Map subsidy reimbursement and review or handoff of property tax bills.
 * Consults with contracting or partner agencies regarding fiscal and budget matters.
 * Prepares ad hoc financial analyses, data sets, and management reports in response to operational, organizational, or policy needs
 * Prepares and coordinates Board of County Commissioners agenda items, resolutions, minutes, and supporting fiscal documentation and attends pre-agenda meetings as required
 * Participates in committees, interview panels, strategic initiatives, financial or enterprise resource planning system evaluation and implementation, and other cross-functional projects
 * Attends meetings, training, and professional development as required.
 * Meets all job safety requirements and applicable safety standards that pertain to essential functions.
 * Demonstrates regular and predictable attendance and may be required to work outside normal business hours during budget cycles, audits, fiscal year-end activities, emergencies, or other operational needs.
 * Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS: An example of acceptable qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in Business Administration, Public Administration, Accounting, Finance, Planning, or a closely related field and five (5) years of work experience in fiscal planning and administration, including experience with computerized financial or data systems; or any equivalent combination of education, experience, and training which provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.
 
 
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Demonstrated experience directly supervising and developing staff, including delegation, coaching, performance evaluation, cross-training, and addressing performance concerns, is preferred. Additional relevant experience in public-sector or governmental finance, particularly Ohio county or local government; budget development and monitoring; governmental accounting and financial reporting; capital-project and grant financial administration; audit coordination; public procurement and contract administration; and financial or enterprise resource planning systems is also preferred.
 
LICENSURE OR CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS: 
Must possess a valid driver's license issued by the state of residency and remain insurable under the County's vehicle insurance requirements.
 
MINIMUM ACCEPTABLE CHARACTERISTICS:  (*indicates developed after employment)
Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities
Knowledge of: County and departmental goals and objectives;* County and departmental policies and procedures;* supervisory and management principles and practices, including delegation, workload planning, performance management, coaching, employee development, cross-training, and continuity planning; employee training and development; governmental budgeting and accounting; generally accepted accounting principles and applicable governmental accounting and reporting standards; Ohio Revised Code and other requirements applicable to agency budgeting and fiscal administration; budget development, forecasting, and financial planning; revenue, expenditure, cash-flow, and variance analysis; capital-project and grant financial administration; grant compliance and reporting; public purchasing, competitive procurement, and contract administration; accounts payable and receivable processes; internal controls, segregation of duties, audit practices, and financial recordkeeping; inventory control; and financial, accounting, enterprise resource planning (ERP), procurement, reporting, and records-management systems.
Skill in: Leading and supervising staff; setting expectations and priorities; delegating and balancing workloads; reviewing work product; coaching and providing constructive feedback; evaluating performance; developing employees through training and cross-training; and addressing performance concerns; developing, administering, and monitoring complex budgets; financial analysis, forecasting, reconciliation, and reporting; reviewing fiscal transactions and supporting documentation for accuracy and compliance; developing and improving fiscal policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls; administering capital-project and grant financial activity; preparing reimbursement requests, billings, audit schedules, procurement documents, and professional financial reports; advanced use of Microsoft Excel for financial analysis, modeling, reconciliation, and reporting; proficient use of Microsoft 365 applications including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive; Adobe Acrobat Pro; financial, ERP, procurement, reporting, records-management, and data-visualization tools; organizing, validating, and presenting financial data; and presenting financial information clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to: Exercise independent judgment and discretion; lead through effective delegation, oversight, coaching, and accountability while personally performing or reviewing complex fiscal work that requires director-level judgment; establish clear expectations, monitor results, and maintain accountability for team performance; develop employee capability and continuity of critical functions; address performance or conduct concerns in a timely and appropriate manner; define complex financial or operational problems, collect and analyze data, establish facts, and draw sound conclusions; interpret and apply laws, regulations, grant requirements, contracts, policies, and accounting guidance to specific fiscal situations; translate financial information into clear analysis and practical recommendations; maintain accurate financial records and strong internal controls; identify financial, process, control, reporting, or system risks and gaps and develop or implement appropriate improvements; prioritize and manage multiple budgets, projects, grants, procurements, audits, and deadlines; communicate effectively orally and in writing with employees, leadership, elected officials, auditors, governmental agencies, vendors, contractors, grantors, and the public; handle sensitive or confidential financial and personnel information appropriately; collaborate across departments and agencies; develop and maintain effective working relationships; adapt to changes in financial systems, regulations, funding requirements, and organizational priorities; and travel to and gain access to County facilities or project locations as required.
 
EQUIPMENT OPERATED:  The following are examples only and are not intended to be all inclusive:
Desktop or laptop computer; mobile devices; calculator; printer, scanner, copier, telephone, and presentation equipment; financial, accounting, enterprise resource planning (ERP), procurement, reporting, and records-management systems; and other standard modern business office equipment.
 
INHERENTLY HAZARDOUS OR PHYSICALLY DEMANDING WORKING CONDITIONS: 
Employee primarily works in an office environment and regularly uses a computer and other office equipment. Work may require travel to County facilities, meetings, or project locations and occasional exposure to traffic, construction or maintenance activity, uneven surfaces, and weather conditions during site visits. Employee may sit or stand for extended periods and occasionally lift, carry, push, or pull office materials or equipment weighing up to 20 pounds.
Note: In accordance with the U.S. Department of Labor physical demands strength ratings, this is considered light work.
In cases of emergency, unpredictable situations, and/or department needs, may be required to lift, push, pull, and/or carry objects heavier than D.O.L. strength ratings recommend.

description_text:
JOIN OUR FINANCE TEAM

Visiting Nurse Association (VNA) is seeking a detail-oriented and dependable Accounting Specialist to support accurate, timely, and compliant accounting and payroll operations for VNA and Easterseals Nebraska (ESN). In this role, you will prepare and analyze financial information, complete general ledger activities and account reconciliations, process payroll, maintain supporting documentation, and contribute to financial, regulatory, statistical, and management reporting. The ideal candidate combines strong accounting knowledge with sound judgment, confidentiality, initiative, and a commitment to exceptional service.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 * Accounting and reporting: Prepare general ledger entries, reconcile accounts, review financial information for accuracy and reasonableness, and support financial statements, dashboards, cash-management reports, work papers, and regulatory and statistical reporting.
 * Accounts payable and receivable: Review invoices and approvals, process payments, maintain vendor records, prepare and post customer invoices, record receipts, monitor balances, reconcile accounts, and follow up on past-due amounts.
 * Payroll administration: Process payroll accurately and on schedule; review timekeeping, pay adjustments, deductions, reimbursements, taxes, benefits, and employer liabilities; and resolve discrepancies promptly.
 * Compliance and close support: Apply generally accepted accounting principles, Medicare regulations, grant requirements, and sound cost-accounting practices while assisting with month-end and year-end close, audits, payroll tax filings, and year-end reporting.
 * Collaboration and service: Coordinate payroll changes with Human Resources and department leaders, respond professionally to employee payroll questions, support Finance team workflows, and assist with training and special projects.
 * Confidentiality and problem-solving: Safeguard sensitive financial and payroll information, independently manage complex assignments, and recommend practical corrective actions when issues arise.


WHAT YOU BRING

 * Two or more years of accounting experience, including accounts payable and payroll responsibilities.
 * A bachelor’s degree in business administration with an accounting specialization is preferred; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
 * Experience with Medicare regulations, nonprofit accounting, grant accounting, payroll, or grant reporting is helpful.
 * Strong proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook; experience with ADP and NetSuite is preferred.
 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to serve internal and external customers professionally.
 * Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to prioritize work, identify inaccuracies, meet deadlines, and make sound decisions.
 * Ability to work independently, adapt to changing procedures and technology, and learn department-specific applications.


WHY JOIN VNA AND EASTERSEALS NEBRASKA?

Our agency is united by a commitment to expert guidance, compassionate care, and equitable access to services. VNA delivers expert, compassionate care to support community health and well-being, while Easterseals Nebraska provides exceptional services that help people with disabilities have equal opportunities to live, work, and play.

Our work is guided by our CARE values: Compassion, Attitude, Respect, and Excellence.


APPLY TODAY

If you are an accounting professional who values accuracy, collaboration, service, and mission-driven work, we invite you to apply for the Accounting Specialist position and help strengthen the financial foundation that supports our community services.

 Equal Opportunity Employer

VNA and Easterseals Nebraska are equal opportunity employers. Employment decisions are made without unlawful discrimination and in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and employment process.

description_text:
Company Description
Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.
The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in agroscience Contract Research Organization services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialized and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.
In over 30 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 58,000 staff across a decentralized and entrepreneurial network of 900 laboratories in over 54 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.
In 2024, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR € 6,515 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.
Job Description
Senior Financial Analyst Include but are not Limited to the Following:
The Senior Financial Analyst will assume end-to-end ownership of the organization’s financial performance, serving as a strategic partner to senior leadership. This role is responsible for analyzing key financial and operational metrics, developing scalable and dynamic financial models, and delivering actionable insights that support data-driven decision-making and long-term growth.
In addition to core FP&A responsibilities, this position will lead the design and implementation of a structured, disciplined collections process to optimize cash flow and ensure timely client payments. The ideal candidate brings a proactive, solution-oriented mindset, strong analytical rigor, and the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders to drive performance and accountability.
Financial Reporting & Analysis:
Prepare, review, and analyze monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) for accuracy and insights.
Generate regular reporting on operational and financial KPIs, highlighting trends and opportunities for improvement.
Conduct variance analysis including volume, mix, and margin trends to identify deviations from budgets and forecasts and propose corrective measures.
Support M&A activities through financial analysis, due diligence, and valuation. Lead post-acquisition financial integration, ensuring alignment of reporting structures, processes, and performance tracking.
Ensure compliance with relevant accounting standards and company policies; recommend and implement internal controls where needed.
Budgeting & Forecasting:
Lead the annual budgeting process, working with department heads to develop realistic, data-driven budgets and ensure alignment with strategic goals.
Build and maintain financial models to project cash flow, revenue, and profitability; monitor performance against these forecasts.
Develop forward-looking financial scenarios that incorporate market trends, growth assumptions, and operational drivers to support executive decision-making.
Business Partnering & Strategic Support:
Collaborate across business segments and functions to provide financial guidance on key business decisions and initiatives.
Build relationships across centralized functions and accounting to ensure accurate reporting and effective financial management.
Perform in-depth profitability and cost analyses to identify cost savings, process improvements, and investment opportunities.
Present management reporting packages to executive leadership, contributing to long-term strategic planning.
Working Capital Management:
Identify and recommend process improvements in financial operations, including billing, collections, and reporting, to improve efficiency and accuracy.
Monitor accounts receivable aging, proactively address outstanding balances and billing discrepancies, identify risks and process improvements, and report on cash flow impacts to support timely client payments and strengthen liquidity.
Partner with business and functional stakeholders to optimize procure-to-pay processes, enhance internal controls, and ensure accurate, timely execution across purchasing and payment workflows
Ad Hoc Projects & Leadership:
Lead or support high-impact financial and operational projects while proactively identifying finance capability gaps.
Contribute to the development of the finance organization, ensuring the appropriate structure, tools, and talent are in place to support business growth.
Qualifications
Basic Minimum Education Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field; MBA preferred.
Basic Minimum Work Requirements:
Minimum 8+ years of progressive experience in financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and/or accounting. Experience in a client services or laboratory environment is a plus.
Technical Skills:
Proficiency with financial modeling and analysis tools such as Excel, Google Sheets, and Power BI.
Familiarity with accounting software such as Oracle, Coupa, Great Plains, and ERP systems.
Solid understanding of GAAP and financial statement preparation.
Collections Expertise: Demonstrated ability to establish or improve a collections process, resolve overdue payments, and manage client billing cycles.
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship.
The Ideal Candidate Possesses the Following:
Analytical & Problem-Solving: Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with the ability to translate data into actionable recommendations. Entrepreneurial problem solver who finds a way to get things done.
Communication & Leadership: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial concepts to non-finance stakeholders.
Team Player: Collaborative mindset with the ability to work cross-functionally and build strong relationships at all levels of the organization.
Additional Information
This is a full-time position, working Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., with some weekend overtime required as needed. Candidates currently living within commuting distance of St. Louis, MO are encouraged to apply.
Excellent full-time benefits, including comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.
Life and disability insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid vacation and holidays

description_text:
About Benchmark Utility Services
Benchmark Utility Services is a growing construction and utility infrastructure company operating across multiple states. We move fast, build strong teams, and take care of the people who power our work — in the field and in the office. If you're the kind of person who takes pride in getting things right and keeping things running, you'll fit in well here.
The Role
We're looking for a detail-oriented Payroll Clerk to join our payroll team and play a critical role in making sure our crews get paid accurately and on time, every pay cycle. You'll work closely with our Payroll Administrator, field supervisors, and HR to verify hours, process payroll data, and maintain clean records. This isn't a background role — accurate payroll is one of the most trust-critical functions in any construction company, and you'll own a meaningful piece of it.
What You'll Do
Enter and verify payroll hours for field crews and office staff — accurately and on deadline, every time
Review and reconcile timecards, flagging and resolving discrepancies with field supervisors
Process regular, overtime, and special pay calculations in line with company policy
Maintain organized, audit-ready payroll records and documentation
Help ensure compliance with federal and state wage and hour requirements
Support certified payroll reporting where applicable
Serve as a bilingual resource for crew members with payroll questions
Collaborate with HR on new hires, terminations, and status changes affecting pay
What We're Looking For
1–3 years of experience in payroll processing, timekeeping, data entry, or similar clerical work
Experience with payroll software (ADP, Paycom, Paylocity, Sage, or similar)
Bilingual in English and Spanish — written and spoken — required
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Office Suite
A natural double-checker — you don't submit until you've verified
Cool under deadline pressure; you know how to prioritize when everything feels urgent
High level of discretion — you understand that payroll data is sensitive and treat it accordingly
Bonus Points
Experience in construction, field services, utilities, or multi-crew environments
Familiarity with prevailing wage or certified payroll requirements
FPC certification (Fundamental Payroll Certification) or working toward it
High school diploma or equivalent; associate degree or coursework in accounting/business a plus
Why Benchmark
A stable, growing company with real career growth potential
A team that values doing things the right way — no shortcuts
Supportive management that invests in the people who show up and deliver
A role where your accuracy and reliability are genuinely valued

title: Investment Strategy & Research Analyst I
ai_core_responsibilities: The analyst will conduct qualitative and quantitative due diligence on external investment managers across various alternative asset classes. They will also synthesize market and manager data to provide actionable research and recommendations for portfolio construction and allocation decisions.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates should have a bachelor's degree in a relevant field and 1-3 years of professional experience in investment research or asset management. Strong analytical, financial modeling, and communication skills are required, along with a commitment to fiduciary integrity.
description_text:
We are seeking an Investment Strategy & Research Analyst I to conduct investment
research, due diligence, and ongoing monitoring of external investment managers
across private equity, private credit, private real assets, and hedge funds.
This role will evaluate investment managers, strategies, performance, market
trends, and portfolio considerations to develop insights and recommendations
that support investment selection, portfolio construction, and allocation
decisions.

In this role you will perform both qualitative and quantitative investment
analysis, including evaluation of manager organizations, investment strategies,
track records, portfolio construction, risk factors, and relative performance.
The role will synthesize financial, market, and manager information into
investment research, analytics, and recommendations for consideration by the
Investment team.

In addition to manager research, you will conduct research on asset classes,
industries, companies, and macroeconomic trends relevant to alternative
investment strategies and portfolio positioning. This role will also contribute
to the continued development of the team's research capabilities through
improved analytical tools, data management, AI-enabled workflows, and other
technology solutions.

Key Responsibilities

 * Conduct qualitative and quantitative due diligence on external investment
   managers across private equity, private credit, private real assets, and
   hedge funds.
 * Evaluate investment strategies, organizations, performance, portfolio
   construction, risk, and competitive positioning to identify key
   considerations and opportunities.
 * Perform investment analysis including benchmarking, peer comparisons,
   performance analysis, financial modeling, and evaluation of market and
   portfolio data.
 * Develop manager research, investment summaries, and recommendations to
   support manager selection, portfolio construction, and allocation decisions.
 * Monitor approved managers and strategies, including performance,
   organizational developments, portfolio changes, and other factors impacting
   the investment thesis.
 * Research asset classes, market trends, industries, and macroeconomic
   developments and assess their implications for alternative investment
   strategies.
 * Prepare and present investment research, market insights, and strategy
   materials to the Investment team and other stakeholders.
 * Enhance research processes through improved analytics, data management, AI,
   and technology-enabled workflow solutions.

Required Qualifications

 * Bachelor’s degree required, with Business, Finance, Economics, or a related
   field preferred; relevant investment experience, demonstrated aptitude, and a
   strong commitment to learning are valued over a specific field of study.
 * 1-3 years of relevant professional experience in investment research,
   investment management, asset management, manager research, portfolio
   analysis, alternative investments, or a related investment discipline.
 * Experience conducting qualitative and quantitative investment research, due
   diligence, financial analysis, and/or performance evaluation.
 * Knowledge of capital markets and investment principles, with demonstrated
   experience analyzing complex financial and investment information.
 * Analytical, financial modeling, problem-solving, and communication skills
   with the ability to develop and clearly articulate investment conclusions.
 * Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate
   effectively with investment professionals and other stakeholders.
 * High ethical standards, sound judgment, and commitment to fiduciary
   responsibility and integrity.
 * Demonstrated ability to apply AI and technology to improve research,
   analysis, workflow efficiency, and communication.

Preferred Qualifications

 * Experience with external manager research, selection, due diligence, or
   monitoring across alternative investment strategies.
 * Experience with investment databases, financial data platforms, performance
   analytics, or portfolio analysis tools.
 * Experience developing or presenting investment research and recommendations
   to investment professionals or decision-makers.
 * Certified Financial Advisor (CFA), Chartered Alternative Investment Analyst
   (CAIA), or other relevant professional credentials, or progress toward
   completion.

Schedule & Work Hours 

 * Work Hours: 40 
 * Work Schedule: Monday - Friday 

Pay Transparency

 * The salary range for this position is $90,00-127,000 per year plus an
   opportunity to earn an annual discretionary bonus. Actual pay is based on
   various factors including but not limited to the budget, work location, and
   relevant skills and experience.
 * We offer competitive pay, comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage,
   retirement benefits, maternity/paternity leave, flexible work arrangements,
   education reimbursement, wellness programs and more. Note, Citizens’ paid
   time off policy exceeds the mandatory, paid sick or paid time-away policy of
   every local and state jurisdiction in the United States. For an overview of

coordinator for the accounting department. This role functions as the central

responsibilities include managing the timely delivery of monthly and quarterly
financial reports, administering Adobe Workfront workflows, and providing

Tax Preparer role involves preparing accurate tax returns for individuals and small businesses, providing exceptional customer service, and staying current with tax regulations and laws. The Tax Preparer will play a critical role in helping clients achieve financial success and compliance.

Customer Service:

Compliance and Accuracy:

 * Stay updated on current tax laws and regulations through ongoing education and training.

Documentation and Recordkeeping:

 * Maintain organized and accurate records of all client interactions and tax returns.
 * Ensure all required documents are filed correctly and securely.
 * Keep up to date with client files and follow up on missing information.

 

Training and Development:

 * Participate in training sessions and continuing education to maintain professional credentials.
 * Stay informed about changes in tax laws and software updates.

 

Collaboration:

 * Work closely with other tax professionals and office staff to ensure a seamless workflow.
 * Assist in mentoring and training junior staff members as needed.
 * Assist in marketing execution

 

Qualifications 

 * Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local tax laws and regulations.
 * Proficiency in tax preparation software and Microsoft Office Suite.
 * Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.
 * Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
 * Superior communication skills, both verbal and written.

Education and Experience

ai_core_responsibilities: The Investment Allocation Specialist monitors portfolio holdings and market developments to generate actionable investment insights and recommendations. They develop scalable analytical tools and dashboards to enhance portfolio oversight and support personalized investment decision-making.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or a related field, with a master's or CFA designation preferred. Applicants require 3–5+ years of experience in investment management and proficiency in Python, SQL, and advanced Excel.
description_text:
The Investment Allocation Specialist combines investment expertise, data
analytics, and technology to identify investment opportunities, generate
portfolio insights, and support personalized investment recommendations across
thousands of portfolios. The role is responsible for developing analytical
tools, dashboards, and solutions that enhance portfolio monitoring, investment
decision-making, and client engagement. Leveraging programming, data science,
and emerging AI capabilities, the Investment Allocation Specialist transforms
market, portfolio, and client data into actionable intelligence that can be
deployed at scale.
 
Why This Role Matters
The Investment Allocation Specialist serves as a key link between investment
research and commercial execution, ensuring the firm's investment views are
translated into scalable tools, insights, and recommendations across a large and
growing global investment platform. By converting complex data into solutions
that can be consistently applied across thousands of portfolios, the role helps
enhance the quality, efficiency, and reach of investment decision-making.
Working closely with investment strategists, commercial teams, technology
partners, and other internal stakeholders, this position supports client
acquisition, retention, and portfolio growth by enabling the delivery of
personalized, data-driven investment recommendations at scale.
 

What You'll Do

 * Monitor portfolio holdings, market developments, and client activity across
   portfolios to generate actionable investment insights and recommendations.
 * Identify investment opportunities and provide data-driven insights to support
   commercial teams and client engagement efforts.
 * Partner with strategists, product specialists, and other internal partners to
   develop, evaluate, and implement investment ideas and allocation strategies.
 * Develop scalable analytics and tools that translate the firm's investment
   views into personalized portfolio recommendations.
 * Lead initiatives to enhance and automate the investment recommendation
   process using data analytics, quantitative methods, and artificial
   intelligence.
 * Build dashboards, reporting solutions, and analytical frameworks that enhance
   portfolio oversight, investment decision-making, and client engagement at
   scale.
 * Serve as a liaison between investment teams and commercial stakeholders,
   translating investment views into actionable insights, tools, and client
   solutions.
 * Prepare investment presentations, reports, and analytical materials for
   commercial teams, investment committees, clients, and other stakeholders.
 * Participate in key investment governance forums, including Strategy, Model
   Portfolio, and Product Committees.
 * Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and internal
   policies and procedures. 

 

What We're Looking For

Required

 * Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or related field
   (Master’s or CFA preferred).
 * 3–5+ years of experience in investment management, asset allocation, or
   portfolio analysis.
 * Solid knowledge of portfolio construction, financial markets, risk modeling,
   and performance attribution.
 * Strong Python and SQL programming skills; VBA and advanced Excel proficiency.
 * Excellent communication and presentation skills.
 * Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced
   environment.

Preferred

 * Proficiency with Bloomberg, Morningstar, and portfolio management systems.
 * Progress toward CFA designation (Level I, II, or Candidate Status).
 * Understanding of alternative investments and multi-asset strategies.
 * Fluency in Portuguese and/or Spanish.

title: Risk Management - Wholesale Quantitative Research, Associate
locations_derived: Jersey City, New Jersey, United States
ai_core_responsibilities: Develop and enhance wholesale credit risk measurement models, including stress testing and credit loss estimation for various portfolios. Partner with cross-functional teams to translate business needs into scalable solutions and communicate model methodology to stakeholders and regulators.
ai_requirements_summary: Requires a Master's degree or higher in a quantitative discipline and at least 3 years of experience in statistical or economic modeling within financial services. Proficiency in Python, regression techniques, and machine learning is essential for building and maintaining robust risk models.
description_text:
Bring your Expertise to JPMorganChase. As part of Risk Management and
Compliance, you are at the center of keeping JPMorganChase strong and resilient.
You help the firm grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new
and emerging risks and using your expert judgement to solve real-world
challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. Our culture in
Risk Management and Compliance is all about thinking outside the box,
challenging the status quo, and striving to be best-in-class.  

As a Quantitative Researcher in Wholesale Credit Risk Modeling
team, , you will develop and enhance quantitative models that support
responsible growth and strong risk controls. You will partner with credit risk,
finance, and technology teams to translate business needs into scalable model
solutions. You will help us strengthen model methodology, documentation, and
governance for key regulatory and risk management use cases. You will present
model approaches, results, and limitations to senior stakeholders and model
governance forums.  

 

Job Responsibilities  

 * Develop wholesale credit risk measurement models for portfolios such as
   Commercial Real Estate loans and structured product vehicles  
 * Build credit loss models supporting the bank’s Current Expected Credit
   Loss estimation  
 * Develop stress testing models supporting Comprehensive Capital Analysis and
   Review processes  
 * Create scorecard and modeling approaches to measure credit risk for
   Commercial Real Estate clients  
 * Assess model performance, limitations, and use appropriateness
   to identify and monitor model risk  
 * Design efficient numerical methods to support model estimation, calibration,
   and validation  
 * Implement high-performance computing solutions to improve model runtime and
   scalability  
 * Build reusable analytics software frameworks and integrate model outputs into
   downstream systems  
 * Analyze large, real-world datasets to derive insights that improve model
   accuracy and stability  
 * Partner with credit officers, portfolio managers, finance, and technology to
   deliver business-ready solutions  
 * Communicate methodology, results, and limitations clearly to model governance
   committees and regulators  

 

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills  

 * Master’s degree or higher in a quantitative discipline (for example:
   mathematics, physics, statistics, economics, finance, or computer science)  
 * 3 years of experience developing statistical and/or economic models in a
   financial services or risk context  
 * 3 years of experience applying regression and multivariate statistical
   techniques to real-world datasets  
 * 3 years of hands-on programming experience in Python for data analysis and
   modeling (including pandas and NumPy)  
 * 2 years of experience working with machine learning techniques in model
   development or analytics workflows  
 * Demonstrated experience working with large datasets and building repeatable
   data pipelines for modeling  
 * Knowledge of core banking risks and how risk is measured and managed in a
   wholesale credit context  
 * Ability to explain complex quantitative concepts to non-technical
   stakeholders in clear, concise language  
 * Proven ability to collaborate across functions and translate business needs
   into quantitative solutions  
 * Strong attention to detail, with a disciplined approach to testing,
   documentation, and controls  
 * Ability to adapt quickly, learn new domains, and deliver in a fast-paced
   environment  

 

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills  

 * Doctorate in a quantitative discipline (for example: mathematics, physics,
   statistics, economics or finance)  
 * Experience developing wholesale credit risk models for Basel, Comprehensive
   Capital Analysis and Review, or Current Expected Credit Losses exercises  
 * Experience designing numerical algorithms (for example: optimization or
   root-finding) for model calibration  
 * Experience with Linux or Unix environments for research and production
   workflows  
 * Familiarity with cloud platforms and model lifecycle tooling (for example:
   AWS, Azure, MLflow, Kubeflow, or SageMaker)  
 * Experience using modern artificial intelligence tools to accelerate model
   development, testing, or documentation workflows  
 * Knowledge of graph or network analytics for counterparty or contagion risk
   modeling

description_text:
The Enterprise Operational Risk Management Division identifies, assesses,
measures, mitigates, monitors, and reports organizational risks through
strategic oversight of Business Unit Risk, Third-Party Risk Management, Business
Resiliency Management, and Asset Risk Assessment. These programs use data-driven
risk management and enterprise risk management tools to strengthen risk
awareness, improve consistency, and support proactive management of strategic
and operational risks.

 

The Summer Associate will support Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) activities
by assisting with program guidelines, process documentation, reporting
materials, stakeholder communications, training materials, and opportunities to
improve TPRM processes and supporting tools. Working within established program
guidelines, the Summer Associate will help promote consistent adoption of TPRM
requirements, collaborate with business units, risk owners, subject matter
experts, and other enterprise partners, and contribute insights that support
proactive operational risk management and sound decision-making across
third-party risk activities.

 

Potential projects may include:

 * Support TPRM program documentation and process improvements by summarizing
   updates, organizing materials, and identifying opportunities to improve
   clarity, consistency, and adoption.
 * Assist with project coordination by tracking action items, timelines, status
   updates, and deliverables.
 * Support the development of stakeholder communications and training materials
   that explain TPRM requirements, processes, and expectations.
 * Gain exposure to third-party risk management by supporting vendor risk
   assessments, engagement with risk management subject matter experts, and
   related process activities.
 * Compile and analyze TPRM data to inform program reporting, dashboards,
   program materials, and opportunities to improve risk management processes and
   supporting tools.

 

The Summer Associate Program is a 12-week internship program beginning in May
2027 and ending in August 2027. Students will contribute to meaningful projects
and work during their internship. To qualify for this position, applicants must
be currently pursuing a degree from an accredited college or university and have
an anticipated graduation date of December 2027 or later.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Manage multiple priorities, deliverables, and timelines effectively
 * Apply analytical, research, and problem-solving skills to support reporting,
   process improvements, and recommendations
 * Communicate effectively through written materials, presentations, and team
   discussions
 * Collaborate with team members and business partners to develop presentations,
   training content, and program materials


QUALIFICATIONS

 * Currently pursuing a degree in Operational Risk Management, Business,
   Finance, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field
 * Familiarity with risk management best practices, risk and control concepts,
   third-party risk management, or related risk disciplines
 * Familiarity with creating clear business materials, such as process maps,
   presentations, standard operating procedures, training guides, and other
   documents that explain processes or requirements
 * Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills

 * Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM ET

title: Senior Manager- Regulatory and Compliance (Alternative Assets)
locations_alt: 109 Stevenson St, San Francisco, CA 94105, USA
ai_core_responsibilities: Provide regulatory compliance support to investment adviser clients, ensuring programs meet SEC rules and federal securities laws. Lead client interactions, oversee junior staff, and conduct annual compliance reviews and testing of internal controls.
ai_requirements_summary: Requires a bachelor's degree and 6 to 8 years of relevant compliance experience within the investment sector. Candidates must possess deep knowledge of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and the Investment Company Act of 1940.
description_text:
Company Description
We’re a leading Investor Services group offering end-to-end services in administration, accounting, reporting, regulatory and compliance needs of the investment sector worldwide. We employ a global workforce of 5,800+ people across 25 jurisdictions and have assets under administration (AUA) exceeding US$750 billion. We work with 13 of the world’s top-15 private equity firms. 
Our services are underpinned by a Group-wide commitment to ESG and best-in-class technology including a global data platform and innovative proprietary tools supported by in-house experts. Above all, what makes us different is our people. Operating as trusted partners to our clients, we deliver intelligent solutions through a combination of technical expertise and strong relationships based on deep client understanding. 
We’re driven by our Group purpose, to power people and possibilities. 
Job Description
Provide regulatory compliance support to IQEQ’s investment adviser clients, ensuring their compliance programs meet SEC Rules 206(4)-7 and 38a-1, along with other applicable state and federal securities laws. Responsibilities include maintaining and updating compliance programs to reflect regulatory changes and best practices. Work directly with top private equity and hedge fund firms in the alternative asset industry, under the guidance of seasoned professionals. Key tasks involve assisting, performing, and reviewing various compliance-related activities to facilitate the firm’s service offerings.

What you’ll do
You’ll advise clients on compliance with key U.S. securities laws, including the Securities Act, Exchange Act, and Advisers Act, often independently with minimal input from senior team members.
You’ll lead and support client interactions, including calls, training sessions, and reviews of marketing materials, regulatory filings, and compliance policies to ensure adherence to applicable regulations.
You’ll oversee and mentor junior team members in executing compliance functions such as personal trading reviews, email monitoring, and surveillance of trading activities.
You’ll conduct and manage annual compliance reviews and testing systems to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls and surveillance programs.
You’ll contribute to special projects and perform other compliance-related tasks as needed, helping maintain high standards across client engagements.
What we offer
IQ-EQ offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support employees' well-being and work-life balance. 
Employees receive generous paid time off, including 4 weeks of PTO that increases over time, sick time and paid holidays, and financial wellness is supported through a 401(k) plan with a company match (subject to eligibility).
Health benefits include medical, dental, vision, mental health support and additional ancillary insurance plans. 
Additional benefits include paid parental leave and a hybrid work schedule, promoting both personal and professional fulfillment.
The salary for this position will be dependent on experience and location ($100,000-$135,000).
Qualifications
You have a bachelor’s degree and bring 6 to 8 years of relevant compliance experience from a registered investment adviser, law firm, or investment consulting firm—preferably with legal practice involving registered investment companies.
You understand the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and the Investment Company Act of 1940, and can apply this knowledge effectively in compliance roles.
You are familiar with SEC examination practices and ideally have hands-on experience with both actual and mock SEC exams.
You possess knowledge of regulatory requirements from CFTC, NFA, and FINRA, which adds value to your compliance expertise.
You’re equipped to handle complex compliance responsibilities independently, contributing to regulatory oversight and strategic guidance for clients.
Additional Information
Our commitment to you and the environment
Sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Our sustainability depends on us building and maintaining long-term relationships with all our stakeholders – including our employees, clients, and local communities – while also reducing our impact on our natural environment. 
There is always more we can, and should do, to improve – whether in relation to our people, our clients, our planet, or our governance. Our ongoing success as a business depends on our sustainability and agility in a changing and challenging global landscape. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable and diverse culture for our people, led by our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion steering committee. 
Our learning and development programmes and systems (including PowerU and MyCampus) enable us to invest in growing our employees’ careers, while our hybrid working approach supports our employees in achieving balance and flexibility while remaining connected to their colleagues. We want to empower our 5,800+ employees - from 94 nationalities, across 25 countries - to each achieve their potential. Through IQ-EQ Launchpad we support women managers launching their first fund, in an environment where only 15% of all private equity and venture capital firms are gender balanced. 
We’re committed to growing relationships with our clients and supporting them in achieving their objectives. We understand that our clients’ sustainability and success leads to our sustainability and success. We’re emotionally invested in our clients right from the beginning.
