description_text:
Job Summary

The Cost Controller is responsible for ensuring rigorous financial governance
across all phases of the project lifecycle. This role oversees supplier payment
processes, purchase order and change control, budget management, forecasting,
and cost‑to‑complete reporting. The Cost Controller partners closely with
project leadership to maintain financial discipline, support informed
decision‑making, and ensure compliance with Vertiv’s commercial and governance
standards.

Responsibilities:

Supplier Payment & Invoice Management

 * Manage end‑to‑end processing of supplier payment applications, including
   receipt, accrual tracking, certification, and invoice validation.
 * Issue acceptance certificates and coordinate purchase order receipt
   processing in Oracle.
 * Validate supplier invoices against acceptance certificates and contractual
   terms.
 * Maintain accurate registers for supplier applications, invoices, and
   accruals.
 * Identify invoices not supported by purchase orders, obtain required
   approvals, and enforce PO compliance standards.
 * Maintain and reconcile Requisitions and PO registers across the project
   lifecycle.
 * Vet supplier invoices for valid PO references and return non‑compliant
   invoices.
 * Monitor open commitments and ensure alignment with approved budgets and
   forecasts.

Budget Management, Forecasting & Variance Analysis

 * Establish and maintain project budgets within financial systems.
 * Perform ongoing budget updates reflecting approved changes and actual costs.
 * Produce monthly forecast variance analyses and Year‑To‑Date (YTD) budget
   comparisons.
 * Coordinate site and project team inputs for monthly cost‑to‑complete
   evaluations.
 * Prepare budget updates, forecasts, and financial insights for Project
   Director review.

Change Management

 * Evaluate and forecast the probability of future customer change order intake.
 * Support preparation of COR cost estimates and pricing models.
 * Communicate revenue and cost impacts of CORs for Project Operating Reviews
   (POR).
 * Define and track sunk cost elements included in COR pricing.
 * Integrate approved and forecast CORs into future budget and forecast updates.
 * Supplier Change Order Requests
 * Coordinate with Quantity Surveyors and Estimators to forecast actual and
   anticipated supplier COR costs.
 * Identify change orders required to recover scope omissions or cost overruns.
 * Incorporate supplier CORs into cost‑to‑complete forecasts.
 * Change Management & Commercial Governance
 * Maintain a comprehensive change register for all project commercial changes.
 * Coordinate evaluation, pricing, and financial impact assessments of change
   events.
 * Ensure change approvals comply with Vertiv governance requirements.
 * Update budgets, forecasts, and cost‑to‑complete metrics based on approved
   changes.
 * Support the Project Director in commercial negotiations related to change
   events.

 

Requirements:

Education

 * Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Construction Management,
   Engineering, Business, or a related discipline
 * Master’s degree or professional qualifications (MBA, MSc, etc.) preferred but
   not required

Experience

 * 7+ years of experience in cost control, project controls, commercial
   management, or project finance, ideally within: 
 * Engineering, construction, infrastructure, or industrial projects
 * Proven experience managing: 
   * Project budgets, forecasts, and cost‑to‑complete evaluations
   * Supplier payment applications, invoices, PRs and POs
   * Change orders (customer and supplier) and commercial change registers
 * Experience supporting Project Directors / Project Managers with financial
   reporting and commercial decisions

Technical Skills

 * Strong working knowledge of ERP systems (Oracle preferred) for:
 * Purchase orders, receipts, invoicing, and accruals
 * Advanced proficiency in Excel (pivot tables, lookups, variance analysis,
   forecasting models)
 * Experience preparing:
 * Monthly cost reports
 * YTD budget vs. actual analysis
 * Forecast and variance commentary
 * Familiarity with project governance, approval matrices, and financial
   controls

Commercial & Analytical Skills

 * Strong understanding of: 
   * Contractual cost control principles
   * Change management and commercial risk
   * Revenue and cost forecasting
 * Ability to assess financial impacts of scope changes and omissions 
 * High attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate financial
   registers

description_text:
POSITION SUMMARY

Provides support for Membership Accounting matters and servicing of various needs for existing members. Frequent communications with members both in-person and via email. New member account setup / billing questions and corrections, monthly billing to member statements, delinquent accounts, member cancellations and reclassifications, as well as office reception duties /clerical and phone support for Membership Department and Membership Accounting related issues. 





ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

 * Responsible for member billing of dues and initiation fees, monthly statements and posting membership payments, and member questions regarding statements.
 * Running credit reports for new membership applications.
 * Assists in creating new member files in SMS and editing member information as needed including cancellations, new credit card updates, etc.
 * Posting membership dues for all membership types. 
 * Posting referral fees for new memberships
 * Responsible for setting up and posting recurring membership charges for misc. charges, for example: Cable, Telephone lines etc.
 * Responsible for contacting delinquent members and filing a lien if necessary.
 * Assist new members with access to members portal.
 * Answer incoming calls re: membership accounting issues and handle member needs regarding billing and any membership inquiries/ refer new member inquiries to Director of PR & Membership
 * Cover basic responsibilities of membership coordinator when needed.
 * Operate key office equipment including but not limited to computer, SMS and copier.
 * Maintain complete understanding of membership categories, sales processes and new member enrollment processes. 
 * Review Member Portal to help better respond to members. 
 * Member RFID requests / tracking of supplies / replenish membership packets.




In addition to performance of the essential functions, this position may be required to perform a combination of the following supportive functions, with the percentage of time performing each function to be solely determined by the Membership Director based upon the particular requirements of the Club:

 * Assists in the preparation of monthly membership reports for Board of Governors.
 * Maintains flexibility to take on new and different tasks as directed by the Director.
 * Incorporates safe work practices in job performance.
 * Attend member functions when requested to co-host, assist members, check in members, etc.
 * Attend staff meetings.


EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s Degree (BS or BA) or equivalent; or 2 years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.





REQUIREMENTS

LANGUAGE SKILLS: 

 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills
 * Read and interpret documents in English such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedural manuals, newspapers, periodicals, journals, and manuals.

REASONING ABILITY: 

 * Apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form.

 * Read and interpret business records and statistical reports.

COMPUTER SKILLS: Must have sufficient computer/ tech skills that will allow them to be able to use, in a proficient manner, all Salamander Hospitality issued software programs implemented, including but not limited to the following:

 * Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, SMS
 * Internet browser programs

 * Ability to accurately type at a professional pace





PHYSICAL DEMANDS

 * While performing the duties this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; walk; have manual dexterity to grasp and manipulate objects reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch; talk and hear.

WORK ENVIRONMENT




 * Must be able to work effectively in a stressful environment, communicate with others, effectively deal with customers and accept constructive criticism from supervisors.

title: Senior Payroll Administrator
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Payroll Administrator manages end-to-end payroll processing for domestic, multi-state, and international employees while ensuring compliance with legal standards. They also support payroll system improvements, conduct audits, and provide guidance to the payroll team.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a minimum of 5–7 years of full-cycle payroll experience and a high school diploma or GED. Proficiency in payroll systems like JD Edwards or Oracle and a strong understanding of multi-state tax compliance are required.
description_text:
Position Summary: The Senior Payroll Administrator serves as a subject matter
expert and strategic partner working alongside the accounting department and
reporting to the Payroll Manager. This role is responsible for accurate, timely,
and compliant processing of full-cycle payroll for domestic, multi-state, and
international employees. This position requires independent judgement and
decision making, managing complex payroll transactions, maintaining payroll data
integrity, and ensuring all processes meet legal and company standards. The
Senior Payroll Administrator also supports payroll system improvements, audits,
and special projects, and provides guidance and direction to other payroll team
members. International communication may occasionally require availability
during off-hours. This position is fully on site at our Lake Oswego, OR main
office.

 

Salary Range: $90,000 - $105,000 DOE

 

Essential Responsibilities:

 * Oversee and manage end-to-end payroll process for salaried and hourly
   employees, ensuring accuracy in hours, rates, deductions, and benefits.
 * Interpret and apply wage and hour laws and internal policies to resolve
   complex payroll issues and discrepancies.
 * Advise management on payroll tax implications, compliance changes, and
   internal control improvements.
 * Validate compensation and benefit data, calculate payroll adjustments, and
   reconcile discrepancies prior to final submission.
 * Maintain and review payroll systems for both domestic and international
   employees to ensure compliance and accuracy.
 * Assist and back up the payroll tax withholdings set up and process,
   unemployment, workers’ compensation, and other statutory payments.
 * Ensure payroll practices comply with federal, state, local, and international
   wage and hour laws.
 * Assist with the coordination of quarterly and annual tax filings and assist
   with statutory reporting requirements.
 * Partner with external tax vendors and internal departments (Finance, HR, and
   IT) to ensure consistent data and efficient processing.
 * Prepare detailed ad-hoc payroll reports including summaries of earnings,
   deductions, taxes, and leave balances.
 * Maintain complete and accurate payroll records in accordance with company
   policy and legal requirements.
 * Support internal and external audits by providing documentation and
   responding to auditor inquiries.
 * Identify and recommend process improvements to enhance payroll accuracy,
   compliance, and efficiency.
 * Document and maintain payroll procedures, ensuring policies are clearly
   communicated and consistently applied across the team.
 * Provide functional guidance to payroll team members to ensure a high standard
   of accuracy and service.
 * Manage confidential information with the highest level of discretion and
   professionalism.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

Professional Experience and Education:

 * High School Diploma or GED required.
 * Associate’s degree in Accounting, HR, or related field preferred.
 * Minimum of 5–7 years of full-cycle payroll experience including multi-state
   payrolls required.
 * Experience with international payroll preferred.
 * Experience with JD Edwards or similar ERP platform preferred.
 * Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) certification preferred.

 

Position Related Skills:

 * Proficient in Microsoft Office 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams).
 * Working knowledge of payroll systems such as JD Edwards, Oracle, or ADP.
 * Strong understanding of payroll tax compliance and regulatory requirements
   across multiple jurisdictions.
 * High level of attention to detail and accuracy.
 * Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 * Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work collaboratively across
   departments.
 * Dependable, organized, and able to maintain confidentiality in handling
   sensitive data.

 

Physical and Mental Requirements:

 * Combination of sitting, standing, and walking throughout the day.
 * Frequent use of hands and fingers for computer work; occasional lifting up to
   20 lbs.
 * Requires strong focus, accuracy, and attention to detail.
 * Must be able to work independently, prioritize effectively, and meet strict
   deadlines.

Essential Responsibilities:

description_text:
The Company
Dallas-based CSW Industrials, Inc. (CSWI) is a publicly traded diversified
industrial growth company with a strategic focus on providing niche, value-added
products in the end markets we serve. The Company’s products include mechanical
products for heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration
("HVAC/R"), plumbing products, grilles, registers, and diffusers, building
safety solutions and high-performance specialty lubricants and sealants. End
markets that the Company serves include HVAC/R, architecturally specified
building products, plumbing, energy, rail, mining and general industrial. The
Company’s manufacturing operations are concentrated in the United States, Canada
and Vietnam, and the Company has distribution operations in the U.S., Australia,
Canada, and the United Kingdom.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Senior Payroll Manager, the Senior Payroll Specialist is
responsible for the accurate and timely processing of multi-state payrolls for
CSW Industrials and its operating companies. This role partners closely with
Human Resources, Finance, and business leaders to ensure payroll accuracy,
regulatory compliance, and exceptional employee experience. The ideal candidate
possesses strong UKG Pro expertise, payroll tax knowledge, and the ability to
thrive in a fast-paced environment supporting multiple business units.

Key Responsibilities

 * Process weekly, biweekly, and off-cycle payrolls utilizing UKG Pro.
 * Audit payroll transactions, earnings, deductions, taxes, and benefit changes
   to ensure accuracy and compliance.
 * Perform payroll balancing and reconciliation activities before and after each
   payroll cycle.
 * Review payroll exception reports, variance analyses, and control reports,
   investigating and resolving discrepancies.
 * Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local payroll tax regulations,
   wage and hour laws, and company policies.
 * Support quarter-end and year-end payroll activities, including W-2 processing
   and payroll tax reconciliations.
 * Process adjustments, manual checks, reversals, and retroactive pay
   corrections as needed.
 * Partner with HR and Benefits teams to validate employee data, compensation
   changes, and benefit deductions.
 * Assist with acquisitions, system implementations, payroll integrations, and
   process improvement initiatives.
 * Maintain payroll documentation, internal controls, and audit readiness
   standards.
 * Provide exceptional customer service by responding to employees, managers,
   and business partners regarding payroll inquiries.
 * Identify opportunities to streamline payroll processes and leverage UKG
   functionality to improve efficiency.

Qualifications

 * 7+ years of payroll processing experience in a multi-state environment.
 * Strong working knowledge of UKG Pro (UltiPro) payroll processing and
   reporting.
 * Knowledge of payroll tax regulations, garnishments, deductions, and wage and
   hour compliance.
 * Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data analysis and
   reconciliation functions.
 * Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
   and deadlines.
 * Excellent attention to detail, analytical thinking, and problem-solving
   abilities.
 * Effective verbal and written communication skills.
 * Experience supporting manufacturing or multi-entity organizations preferred.
 * CPP certification required.
 * Commitment to accuracy and confidentiality.
 * Strong customer-service mindset.
 * Ability to work collaboratively across departments.
 * Continuous improvement focus with a desire to enhance payroll processes and
   controls.
 * Ability to adapt in a growing, acquisition-driven organization.

title: Treasury Manager
ai_core_responsibilities: The Treasury Manager monitors company financing requirements, manages daily cash activities, and oversees corporate credit card and merchant processing programs. They also supervise the treasury team and serve as the primary point of contact for banking and lender relationships.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must possess a bachelor's degree in finance or accounting and at least five years of related experience, including two years in a treasury function. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, specifically Excel, and strong financial analysis skills are required.
description_text:
WHO WE ARE

 

 

Helena Agri-Enterprises, LLC is an innovator and service provider for
agricultural and professional markets in the United States and around the world.
We are one of America's only retailers and distributors with expertise in
formulation, research and development, precision technology, data solutions,
professional application and manufacturing. For nearly 70 years our people have
been driven to provide sustainable solutions that help feed, clothe and fuel the
world. With over 450+ locations nationwide and over 6,000 employees we rank
among the top agricultural service companies in volume and sales of agricultural
products and services.

 

 

ABOUT THE JOB

 

The Treasury Manager assists the treasurer in monitoring the company's financing
requirements, managing daily cash activities, overseeing the corporate credit
card programs, managing the company's merchant processing activities, building
and maintaining banking relationships and assisting in the forecasting and
budgeting processes. This position supervises the sr. treasury analyst, cash
management specialist, payment systems specialist, and payment systems
assistant.

 

WHAT YOUR DAY WILL LOOK LIKE

 

 * Monitors the company's borrowings, financing requirements and cash flows for
   both short-term and long-term.
 * Serves as the primary point of contact for the company's banks and lenders
   for financial information, forecasts and explanation of variances from
   forecast and budget.
 * Assists in the annual and quarterly budgeting process.
 * Assists in building and maintaining bank and service provider relationships.
 * Monitors loan covenant compliance and financial reporting to lenders.
 * Manages the company's corporate credit card programs.
 * Manages the company's merchant processing activities.
 * Develops and updates policies related to internal controls, credit card
   programs and banking activities.
 * May be required to drive company vehicle.
 * Manages other members of the team.
 * Provides excellent customer service to all internal and external customers.
 * Other work-related duties as assigned by leader.
 * Reliable and regular attendance is required.
 * Follows all company policies and procedures.

 

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

 

 * Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting or related business discipline is
   required.
 * Five years of related experience with at least two years in a treasury
   function is required.
 * Certified Treasury Professional (CTP) designation is preferred.
 * Master's degree in finance, accounting or related business discipline is
   preferred.

 

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

 

 * Demonstrated decision-making skills.
 * Advanced financial analysis skills.
 * Advanced computer skills including working knowledge of Microsoft Office and
   Excel, as well as Concur Expense, are required.
 * Travel by various means up to 15-20% of the time is required.
 * Ability to read, write and speak in English is required.
 * Communicating in Spanish is a valuable skill at Helena.
 * Valid U.S. driver's license is required and must meet all company
   requirements to operate a Helena vehicle.

 

Successful completion of a drug test and background check is required for all
positions at Helena.

 

 

BEING A LEADER AT HELENA

 

At Helena, our leaders are expected to demonstrate the same qualities that we
value in our employees -- integrity, passion and accountability. In this
leadership role, you will be responsible for overseeing other team members. This
includes carrying out leadership responsibilities such as interviewing, hiring,
training and coaching employees; planning, assigning and directing work;
appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees and addressing
complaints and resolving problems by following all of Helena's policies,
procedures and applicable laws.

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL ASPECTS OF THE JOB

 

The work environment for this position is that of a typical office environment
where the noise level is mostly quiet. This position requires you to use your
hands for many different tasks and to talk, hear, walk, stand and sit. You may
be occasionally required to lift or move up to 10 pounds.

 

BENEFITS AT HELENA

 

 * Health, Dental & Vision Insurance STARTS THE SAME DAY YOU DO!
 * Earn up to $3,000 in Reward Dollars from Helena for your Health Savings
   Account (HSA).
 * Helena's robust 401(k) Savings Plan offers you a 100% company-match up to 5%
   starting on your first day. As your years of service with Helena increase, so
   does our company-match - up to 10% based on your contribution amount.
 * Three-year vesting on company-match with 1,000 hours of service.
 * Access your earned pay between paydays through Earned Wage Access (EWA) with
   DailyPay.
 * Employees are eligible for paid time off and holiday pay.
 * Free Term Life Insurance at 1x your annual base pay - paid for by Helena at
   no cost to you.
 * Free Short & Long-Term Disability.
 * Up to four weeks of paid Parental Leave.
 * Education Assistance.
 * And much more!

 

For more detailed information about our benefits, visit
helenacareers.com/benefits.

 

STAY CONNECTED TO HELENA!

 

Follow us on social @HelenaCareers or visit us at helenacareers.com.

 

Helena supports individuals with disabilities, and reasonable accommodations may
be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential
job functions. Helena is an equal opportunity employer.

As an Accountant, you will prepare, submit, review, analyze, and report tax- and expense-related exhibits and schedules used in financial reporting, regulatory filings, budgeting, planning, and statutory reporting. You will also prepare and review monthly reports and respond to inquiries and requests from external sources.

As a Senior Accountant, you will perform the Accountant responsibilities while taking on more complex work and broader reporting support. Additional duties include preparing exhibits and schedules for quarterly and annual subsidiary financial statement filings and tax reporting, supporting Company financial statements and analytics, responding to external agencies and auditors, and assisting with employee training.




This position may offer flexibility through a telecommuting arrangement and can be performed from either the Greater Houston or Greater Binghamton area. If you reside in the Greater Houston or Greater Binghamton area, this may be an opportunity for you!




Description of Duties & Responsibilities of an Accountant or Senior Accountant: 

 * Prepare and submit various state income tax forms & filing forms for parent, subsidiary companies and nonprofit. Prepare sales tax returns, premium and municipal taxes, state tax forms and various workpapers to support federal income taxes.
 * Prepare, analyze, and review financial statements expenses, taxes, licenses and fees for budgeting, forecasting, planning, and statutory reporting.
 * Act as Third Party Administrator to prepare monthly financial reports for MetLife.
 * Create, review and approve general ledger entries and reconcile various general ledger accounts. Prepare and review bank reconciliations and assist in daily banking transactions.
 * Work with various departments on correcting accounting entries and accounting and internal audit training. Research accounting variances; assist auditors with supporting documentation, correspond with advisors and custodian representatives
 * Work with various departments on correcting accounting entries and accounting and internal audit training. Research accounting variances; assist management with supporting documentation and preparation for audits.




Additional description of Duties & Responsibilities of a Senior Accountant: 

 * Handle more complex processing issues, provide processing support and assist with training.
 * Respond to inquiries and requests from tax agencies, auditors, regulatory agencies and other external sources.
 * Prepare various statutory exhibits under the review and supervision of Management.
 * Work with Management to create dashboards and analytics in Adaptive software.




Required Skills & Experience: 

 * Minimum of 5 years of experience in Accounting is required for the Accountant position. Internship experience may be considered. 
 * Minimum of 10 years of experience in Accounting is required for the Senior Accountant position. 
 * Knowledge of GAAP accounting is required.
 * Experience with accounting software (especially QuickBooks) is preferred.
 * Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel. 
 * Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Word.
 * Excellent verbal and written communications skills. 
 * Strong analytical problem-solving skills.  
 * Ability to pay close attention to detail. 
 * Ability to prioritize and organize a heavy workload. 
 * Ability to perform work accurately and thoroughly.




Education Required: Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting is required. Accountant (CPA) Certification is preferred for the Senior Accountant position. 




Pay Range: 

Accountant: $28.42 to $35.00 hourly

Senior Accountant: $77,000 to $90,000 annually

description_text:
Are you ready to make a significant impact across the Consumer & Community
Banking finance organization? Join our Consumer & Community Banking Treasury
Analytics team and play a pivotal role in leading innovative treasury deposit
analysis! This is your chance to empower streamlined and intelligence driven
perspectives influencing Consumer & Community Banking Treasury and contributing
to high-profile decision making on both core and topical challenges. 

As a Treasury Analytics Lead within Consumer and Community Banking Treasury, you
will collaborate with partners across Treasury, Data, Deposit Analytics, and
Finance to advance interest rate risk and liquidity frameworks. You will curate
and enhance analytical and intelligence processes that support a retail deposit
portfolio exceeding $1 trillion.

 

Job Responsibilities: 

 * Lead Deposit Insights: Analyze deposit performance across key client
   segments, becoming a subject matter expert on cross-business impacts and the
   related impact on deposit liquidity helping inform strategies for our
   fortress balance sheet.
 * Drive Customer Analytics: Examine customer segmentation and trends that will
   empower a client driven approach to our portfolio analytics. Your input will
   contribute to supporting high-profile decision making both on core and
   topical challenges as well as support a transformational view of our
   portfolio characteristics. 
 * Collaborate & Connect: Build and nurture relationships across the firm,
   influencing colleagues at all levels. Serve as an internal consultant,
   tackling major business challenges and ensuring timely delivery in a dynamic,
   high-stakes environment.
 * Accelerate Intelligence: Leverage existing tools and cutting-edge
   technologies to create repeatable processes for intelligence generation,
   driving efficiency, reducing errors, and maximizing speed to actionable
   insights.
 * Master Communication: Hone your skills in delivering high-impact,
   well-structured analytics. Support the team's analytical perspectives with
   finance and non-finance audiences alike, sharing compelling messages with our
   senior leaders
 * Grow Talent: Attract, retain, and develop talented associates, fostering a
   culture of excellence and continuous professional development within the team
 * Treasury Analytics: Gain unparallel exposure to core finance and banking
   skills, including interest rate risk, capital, liquidity, transfer pricing,
   and strategic analytics, exploring a wide range of elements of our fortress
   balance sheet

 

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

 * 8+ years of full-time work experience in data analytics, ideally in financial
   services, investment banking, consulting or strategy
 * Experience with business intelligence analytic and data wrangling tools such

 * Excellent communication skills both verbal and written, with experience in
   debating complex concepts with key stakeholders and writing of impactful
   presentations

title: Group Finance Manager
ai_core_responsibilities: The Group Finance Manager will oversee end-to-end financial performance for the SME&C ABS & Security business, driving strategic decision-making and execution excellence. They will lead business case development, manage financial reporting, and ensure strict adherence to corporate risk and compliance policies.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field with significant post-graduate experience. description_text:
Overview
Seeking a Finance role that is at the forefront of looking across the Microsoft Customer and Partner Solutions (MCAPS) business? Keen on working with and learning from finance teams in the Field and at Corporate? Energized by teamwork and playing an integral role in helping leaders see beyond the numbers? If yes, come and join us! We are looking for an energetic, self-starter, and experienced person who will own end to end Small & Medium Enterprises and Channel (SME&C) ABS & Security as a Group Finance Manager. 
WW SME&C Finance team is a group of finance professionals who analyze the Microsoft business models across countries, channels, and product groups on a daily basis. Our responsibilities range from financial analysis, transformational analysis, pricing & licensing analysis, investment analysis, and competitive analysis to forecasting, planning, and whitespace identification. We help business partners make strategic decisions through educating, driving and implementing financial thinking around revenue today and business models for the future. We drive thought leadership on how to measure success for our scale business in the Corporate Managed and SMB Business space. 
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and organization on the planet to achieve more. That’s what inspires us, drives our work and pushes us to challenge the status quo every day. Through our Cloud-first strategy, we strive to deliver solutions that are optimized for the world and enable customers to drive their business more successfully. 


Responsibilities
The SME&C ABS & Security Group Finance Manager position provides a great opportunity to work with the WW MCAPS Finance Team, Area finance CSA teams, and WW SME&C Business to oversee Microsoft SMC Commercial revenue worldwide.
In this role you are accountable for:
GTM execution excellence across ABS & Security, helping translate the plan into measurable execution indicators and driving the actions that close performance gaps.
Lead business case development for new initiatives and strategic changes, partnering with EG and Core teams to drive alignment, and rapid execution.
Provide actionable insights on pricing, new SKU (GTM), and resource allocation to inform executive decisions
Own end to end CSP and Direct for ABS & Security, partnering with the channel teams to define metrics, leading indicators, and the risk and opportunity narrative carried to leadership.
Serve as the central point of contact for the SMB segment on all ABS & Security finance matters — the single front door for questions on performance, budget, targets, definitions, and data, and the person who routes and resolves them across Corporate and the field.
Foster strong cross-team collaboration across finance, sales finance, and corporate functions.
Drive standardization and simplification across the SME&C CSA community, SME&C Ops, shared resource teams, and Corporate teams (EG, MCAPS HQ, FDE), retiring duplicative reporting and raising the floor on quality.
Prioritization
Lead and influence finance transformation efforts, including systems, tools, and process improvements (e.g., financial systems implementation, BI, and Copilot-enabled finance workflows).
Guides the team on the rhythm of the business that keeps our teams aligned to one calendar, one set of definitions, and one version of the numbers across every solution area within the CSA team.
Mentor and coach peers and the finance community by setting direction, raising the analytical bar, and helping them translate data into insight and build their own bench strength.
Partnership
Provides insights into business health, industry benchmarks, and growth. Advances solutions and action plans to land accountabilities.
Parter with FP&A team to enable financial reporting, KPI frameworks, and business performance management for SME&C
Understands business results and translates into forward looking point of view to drive strategic decisions with the senior leaders.
Facilitates to resolve complex issues and offer solutions to ensure business objectives are met. Shares business expertise to help others implement and execute their goals.
Protect
Drives the right tone from executive leadership and ensures strict adherence and understanding of Microsoft policies on risk and compliance.
Influences leadership to ensure compliance is a top priority and modeled throughout the organization. Drives a compliant culture through actions and decisions to instill trust; advocates, educates and promotes best practices and new developments.
Directs team and holds others accountable to ensure financial control processes, policies, instruments, and procedures are executed.
Guides team and encourage others to identify and share risks to compliance and take steps to mitigate.
Other
Embody Microsoft’s culture and values 


Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Master's Degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Data Science or related field AND 4+ years experience in financial analysis, accounting, controllership or finance, or related field OR Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Data Science or related field AND 6+ years experience in financial analysis, accounting, controllership or finance, or related field OR equivalent experience.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Master's Degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Data Science or related field AND 8+ years of post-graduate financial analysis, accounting, controllership, or finance work experience OR Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Data Science or related field AND 12+ years of post-graduate financial analysis, accounting, controllership, or finance work experience OR equivalent experience.
3+ years experience in multinationals with multi-product/multi-segment finance roles.
3+ years work experience in matrix-based organization.
3+ years work experience in the technology or software industry.

There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $148,400 - $222,600 per year.

title: Sr Billing Specialist
ai_core_responsibilities: The Billing Specialist is responsible for auditing vessel logs and operational data to generate accurate invoices while reconciling labor and equipment charges against commercial contracts. They also provide support to finance leadership through revenue forecasting, accruals, and the resolution of billing discrepancies.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must possess an associate degree in Accounting, Finance, or Logistics, with a strong preference for experience in the maritime or freight forwarding industry. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with ERP or Terminal Operating Systems are essential for success in this role.
description_text:
We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Billing Specialist to join our
marine accounting team. As a Billing Specialist, you will play a critical role
in the revenue cycle of our port operations. You will be responsible for
reviewing daily vessel operational reports, calculating complex labor and
equipment charges, auditing stevedoring
contracts, and generating accurate, timely invoices for shipping lines and cargo
owners. The ideal candidate possesses strong numerical acumen, experience in
maritime/logistics billing, and the ability to reconcile operational data with
commercial agreements. This highly visible position supports the Controller,
accounting staff, and key operational leaders of various business units. The
position requires the ability and drive to provide high quality, accurate, work
products within tight timeframes. The ideal candidate will appreciate working in
a small office environment and should be a flexible team-player with a desire to
thoroughly engage and grow with the business.

Essential Duties:

 * Invoice Preparation: Audit vessel logs, timesheets, and terminal operating
   data to generate
   detailed, accurate invoices.
 * Contract Application: Review customer contracts, rate sheets, and port
   tariffs to ensure correct
   application of commodity rates, detention/demurrage, equipment usage, and
   ancillary service
   charges. Update contracts, as needed.
 * Labor Reconciliation: Verify labor hours, shift differentials, overtime, and
   stand-by time against
   operational logs.
 * Customer Service: Partner closely with vessel operations managers and client
   representatives to
   promptly resolve billing disputes and discrepancies and provide excellent
   customer service, as
   needed.
 * Reporting & Analysis: Conduct monthly reconciliations, and assist finance
   leadership with accruals,
   revenue forecasting, and job-costing variance analysis.
 * Research and resolve billing or accounting related problems and
   discrepancies.

Working Conditions:
    In-person, small office environment, M-F 8-5


Minimum Requirements:

 * Associates degree in Accounting, Finance, Logistics, or equivalent work
   experience

Preferred Qualifications:

 * 1+ years of experience in billing, financial analysis, or cost accounting
   within the maritime,
   stevedoring, freight forwarding, or logistics industry (strongly preferred).
 * Technical Proficiency: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (VLOOKUP,
   Pivot Tables, SUMIFS).
 * Experience with Terminal Operating Systems (TOS) and ERP/accounting systems
   (e.g., Oracle
   High attention to detail and ability to work with large datasets.
 * Understanding of maritime terminology, demurrage, laytime, and cargo handling
   operations.
   Excellent communication skills to interact professionally with operations
   teams, port authorities, and global
   shipping agents.
 * Ability to work accurately under very tight timeframes
 * Strong analytical skills to identify and resolve discrepancies
 * Excellent interpersonal skills to properly interact with supporting staff and
   leadership
 * Navigates effectively in a changing environment where competing priorities
   require flexibility and agility

NOTE:

Compensation & Benefits:  Actual compensation will be determined based on
factors such as experience, qualifications, skills, and geographic location.
Eligible employees may receive a comprehensive benefits package, including
medical, dental and vision coverage, retirement benefits, paid time off, paid
holidays, and other company-sponsored benefits. Additional incentive
compensation may be available based on the position. 

This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform
other related duties as needed to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

Ports America is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will
receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion,
national origin, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity
or expression, age, disability, genetic information, citizenship status,
military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable
federal, state, or local law.

Work Authorization: This position does not offer employment-based immigration
sponsorship. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States
without current or future sponsorship.

Applicant Privacy: For additional information regarding how Ports America
collects, uses, and protects applicant information, please review our Applicant
Privacy Notice
[https://artifacts.portsamerica.com/pdf/Applicant%20Privacy%20Notice.pdf].
Questions regarding the handling or protection of applicant data may be directed
to human.resources@portsamerica.com [human.resources@portsamerica.com].

description_text:
Hexagon Agility is the leading global provider of clean fuel solutions for commercial vehicles and gas transportation solutions with more than $400 million in revenues. Our product offerings include (renewable) natural gas distribution systems, Type 4 composite natural gas cylinders and (renewable) natural gas fuel systems. These products transport clean gaseous fuels and enable vehicles to reduce emissions while saving operating costs. Join us in driving energy transformation. To learn more, visit our website at hexagonagility.com.

We are currently seeking an Accounting Manager that will report to the Director of Accounting. This position will be based out of our Salisbury, NC locations. Candidates should expect a fast-paced, growth environment and have experience with multi-site operations. We are making significant investments to transform ourselves into more of a data-driven company and this position will play a key supporting role in enhancing financial performance management.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

 * Manage month-end closing for sites and prepare weekly/monthly financial statements and other operation reports.
 * Support site leadership and cross-functional management teams with problem solving, analysis and commentary of drivers behind issues and variances to budget and forecasts.
 * Review weekly/monthly KPI data with site teams to understand trends and help analyze root causes.
 * Support the cost accounting functions as it pertains to inventory, costing, and ERP maintenance of the FleetCare locations
 * Collaborate with local accounting teams and centralized AR/AP team supporting multi-location activities
 * Assist with preparation and inputs to annual budget and periodic financial forecasts.
 * Proactively identifies and implements policy, process, and system improvements to increase overall efficiency and accuracy while maintaining expected results.
 * Assist with preparation of the yearly audits and physical inventory counts
 * Perform all other duties as assigned

Qualifications

 * Bachelor’s degree in Accounting.
 * At least 5 years of relevant experience working in a manufacturing environment and leading a team.
 * Experienced user of larger ERP systems and financial reporting platforms.
 * Strong business acumen and communications.
 * Strong project management skills.
 * Power user of Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Power BI or similar.

Professional Skills Qualifications

 * Must be able to work across organization boundaries at all levels of the company to achieve site and corporate objectives.
 * Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and follow through to resolve outstanding issues.
 * Solid knowledge of US GAAP.
 * Thorough understanding of Cost Accounting.
 * Strong time management skills with the ability to handle multiple jobs and adapt to a rapidly changing work environment with fluctuating priorities and tight deadlines.
 * Highly self-motivated with ability to bring a high-level of energy to work.
 * Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
 * Ability to analyze/interpret data and take appropriate action. 

Work Environment

This job operates in a professional office environment at a plant location. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, etc.

title: Senior Accountant
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Accountant manages key accounting activities including reconciliations, journal entries, and general ledger responsibilities while ensuring financial accuracy. They also partner with the Finance team to support month-end/year-end close processes and drive process improvements.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a bachelor's degree in accounting or finance and 3-6 years of progressive accounting experience. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with ERP or financial reporting systems are required.
description_text:
SENIOR ACCOUNTANT


ENSURE ACCURACY. SOLVE PROBLEMS. DRIVE RESULTS.

 

As our Senior Accountant, you will play a key role in maintaining the accuracy
and integrity of Stinker’s financial information while helping strengthen the
processes behind it. This experienced accounting position independently manages
key accounting activities, including account reconciliations, journal entries,
accounts receivable, electronic payment activity, accruals, allocations, and
other general ledger responsibilities.

 

This role goes beyond completing assigned accounting tasks. The Senior
Accountant is expected to take ownership of issues, critically evaluate
problems, develop practical solutions, and help drive matters through to
resolution. You will work closely with the Corporate Controller and Finance Team
to support month-end and year-end close, maintain strong accounting controls,
research and resolve financial discrepancies, and identify and implement
opportunities to make our accounting processes more accurate, efficient, and
scalable.

 

As a senior member of the accounting team, you will also serve as a resource to
others by sharing knowledge, providing guidance, helping solve complex
accounting issues, and promoting consistent and effective accounting practices
across the department.

We value collaboration, innovation, accountability, and people who continuously
look for better ways to serve our employees, guests, and communities. If you
enjoy taking ownership, solving problems, improving processes, and turning ideas
into results, we'd love to meet you.

 

What You Will Do

 * Prepare monthly and quarterly balance sheet reconciliations, research
   discrepancies, identify root causes, and drive outstanding items through
   timely resolution.
 * Support month-end and year-end close processes by completing assigned
   accounting activities accurately and within established deadlines, while
   proactively identifying issues that could impact the close or financial
   results.
 * Submit and reconcile fuel vouchers and other amounts due from outside
   agencies.
 * Take ownership of accounting issues and projects, determine appropriate next
   steps, engage the right stakeholders, and help drive matters through to
   conclusion.
 * Research financial activity, identify trends, discrepancies, or issues,
   critically evaluate available information, and develop practical solutions
   and recommendations.
 * Maintain appropriate documentation and accounting controls to support
   accurate financial reporting and audit readiness.
 * Proactively identify and implement opportunities to simplify and streamline
   accounting processes, strengthen controls, improve accuracy, reduce manual
   work, and increase efficiency.
 * Challenge existing processes when appropriate and help develop better, more
   scalable ways of accomplishing accounting and finance objectives.
 * Serve as an accounting resource to team members by sharing knowledge,
   providing guidance, and supporting consistent accounting practices.
 * Help lead accounting initiatives and cross-functional projects by organizing
   issues, following up on outstanding items, removing obstacles, and
   maintaining momentum toward completion.
 * Partner with Finance and other departments to resolve accounting questions,
   develop solutions, and communicate financial information clearly.

 

You'll Thrive Here If You...

 * Bring strong accounting knowledge and take ownership of accurate, reliable
   work.
 * Are naturally proactive and look for what needs to be done rather than
   waiting to be told what to do.
 * Take ownership of problems and follow them through to resolution, even when
   the solution is not immediately obvious.
 * Think critically, ask good questions, evaluate alternatives, and use sound
   judgment to recommend solutions.
 * Work independently while recognizing when collaboration or escalation is
   appropriate.
 * Look beyond the immediate task to understand root causes and identify
   opportunities to make processes better.
 * Stay organized and manage multiple priorities, projects, and deadlines with
   strong attention to detail.
 * Are comfortable helping lead initiatives, coordinating with others, and
   keeping work moving toward completion.
 * Adapt to changing priorities, systems, and processes and help others navigate
   change effectively.
 * Build collaborative relationships and communicate effectively with both
   financial and non-financial audiences.
 * Demonstrate integrity and discretion when handling confidential financial
   information.

 

About Stinker

Founded in 1936, Stinker is a family-owned convenience retailer serving
communities throughout Idaho, Colorado, and Wyoming.

We got our name in a fight. In 1936, a 20-year-old named Farris Lind opened a
service station in Twin Falls and started selling gasoline for less than the
major oil companies thought he should. They didn’t take it well. When one of
them told a newspaper that Farris Lind was a real stinker, he took it as a
compliment, put the word on his stations, and drew a skunk wearing red boxing
gloves (Polecat Pete).

So, the gloves came first, and they were never a joke. Fearless Farris put them
on because he spent his career punching above his weight on behalf of the
customer, and because a small Idaho company that refuses to be pushed around
must be willing to fight for what it believes in. Ninety years later, that’s
still the job. We fight for our employees. We fight for our guests. That’s what
sets us apart, and it’s what we look for in the people we hire.

Our purpose is simple:

To make our world a better place by being a bright spot in the lives we touch,
one employee, one guest, and one community at a time.

We believe our success starts with our people. That means developing others,
building trust, welcoming new ideas, recognizing contributions, holding
ourselves accountable, and having the courage to do what’s right.

We still know how to have fun; our mascot is a skunk, after all. But take a
close look at Pete: he’s got his gloves on.

Required Qualifications

 * Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or a related field, or an
   equivalent combination of education and relevant accounting experience.
 * 3–6 years of progressive accounting experience, including experience
   independently managing general ledger and account reconciliation
   responsibilities.
 * Strong knowledge of generally accepted accounting principles, general ledger
   accounting, journal entries, account reconciliations, accruals, and financial
   reporting.
 * Experience supporting month-end and year-end close processes.
 * Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to research
   accounting issues, identify root causes, evaluate alternatives, and develop
   appropriate solutions.
 * Demonstrated ability to independently take ownership of problems, projects,
   or accounting matters and drive them through to resolution.
 * Demonstrated ability to identify and implement process improvements that
   increase efficiency, accuracy, or control.
 * Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including working with formulas and
   large data sets.
 * Experience working with accounting, ERP, or financial reporting systems.
 * Ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and deadlines while
   maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
 * Ability to communicate financial information clearly to financial and
   non-financial audiences.
 * Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise critical thinking and
   sound judgment, and maintain confidentiality.
 * Successfully pass a background check.
 * Work in a professional office environment, including extended periods at a
   computer.

 

 

Preferred Qualifications

 * Experience supporting retail, convenience, fuel, or other multi-location
   operations.
 * Experience working with multiple legal entities or lines of business.
 * Public accounting experience.
 * Experience identifying and implementing accounting process improvements or
   automation.
 * Experience leading projects or initiatives involving multiple departments or
   stakeholders.
 * Experience mentoring, training, or serving as a resource to other accounting
   team members.
 * PDI or other comparable financial systems experience.

 

Ready to Lead with Us?

If you're looking for an opportunity to lead an important financial function,
develop people, strengthen controls, improve processes, and help build an
efficient and scalable accounts payable operation, we'd love to hear from you.

We Offer

 * Competitive pay with annual merit increases.
 * Paid Time Off that increases with tenure.
 * Eight (8) paid holidays.
 * Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage.
 * HSA and FSA options, including a company contribution to eligible HSAs.
 * Optional accident and/or life insurance coverage.
 * Free virtual healthcare for employees enrolled in a Stinker medical plan.
 * 401(k) and Roth 401(k) options with a discretionary company match of 25% on
   the first 10% of wages contributed.
 * DailyPay, providing access to eligible earned wages before your regular
   payday.
 * Employee Assistance Program.
 * Employee discounts on fuel, merchandise, food, and more.
 * Employee referral bonuses.
 * Professional development and opportunities for career growth.

 

Location: Boise, Idaho

Schedule: Full-time; office based.

Hours: 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Monday-Friday

Work Environment: Work is performed in a temperature-controlled office
environment and may require extended periods working at a desk or computer.
Stinker’s corporate office is dog friendly.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you enjoy turning financial details into accurate results, solving complex
accounting challenges, and strengthening processes that help the business

description_text:
The Sponsor Project Accountant is responsible for ensuring all expenditures
charged to grants and contracts comply with the Government and institutional
policies, regulations and the terms and conditions of the award. The accountant
must ensure the expenses are allowable, reasonable, allocable to the project and
properly approved according to the Sponsor’s and School’s policies and
procedures. 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Review grants and contracts portfolio.
 * Review and approve all transactions for each grant/contract according to the
   Sponsor's and School's policies and procedures.
 * Compare salary/effort charged to grants/contracts to approved award budget.
 * Ensure cost allocations between grants for closely related work are allocated
   based on a reasonable and approved methodology.
 * Collect, and analyze data relating to grants and contracts to detect
   non-compliance with laws, regulations, and management policies.
 * Inspect account books for accuracy and use of accepted accounting procedures
   to record expenditures.
 * Examine and evaluate financial data to ensure data integrity.
 * Inspect cash on hand for grant accounts, and Sponsor’s payment schedule to
   confirm records are accurate. Follow up on outstanding receivables.
 * Prepare, examine, or analyze accounting records, financial transactions and
   reports to assess accuracy, completeness, and conformance to award terms and
   conditions and Sponsor’s reporting standards.
 * Review accounts for discrepancies and reconcile differences.
 * Prepare adjusting journal entries.
 * Analyze grant budget, costs, revenues, financial commitments, and obligations
   to project the correct status of grant accounts.
 * Report to management, department administrators, and the principal
   investigators regarding the finances of the grant.
 * Analyze grant budget and expenditures, and prepare reports that compare
   budgeted costs to actual costs.
 * Analyze and prepare annual and other required financial reports, variance
   analysis and other records, using accepted accounting methods to meet
   reporting deadlines and facilitate financial planning.
 * Other special projects/responsibilities assigned as needed.


QUALIFICATIONS

 * Bachelor's degree in Accounting.
 * 0 -1 year experience in accounting. Auditing experience desired.

description_text:
Mercury is building radically different banking and offering a complete finance stack for startups and business owners. We work hard to create the easiest and safest banking* experience possible to simplify entrepreneurs’ and business owners’ financial lives. At Mercury, compliance is a strategic function. We have a modern approach where teams move fast and compliance provides the frameworks, systems, and regulatory expertise that make that speed sustainable while protecting our customers and earning their trust.
We're hiring a Senior Manager, Compliance Governance to lead the core programs of Mercury's Compliance Management System: compliance risk assessment, enterprise policy governance, enterprise compliance training, and compliance reporting, along with oversight of compliance issues. This leader will mature these programs to meet the expectations of a regulated bank and lead them through regulatory examinations. Mercury has obtained a provisional national bank charter and is currently building towards final approval.
This role is well-suited for someone who knows what regulators expect from a CMS and can adapt established frameworks to how Mercury actually operates. The individual will lead a team of compliance professionals, be a key leader within Mercury's Compliance team, and operate in a highly collaborative environment. The role involves especially close coordination across the Compliance function, with partnership with Enterprise Risk, Legal, Internal Audit, executive leadership, and our banking* partners.

Lead and develop the Compliance Governance team: set priorities, hold a high bar, and develop your team’s capabilities.
Own the compliance risk assessment, including methodology, execution, and alignment with Mercury's enterprise risk framework.
Own enterprise policy governance: the policy lifecycle, standards, and ownership across Mercury.
Own enterprise compliance training: a risk-based curriculum that measures whether training works, not just whether people completed it.
Oversee compliance issues within Mercury's enterprise issues management program, partnering with Enterprise Risk Management on identification, remediation, and validation.
Design and deliver compliance reporting to executive leadership and governance committees, with metrics that show whether programs are working.
Support exam and audit readiness for the CMS. 
Provide credible challenge across the business and escalate when it's warranted.
Use technology and automation to make governance programs scalable, measurable, and less manual.
Partner across Compliance (Advisory, Oversight & Monitoring, Financial Crimes) and with Risk, Legal, and Internal Audit.

8+ years of experience in compliance or risk management at a fintech, bank, or other regulated financial institution, including 3+ years leading teams
Hands-on experience owning core CMS components, such as compliance risk assessment, policy governance, training, compliance reporting, or issues management
Experience leading or playing a central role in regulatory examinations, including managing requests, engaging with examiners, and responding to findings
Broad knowledge of banking regulations, including consumer protection and BSA/AML, sufficient to provide credible challenge with subject matter experts
Demonstrated ability to present compliance programs to, and persuade, executive leadership, Board committees, banking partners, and regulators

ai_core_responsibilities: The Accounting Manager will execute monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes while managing clinical and non-clinical accruals. description_text:
Who We Are

Programmable Medicine is a pre-revenue, clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on discovering and developing innovative therapies for patients with serious diseases. The company operates across multiple legal entities and partners with external CROs, CMOs, and research institutions globally. Backed by leading venture capital investors, Programmable Medicine is building a scalable technical operations function to support rapid growth and pipeline advancement.

The Position

The Accounting Manager will be a hands-on, individual-contributor role supporting the accounting operations of a multi-entity biotech development organization. This role executes and owns key aspects of the close process, maintains accurate financial records, and applies strong technical accounting judgment to complex areas including clinical and nonclinical accruals, revenue recognition, and cost accounting. This is an experienced-level position: the ideal candidate operates independently, brings a strong technical accounting foundation, and can serve as a working-level resource to the Controller on technical matters.

This role partners closely with FP&A, providing significant support around clinical and non-clinical accrual estimates, actuals, and variance analysis.

Candidates must be able to work full days, on site, at our corporate headquarters in Redwood City, a minimum of 3 days per week and as required based on business needs.

 

Key Responsibilities

Execute assigned key components of the monthly, quarterly, and annual close process

Prepare journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules across multiple legal entities

Own the preparation and review of clinical and nonclinical accrual estimates in close partnership with FP&A and clinical/program stakeholders, ensuring accuracy and timely reporting of actuals and variances

Process and record intercompany transactions across the multi-entity structure, including recording pass-through costs, reclass entries between entities, and intercompany billings with cost-plus markups; reconcile intercompany balances

Apply technical accounting judgment to support revenue recognition under ASC 606, including contract- and milestone-based arrangements common in CRO/CDMO environments

Support cost accounting activities, including inventory, standard costing, and manufacturing variance analysis

Research and document technical accounting positions and memos, escalating and partnering with the Controller on judgmental or complex matters

Ensure adherence to U.S. GAAP and company accounting policies

Maintain and strengthen internal controls, including documentation and audit support

Prepare schedules and documentation for external audits and tax compliance

Provide accurate, well-supported financial data and accounting analysis to FP&A, including actuals and variance support

Identify and help drive process improvements and automation within accounting

Support ERP system integrity and reporting enhancements

 

Your Background

Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance; CPA or CPA-track preferred

5+ years of progressive accounting experience, preferably including CRO, CDMO, or biotech/pharma

Demonstrated technical accounting expertise, with the judgment to research and document positions independently

Experience with clinical trial or R&D-related accrual accounting strongly preferred

Experience with intercompany transaction accounting in a multi-entity environment, consolidation experience a plus but not required

Strong working knowledge of revenue recognition (ASC 606), including contract- and milestone-based arrangements

Exposure to cost or inventory accounting preferred

Experience with ERP systems (e.g., Sage Intacct, NetSuite, SAP, Oracle)

Advanced Excel skills

High degree of ownership, attention to detail, and accuracy in a hands-on capacity

Comfortable operating independently in a lean, fast-paced environment with no direct reports

Clear and effective communication with cross-functional stakeholders, including FP&A, clinical operations, and executive leadership 

What we can offer you

We have a comprehensive total compensation package including fully paid medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family.  The Company also offers participation in the annual bonus program along with a new hire equity program.  The salary range for candidates located in the Bay Area is $135,000 - $158,000 annually. We consider various factors when determining the base compensation, including market survey data, experience, and directly related qualifications, which means that the actual compensation may vary depending on the candidate’s knowledge and experience.  Candidate’s with less experience than what is required may be considered for the position at a lower job title and compensation.

 * The employee will adhere to all banking rules and regulations, including but
   not limited to the requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act. In addition, the
   employee will be proactive in the prevention of illegal activities, will
   vigilantly look for activities that may constitute any type of fraud
   including money laundering, and will report any suspicious activity to the
   BSA Officer.

Detection & Investigation

 * Lead investigations into complex fraud cases, including identity theft,
   account takeover (ATO), business email compromise (BEC), vendor email
   compromise (VEC), loan fraud, elder financial abuse, and internal/employee
   fraud.
 * Act swiftly to restrict compromised accounts, place holds, initiate wire/ACH
   recalls, and coordinate with peer financial institutions to recover stolen
   funds.
 * Maintain meticulous investigative files, documenting evidence, video
   retention, loss calculations, and root-cause analyses.
 * Oversee fraud detection, monitoring, and investigation activities.
 * Analyze deposit account, loan, ACH, wire transfer, check, remote deposit
   capture, and online banking activity for potential fraud.
 * Identify fraud patterns and recommend improvements to monitoring procedures.
 * Assist with recovery efforts and restitution opportunities when fraud losses
   occur.

Compliance & Reporting

 * Draft and file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) related to fraud within
   mandatory regulatory timeframes, ensuring strict adherence to FinCEN
   guidelines.
 * Prepare regular fraud trend reports, loss metrics, and mitigation strategies
   to the Enterprise Risk Management Committee, Audit & Risk Committee, Board of
   Directors, and various areas of management as needed.
 * Support internal audits, external audits, and regulatory examinations.
 * Provide documentation and reporting requested by examiners and auditors.

Collaboration & Training

 * Serve as a point of contact for local, state, and federal law enforcement
   agencies and preparing documentation when subpoenaed.
 * Design and deliver ongoing fraud awareness training for frontline staff, loan
   officers, and back-office teams to improve early detection.
 * Partner with Marketing and Digital Banking to develop educational materials
   helping retail and commercial/ag customers protect themselves against fraud.
 * Work closely with Operations, Information Security, Retail Banking, Lending,
   Compliance, and BSA personnel.
 * Coordinate Fraud training to all staff members across the organization and
   Fraud Department training to expand knowledge based on recent fraud emerging
   risks and trends impacting Bravera.
   
   

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES & COMMITTEES:

 * Participate in Fraud Focus Group
 * Participate in Action Teams and Committees as assigned.
   
   

 SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:

 * Fraud Specialist Lead
 * Fraud Specialist staff
   
   

 QUALIFICATIONS (KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES):

Education & Experience

 * Education: Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, Finance, Business
   Administration, or a related field (equivalent experience may be considered).
 * Experience: Minimum of 5–7 years of banking experience, with at least 3–5
   years directly in financial fraud investigation or fraud risk management at a
   community or regional bank.
   
   

CERTIFICATIONS (Highly Preferred)

 * CFE (Certified Fraud Examiner)
 * CAFP (Certified AML and Fraud Professional)
 * CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist)
   
   

LOCATION: Any Bravera location. Bismarck, ND or Fargo, ND preferred.

Benefits

which includes a competitive salary, incentive compensation opportunities,

organization, we are committed to investing in the growth and development of our

salary information is included, it is industry information and not specific to

Our Values

 * Give and earn trust. We support and empower one another to earn trust through
   accountable performance.
 * Learn, teach and mentor. We are a learning organization that invests in
   growth and development.
 * Collaborate and innovate. We work together to drive continuous improvement to

org_linkedin_description:
We are Bravera, an employee- and director-owned company of advisors who help build the financial strength, stability and growth of every community to which we belong. We’re driven to serve you, coming together to forge new paths to help you achieve your business and personal goals.
 
From small towns to larger cities, from the wide-open plains to the rugged beauty of the mountains, from family farms to energy fields, to the people building businesses and lives in our communities, Bravera is powered by the energy of all those we serve with a footprint that reaches far and wide, with a focus always on our people. 

With roots dating back to 1909, we are comprised of Bravera Bank, Bravera Insurance and Bravera Wealth; all falling under the holding company, Bravera Holdings Corp. This allows us the unique opportunity to offer customers a complete financial services package.

Located in North Dakota and Montana, the three Bravera entities have 32 locations in 27 communities including Bismarck, Burlington, Cando, Carrington, Cooperstown, Fargo, Finley, Devils Lake, Drake, Dickinson, Killdeer, Leeds, Mandan, McClusky, Minot, New England, Northwood, Stanley, Underwood and Watford City in North Dakota and Billings, Glendive, Great Falls and Helena in Montana and Albertville and Kerkhoven in Minnesota

Bravera Bank is Member FDIC / Equal Housing Lender.

Products and services offered through Bravera Insurance and Bravera Wealth are not a deposit, not FDIC insured, not insured by any federal government agency, not financial institution guaranteed and may lose value. Products and services offered by Bravera Wealth may be subject to investment risk, including loss of principal amount invested.
